verdicts.reason: Confirmed in phases2_to_8.py and full_12layer_pipeline.py: only tests with overlap>=2 and raw p<0.1 are kept, then BH runs on that subset. The spec (01-sae-atlas.md:182) calls for BH across all terms for each feature. Accepted rows have raw p up to 0.042. I recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv, treating untested and retained-but-nonsignificant rows as p=1 (the BH-nonsignificant rows retained at p<0.1 are not saved). Per-feature BH over all 2,369 terms leaves 104/2498 (4.2%) L0, 84/4928 (1.7%) L5 and 55/4924 (1.1%) L11 features annotated. Global BH leaves 29, 5 and 0. The median overlap is 2. The reported 80.7/67.8/61.7% rates, the U-shape, the 'more interpretable than Geneformer' claim and annotation-based feature selection all rest on this.

Confirmed. phase0_extract.py adds the full k×k slice of the causal attention matrix, so upper-triangular zeros are included, and divides by pair_counts over every cell that has both genes. phase1 reads only attn_primary[pert_hvg,:], the query=source row. The edge is therefore partly a measure of relative expression rank, and no reverse or symmetrised edge is tested. README deviation 1 does disclose the directed form, the full attention tensors are not in the snapshot, and the size of the effect on the FAIL verdicts (gene variance beats attention by 6-20 AUROC points) cannot be checked. Real, but likely limited in effect.

Confirmed. The layer-0 Pearson is 0.99999999998 or higher for all three pairs, it is included in the 12-layer mean, and best_layer=0 everywhere. Invariance then falls with depth (lung-extlung 0.795 at L1 to 0.608 at L10; immune-extlung 0.45 at L10), which contradicts the text's 'transformer doesn't introduce tissue-specific divergence'. Dropping L0 only lowers the means by about 0.01-0.025 (to about 0.85/0.75/0.72), so the descriptive numbers mostly stand, and the text concedes the static layer is invariant. The 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel)' framing is overclaimed because no static-embedding comparator was used.

Confirmed from the CSVs. The ext-lung B-cell result (3 markers, obs 0.0556 = null_p95 0.0556, i.e. a single kNN hit) is reported as significant with z=3.05, so '4/4 lineages sig' should be 3/4. The nulls are random gene sets of the same size and a plain TF-degree permutation, with no matching on expression. H-hub z=2.34/2.36 (lung z=1.31, n.s.) comes from 100 permutations with no correction across domains, yet it is called 'the strongest new result'. These are secondary exploratory claims, and the table does label H-hub 'weak-positive'.

The facts check out: the centroid classifier is fit and scored in-sample, the permutation null mean is 0.539-0.546, and L3-L5 fall below the null mean. However, the spec itself prescribes the centroid classifier, and the permutation null refits in-sample, so the perm_p values and the '5/12 layers significant' count are valid (5 even survive BH). Subtracting the higher floor would only make MaxToki look weaker than the paper (whose null is about 0.50), and the summary already calls it 'weaker'. Small wording errors remain (mean is 0.567 not 0.572; 'L0 ~0.53' should be 0.596), but no conclusion changes.

Confirmed. lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv has B cell n=6 (TwoNN 101 at L0 to 6.2 at L11), T cell n=9 and Myeloid n=1 (NaN). With F<0.9 the fit uses only about 5 points, and the estimates follow the global 102→6.7 decline. There is no size-matched random-set null. The spec itself uses about 7-12 markers, so the run follows protocol, but the 'B-cell replicated / T-cell divergent' verdicts and the 'geometry encodes time rather than lineage identity' interpretation cannot be told apart from estimator noise or the global trend. These are secondary claims.

Confirmed. phase9b uses a gene-label-shuffle null (null sd 0.001) on the off-diagonal Pearson of cosine matrices. The spec's paper result is a raw-cosine test with p>0.3 under a 'shared-vocabulary null'. These are different statistics and different nulls, so calling them 'two clean non-replications' compares unlike tests. A label shuffle also breaks any vocabulary-order or token-frequency structure, so it cannot support 'not an artefact of vocabulary order'. The B-cell prec@10 gene-set caveat is partly disclosed. This affects 1-2 of the 29 scored sub-analyses.

Confirmed. The log says 'leidenalg not installed'. The fallback is SpectralClustering(n_clusters=min(10,n_alive)), so 10 modules covering every alive feature is guaranteed, and all 12 layers in the 12-layer run report exactly 10. In phases2_to_8.py the fallback also clusters pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive] and writes the labels to alive_idx, so L0 (2,430 dead features) gets misassigned labels. The 12-layer script fixes the indexing with np.ix_. The claimed exact match to the paper ('10 modules at 99.9-100% coverage matches precisely') is produced by the parameter setting, not the data.

Confirmed by simulation: 4,928 random unit vectors in 1232-D against 50 orthonormal directions give a mean max |cos| of 0.072 and a maximum of 0.127, with 0 above 0.7. Any dictionary would therefore come out about 100% 'novel', and 'massive superposition confirmed' has no control behind it. The metric comes from the spec and the paper (cos>0.7), so the replicated number is faithful. The error is in what is inferred from it. The code also counts dead L0 features.

Scope as stated is correct: 500 K562 cells, one SAE seed, 3 layers; circuit tracing uses 200 K562 cells, K562/K562 only, with phases 8 and 13 skipped. The interpretation still generalises to 'single-cell foundation models, regardless of architecture ... have not internalised causal regulatory wiring' and 'the limitation is in MaxToki's representations, not the SAE training data'. This overreaches a single-condition, single-seed harness. The scope is disclosed elsewhere, so this is an interpretive overreach rather than a numerical error.

Confirmed. The 3-layer summary says 'Features are overwhelmingly layer-specific — no persistent scaffold. Replicates' and 'Annotation declining with depth'. The 12-layer summary (same SAEs; L0→L5 = 125 in both logs) reports L6→L7 21.5% and L0→L8 13.3%, calls this 'differs from paper', and describes a U-shaped annotation profile. The 3-layer verdict was never updated. Neither summary has a seed-to-seed baseline (the spec does not ask for one either). The underlying data are consistent, so this is a reporting contradiction.

Confirmed from experiments_2_3.py. Pseudotime is PC1 of log1p over 200 randomly sampled TS immune cells of mixed types, so it likely tracks cell type. The switch criterion is |ρ|>0.3, p<0.01, applied to K562-trained SAEs, and cos(g_early,g_late)≈0.999. The headline 'temporal information permeates every layer' and the 5,767-vs-14 comparison are therefore unsupported. One part of the finding is overstated: with n=200, |ρ|>0.3 already means p≈1.6e-5, so multiple testing is not a real issue (about 0.4 expected false positives across about 24.6k tests). The deviations are disclosed in the summary.

Numbers confirmed. Mean branch balanced accuracy is pca10 0.844, svd10 0.837, avgpool 0.792, drift 0.829, z10 0.756, raw 0.142, and z10−pca10 Δ=−0.088 (q=0.26). The headline ('internally encodes', 'first affirmative deployable result') and the multi-axis-hub claims about H38/H95/H103 are never qualified by an expression baseline. §11 of the same summary does disclose that there is no advantage over PCA/SVD/avg-pool. The descriptive claim stands, but the headline framing is overstated.

Confirmed. phase9 uses features = centroids[:, li+1, :] @ A.T, with A = o_proj.weight[:, h*154:(h+1)*154].T. That is a projection of the post-layer residual onto the head's o_proj write directions, not anything the head computes. For L10, centroid index 11 is the HF final post-RMSNorm hidden state. Every input needs a full forward pass, which contradicts the spec's 'no forward pass' direct operator. No random-projection or random-layer control was run. The 'top-1 L10H6 / late-layer concentration' and '2,400× compression to 7.7 KB operator' mechanistic claims in the headline are therefore unsupported as head-level statements.

Confirmed from phase17_cross_axis_h65_h95.json: ruler overlap 0.814, self-fits 0.986 and 0.825, cross-head 0.642. Under independent fit error, attenuation alone predicts 0.986×0.814×0.825 = 0.662, close to the observed 0.642. The scrambled-ruler null (0.022) does not address this. So 'actively rotates away' and the PARTIALLY_ORTHOGONAL verdict are not established. This undercuts the only quantitative support for the multi-axis-hub claim, but not the main H65 result.

review.summary:
Audit of the MaxToki-217M mechanistic-interpretability project (8 runs) against CHECKLIST_DEPLOYED.md §6 (P1–P10) and the §6.11 workflow: inventory, then per-pattern sweep, cross-pipeline triangulation, severity grading and action proposal. For each load-bearing finding I traced the claim to the numeric outputs and then to the script, and recomputed key statistics where the files allowed.

Executive summary: 43 problems found. 6 critical, 26 major, 11 minor. About 8 are partly acknowledged in run documents (attention-GRN Adamson C3 caveat, spectral annotation-biased HVG, manifold Phase-12 caveat, longevity small-cohort note, the H123 'already at floor' remark, the SAE proxy caveat), but none of those acknowledgements fixes the underlying problem. Everything else is unaddressed.

The most serious findings are implementation bugs that fall outside the P1–P10 catalogue (§10 pitfall 4):
1. **CRISPRi metric ignores the circuit.** The circuit-tracing "CRISPRi directional accuracy 54.6%", cited project-wide as near-chance evidence, never uses the circuit's prediction. It is the fraction of target genes whose expression falls on knockdown.
2. **Off-by-one patch hook.** Every SAE ablation and steering hook (Stage 2, Stage 3 Exp 1/2/3) overwrites block l's output with block l's input, so each "single-feature" intervention also deletes a whole transformer block. The run's own outputs show the signature: identical out-degrees across hubs, identical redundancy ratios across distinct triplets, and steering effects identical across features and across α=2 vs α=5. So the "first affirmative positive" (trajectory steering) and the Stage-2/3 circuit statistics cannot stand.
3. **SAE annotation multiple-testing error.** Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) correction was applied only to tests already prefiltered at p<0.1. Recomputed with a correct per-feature BH, annotation rates fall from 81/68/62% to 4.2/1.7/1.1% (full-family BH: 1.2/0.1/0%). This invalidates the annotation claims and everything selected or scored by annotation.
4. **SAE layer mismatch.** SAE Phases 6/8t/9/11 encode hidden_states[l+1] with the SAE trained on hidden_states[l]. Phase 6 also splices in the full reconstruction, so the "1.01× causal specificity, genuine non-replication" is an artefact of the method.
5. **Topology H123 test design.** The headline negative (H123 non-replication) uses a feature built from the evaluated TRRUST labels, uses no held-out splits and has no positive control. The pipeline spec itself (line 549) treats this outcome as a sign of an implementation error.

Major issues include:
- **Cross-model alignment nulls.** CCA and Procrustes nulls are invalid. In-sample CCA chance is ≈0.41–0.43; the scGPT "r=0.40, top-1 5–8%, z=20–30" is exactly chance.
- **Cross-tissue invariance.** It is inflated by layer 0 (context-free embeddings, Pearson=1.0) and tested against a trivial null.
- **Immune domain pool.** It is 98% TRRUST TFs, so it is not comparable with the other two domains.
- **Unsupported positives.** H-hub, H23 and iter_04 positives have no valid null or confidence interval (my reproduced H23 CIs all include 0.5).
- **Spectral-geometry comparisons.** "Learned compression" is supported only by a single feature-shuffle; the CKA and Phase-9b comparisons measure quantities that are not like-for-like with the source paper.
- **Manifold-discovery.** No advantage over PCA-10 on expression, yet headlined as "MaxToki encodes". The frozen 5-gate rule was not followed (no blocked-permutation gate, a post-hoc 3-gate fallback, k changed from 15 to 5). The negative control uses random labels. Head selection and evaluation use the same panel.
- **Attention-GRN.** A false claim that no run beats any trivial baseline (RPE1 does), and C3/C4 are undefined when the baseline AUROC is below 0.5.
- **SAE TF specificity.** "0/48" rests on 3 detected TFs.
- **Cross-cutting.** Positive controls are missing and headline numbers rest on single seeds with no confidence intervals.

Residual exposure by pattern: P1 (weak or unanchored nulls: CCA, gene-shuffle nulls, hard-coded null), P2 (manifold vs PCA, static-only alignment), P3/P9 (causal and steering language, 'encodes', mis-described architectures), P4 (position-level and pair-level pseudoreplication, n=17 donors), P5 (annotation selection, post-hoc reclassification, head double-dipping), P6 (no planted-signal positive control anywhere), P7 (immune pool, single dataset per pipeline), P8 (single seed, no CIs), and P10 (no environment file, hard-coded external paths, silent method fallbacks, diverging summary copies).

Open items: the model weights and large arrays were not available, so the hook bugs are confirmed by code reading and output signatures rather than by re-execution. The scGPT vocabulary alignment could not be verified.

findings.category: code-bug / metric does not measure claim
findings.description: The Phase-11 'CRISPRi directional accuracy' never uses the circuit's predicted direction. predicted_inhibitory = info['max_d'] > 0 is always True (max_d stores an absolute value) and is never used. A pair is scored 'correct' whenever the target's knockdown log fold change (LFC) is below 0. So 54.6% is just the base rate of negative LFCs among the 1.46M (source, target) gene pairs, a property of the Replogle data, not of the circuit. Pairs that share a source gene are not independent, and LFC=0 is scored as wrong. Despite this, 54.6% is cited across the project as 'near-chance, confirming circuits encode co-expression, not causal regulation'.
findings.evidence: Code lines 322-328 (quoted above). outputs/phase11_crispri_validation.json: n_validated=1,458,016, n_correct=796,159, accuracy 0.5461. The value 0.546 equals the share of validated pairs with negative LFC by construction. The paper comparison (56.4%) and the 'near chance' interpretation therefore have no bearing on the circuit.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Map each edge's sign (mean_delta direction) to a predicted LFC sign. Score agreement against (a) the trivial 'always predict decrease' baseline (= the LFC<0 base rate), and (b) a null that shuffles edges across source genes, with resampling grouped by source gene. Until then, remove the 54.6% claim from every FINAL_SUMMARY and cross-reference. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: The ablation patch is applied one block too late. clean_hidden[l] = hidden_states[l], the input to transformer block l: the adapter defines hidden_states[0] as the post-embedding stream and hidden_states[l] as the output of block l-1, and the SAE for 'layer l' was trained on hidden_states[l]. The forward hook is registered on model.layers[l], whose output is hidden_states[l+1], and replaces that output with hidden_states[l] + delta. Every 'single-feature ablation' therefore also deletes the whole of block l. The resulting downstream effects are dominated by the missing block and are nearly the same for every feature. The run's own outputs show this signature, but it was interpreted as biology ('uniformly dense', 'feature-invariant ablation magnitudes ... not a code bug').
findings.evidence: Stage 2 top-5 L0 hub out-degrees are 39,676 / 39,674 / 39,672 / 39,672 / 39,670 (73% saturation of 54,208 possible targets). Exp 1: 1000/1000 features have >1000 edges. Exp 2 v2: four triplets with entirely distinct L0/L5/L9 features give AB 0.1652/0.1652/0.1653/0.1656, BC 0.5861/0.5861/0.5861/0.5858, three-way 0.1896-0.1897 (std <0.0003). The project knew the correct convention: sae-atlas phase6_patching.py:127 uses hidden_states[PROBE_LAYER+1] with the same hook. Affected claims: 2,144,011 edges, 88.2% inhibitory, mean |d| 1.84, depth attenuation, 4,970,096 edges, the redundancy ratios 0.165/0.324/0.190, and 'zero synergy'.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Hook model.layers[l-1] (or the embedding output for l=0), or use a forward_pre_hook on layers[l]. Add a mandatory zero-delta check (a patched forward with delta=0 must reproduce the clean hidden states and logits exactly) and a random-direction control. Re-run Stage 2 and Exp 1/2. Effort: at least half a day of compute.

findings.location: runs/exhaustive-mapping-217M/scripts/experiment3_rerun.py:147-156 (hook_layer_for), 250-280; outputs/experiment3/steering_F*.json; summaries/exhaustive-mapping-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md (Exp 3, 'Steering harness — final-residual hook fix'); cited in summaries/attention-grn-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:140-150, summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:190, runs/topology-141-217M/FINAL_SUMMARY.md:25-27, EXTENDED_FINDINGS.md:86-103
findings.description: The 'first affirmative positive' (activation-addition steering pushes cells toward maturity, with a non-monotonic layer profile) is an artefact. For li<11 the same off-by-one as F02 applies: block li is deleted on every steered pass. For li=11, hidden_states[11] in HF Llama is taken after the final RMSNorm. Injecting it as the output of layers[10] means the final norm is applied twice (norm(norm(x)+delta)), which changes the logits even when delta=0. The summary wrongly calls hidden_states[11] the residual 'before RMSNorm'. The Δs baseline subtracts only the clean-cell score; there is no α=1 or random-feature control.
findings.evidence:
From the per-feature JSONs:
- L0: F40 / F1657 / F4797 have opposite pseudotime directions, yet Δs = 0.0961 / 0.0963 / 0.0964 (α=2) and frac_mat = 0.98 for all three.
- L3: Δs 0.0177-0.0179 for all features.
- L6: Δs −0.0078 for all, frac_dir 0.26 for all.
- L9: Δs 0.0139-0.0142, frac_dir 0.64 for all.
- L11: mean logit delta −1.06 to −1.09 for both the 'positive' and 'negative' features.
- α=2 and α=5 agree to within 1% (the run calls this 'saturation').
The effect is independent of which feature is steered and by how much. Downstream claims that rely on it: 'MaxToki encodes a progenitor→mature axis', 'mid-layer counter-differentiation basin', 'L0 strongest'.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Fix the hook indexing and the L11 handling (hook the final-norm input). Add α=1 (zero-delta), random-feature and random-direction controls per layer, and report Δs relative to them. Retract the steering claim from attention-GRN, SAE and topology cross-references until re-run. Effort: 1-2 hr compute after the fix.

findings.description: Annotation enrichments are recorded only when the raw hypergeometric p < 0.1, and BH is then applied to this pre-filtered subset rather than to all feature × term tests. That inflates discoveries massively: almost every nominal p < 0.04 becomes 'significant'. The reported annotation rates, the 'more interpretable than Geneformer' claim, the U-shaped depth profile and the annotated/unannotated split used downstream are all invalid.
findings.evidence:
Tests per layer: L0 2498×2369 = 5.92M; L5 4928×2369 = 11.67M; L11 4924×2369 = 11.66M. Recomputed from the saved p_raw values (the largest saved p is 0.04):
- Full-family BH: 29/2498 (1.2%), 5/4928 (0.1%), 0/4924 (0%) features annotated.
- Per-feature BH (m=2369): 104 (4.2%), 84 (1.7%), 55 (1.1%).
- Claimed: 80.7% / 67.8% / 61.7%.
- 79-85% of 'significant' enrichments rest on an overlap of 2 genes within a top-20 list.
Downstream uses of these annotations: Stage-2 source-feature selection (sum of −log10 p), coherence 36.1%, Stage-3 '500 annotated + 500 unannotated' and the hub-annotation 'bias', Phase-10 unannotated %, Phase-6 'richly annotated' features, and gene-level predictions.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Apply BH over the full family (or per feature, stated explicitly). Add a random-gene-set or shuffled-activation baseline for the annotation rate. Re-derive every annotation-dependent result in sae-atlas, circuit-tracing and exhaustive-mapping. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.location: runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/phase6_patching.py:127-141; remaining_phases.py:175, 418, 606; phase9_multitissue.py:78, 239; vs phase0_extract_positions.py:42,107 (SAE 'L5' trained on hidden[5])
findings.category: code-bug / layer mismatch and patch construction
findings.description: The SAE labelled L5 was trained on hidden_states[5], the output of block 4. Phases 6, 8t and 11 encode hidden_states[6], the output of block 5, with that SAE. Phase 6 then replaces the block-5 output with decode(z_ablated), the full SAE reconstruction, instead of h + (decode(z_abl) − decode(z)). The reconstruction error, which is even larger on the mismatched layer, is therefore injected identically for every feature, so the target and off-target changes are equal by construction. Phase 9 compares a multi-tissue SAE trained on hidden[6] with the K562 SAE trained on hidden[5] (78.2% vs 88.9% variance explained), which are different layers. The claim 'Phase 6 is a genuine non-replication: MaxToki features are not causally specific (1.01× vs 2.36×)' cannot stand.
findings.evidence: phase6/summary.json: mean_target_delta 1.414 vs mean_other_delta 1.395, median specificity 1.0149, 0% above 2×. The code comment at L126 reads 'Hidden state AFTER layer PROBE_LAYER (= index PROBE_LAYER+1)', while the SAE was trained on index PROBE_LAYER (phase0_extract_positions.py: hidden[li] with li in {0,5,11}).
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Use the matching hidden-state index and an error-preserving delta patch. Add sanity controls (no-ablation patch gives about 0 change; a random decoder direction). Re-run Phases 6, 8t, 9 and 11, and withdraw the 'genuine non-replication' statement until then. Effort: about half a day.

findings.description:
The headline 'H123, the paper's strongest finding, does not replicate (0–1/12 layers)' cannot be interpreted, for three reasons:
1. The H116/H123 motif feature is computed from the TRRUST signs of the in-pool TRRUST edges, the same edges that define is_trrust. The feature is therefore nonzero only on positive pairs, and AUROC measures the share of TRRUST pairs whose sign agrees with Louvain co-membership, not edge recovery.
2. No held-out TF/target split is used; the Phase-1 splits are never read by phase78.
3. There is no planted-signal positive control.
The pipeline's own validation section says that H123 yielding fewer than 18/22 positive rows indicates the sign shuffle or degree strata are implemented incorrectly. The run reports exactly that outcome as a biological non-replication.
findings.evidence: Lung rows: auc_motif 0.403-0.427, and even the sign-shuffle null mean is 0.415-0.437 (below 0.5). In code, feat[tf,tgt] += consistency only for TRRUST rows, and y = is_trrust. The run evaluates 12 layers × 3 domains instead of the source's 22 domain-split rows. A search for 'positive control|synthetic|planted' across runs/ found no control for this pipeline.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) (a) Positive control: a synthetic graph with planted signed motif-community structure, and/or the implementation run on the source paper's scGPT/Geneformer embeddings to reproduce 22/22. (b) Evaluate on held-out TF/target splits, with the feature built from training edges only. (c) Only then restate the non-replication; until then, qualify it as 'not evaluable'. Effort: at least half a day.

findings.category: null model too weak / not anchored to chance (P1)
findings.description:
Both cross-model statistics lack valid chance anchors.
- CCA is fit and evaluated in-sample (about 380 genes, 30 PCA dimensions, top-10 components) with no permutation null on the CCA statistic.
- The top-1 retrieval 'null' reuses the Procrustes rotation fitted on the true pairing and only shuffles columns, so its chance level is about 1/n rather than the in-sample overfitting level.
Consequences: the scGPT result (r≈0.40, top-1 5–8%, z=20–30) is exactly chance, not 'much weaker alignment', and the Geneformer r=0.78 is compared with the 'paper target 0.80 ± 0.05' without any null. The scGPT vocabulary-to-embedding row mapping comes from an external cached .pt file and was not sanity-checked, so a mapping error cannot be excluded (pairwise Pearson −0.019, z=−3.0 in immune).
findings.evidence:
My simulation with independent Gaussian data, n=380/350, d=30:
- Mean of the top-10 canonical r = 0.413 / 0.429 (p95 0.427 / 0.443). scGPT reported 0.401 / 0.438 / 0.406.
- In-sample Procrustes top-1 on independent PCA-30 data: mean 6.2-7.3%, p95 8.0-9.1%. scGPT reported 5.0 / 6.6 / 7.6% with 'null p95' 0.5-0.9%.
- Geneformer: CCA 0.77-0.78 and top-1 38-47% are above these chance levels.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Use a permutation null that refits CCA and Procrustes on gene-shuffled pairs, or held-out-gene cross-validation, and report Δ vs null. Run a within-scGPT sanity check (e.g., STRING co-pole or marker clustering) to rule out a vocabulary misalignment. Restate scGPT as 'no alignment detectable above chance'. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.category: trivial baseline / endpoint mismatch / wrong description (P2/P3/P9)
findings.description: Cross-model alignment was measured only between static token-embedding matrices; the per-layer alignment promised in the script docstring was never computed. Yet the result is presented as Layer-1 (learned-representation) replication and as models that 'converge after independent pre-training on different objectives'. MaxToki and Geneformer share the same Ensembl rank-value tokenizer and gene-median scheme from the same lab, so static alignment may reflect shared corpus and tokenization. Geneformer is repeatedly described as part of 'the autoregressive-Ensembl family'; it is a BERT masked-LM encoder, and the spectral-geometry summary itself says so. scGPT is called an 'attention-only architecture' although all three models are transformers. 'This weakens the source paper's Layer-1 claim' rests on static-only, chance-level scGPT numbers (F07).
findings.evidence: cross_model_alignment.csv contains only tap=static rows. EXTENDED_FINDINGS L24 says 'holds within the autoregressive-Ensembl-tokenizer family (MaxToki ↔ Geneformer V2-316M)'. spectral-geometry FINAL_SUMMARY Phase 9b describes Geneformer as a 'BERT-style encoder'.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify + re-run) Compute per-layer alignment and report the static alignment as a floor (checklist P2). Correct the architecture descriptions. Rephrase as 'static input embeddings of two models sharing a tokenizer are correlated (r=0.39 pairwise)'. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.description:
'STRONG POSITIVE (novel): MaxToki encodes a tissue-invariant gene geometry' is not supported.
- The means include layer 0, the context-free token embedding, which is identical across tissues by construction (Pearson=1.000, top-1=1.000, best_layer=0 for all pairs).
- The null shuffles gene labels, which any residual-stream model beats trivially because each gene's state contains its token embedding.
- There is no within-tissue split-half reference to show that cross-tissue similarity reaches the ceiling set by sampling noise.
- Late-layer top-1 retrieval drops to 0.25–0.30 at L11, which suggests tissue-specific divergence grows with depth, contrary to the narrative.
- The analysis rests on only 75, 168 and 77 shared genes.
The document itself says 'of course the static layer is tissue-invariant'.
findings.evidence: cross_domain_alignment.csv: layer 0 Pearson 1.0 in all three pairs. Means excluding L0: 0.849 / 0.746 / 0.717. Top-1 at L11: 0.667 / 0.250 / 0.299. Pearson z vs gene-shuffle: 6.6-100.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Exclude L0. Per layer, compare cross-tissue similarity with within-tissue split-half similarity, using disjoint cell samples as in spectral Phase 8, and report the difference with a CI. Downgrade the label to 'exploratory'. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: The 'immune' domain was not extracted with the lung pool-selection rule. It reuses 350 genes from the spectral-geometry pool, which was annotation-biased toward TRRUST TFs, and 343/350 (98%) are TRRUST TFs. Lung has 87/382 TFs and external-lung 86/380. The three 'domains' therefore differ in gene composition, not just tissue. Immune-specific results are confounded by this: H123 1/12, H141 2/12 strict-positive, the comparison with the paper's immune +0.012, H-hub z=2.34 computed among 343 TFs, and the missing lineage markers. Cross-domain comparisons rest on 75–77 shared genes (36 shared by all three).
findings.evidence: run_config: reused=true, source=spectral-geometry-217M/outputs/phase0. gene_features: immune is_trrust_tf=343 of 350; phase16 h_hub n_tfs_in_pool: 87 / 343 / 86. MANUAL_REVIEW reports 36 common genes.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Re-extract immune with the same gene-pool rule as lung and external-lung, or report immune as a separate TF-only analysis and remove it from cross-domain tallies. Effort: about half a day.

findings.description: In the pair table, positives are TRRUST pairs, which always contain a TF. Negatives are random non-TRRUST pairs, mostly without a TF, plus every STRING-only pair labelled as a negative. Any geometric feature that tracks TF identity, degree or PPI proximity shifts the AUROC regardless of regulatory structure. STRING-labelled negatives are likely to be geometrically close, which pushes similarity-based features below 0.5. No TF-matched or degree-matched negative set exists, so the 'anti-predictive' readings (e.g., triangle defect −0.055, H16 mean AUC 0.477-0.498) are hard to interpret.
findings.evidence: Code: rows for 'string_pos − pos_set' get is_trrust=0. phase1_summary: STRING positives 48/24/61 alongside TRRUST positives 252/504/138, with negatives sampled at 4× from all pairs. Many reported AUROCs fall below chance.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Sample negatives matched on TF membership and degree (TF-involving pairs not in TRRUST). Analyse STRING-only pairs separately. Re-run Phases 6-12. Effort: about half a day.

findings.description: iter_04 'H-cross NOVEL POSITIVE' has no computed null: the 'null p95' is the constant 0.3. The automated decision (INCONCLUSIVE) was overridden post hoc in MANUAL_REVIEW. The feature is the label-dependent H123 score of F06, whose per-layer AUROC is 0.38–0.53. The interpretation 'community structure is fixed at the embedding layer; the residual stream does not reorganise gene similarities' contradicts spectral-geometry (effective rank 561→94 across depth) and Phase 15 (top-1 retrieval falls from 1.00 to 0.25-0.30 with depth). iter_05 likewise claims to 'rule out the popularity confound' from strata of a signal that is absent (6/36 positive).
findings.evidence: report.json: mean Δ_vs_null 0.30-0.38, computed as Pearson − 0.3. Cross-layer Pearson 0.60-0.68. MANUAL_REVIEW reclassifies to NOVEL POSITIVE.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Compute a real null (e.g., layer-shuffled or random-init embeddings), keep the pre-registered decision rule, label the result exploratory, and remove the 'residual stream does not reorganise' claim. Effort: about 1 hr.
(re-run/qualify) Use a null matched on expression and degree, sweep layers and k, and apply BH across tests. Downgrade to 'weak exploratory association'. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.description: 'DIRECTIONAL REPLICATES across all 3 domains ... Validates the spec implementation' rests on AUROCs computed over 52–123 kNN-graph edges with 11–22 positives, with no confidence interval. A pass is declared simply when AUROC < 0.45. When reproduced with a bootstrap, every CI includes 0.5, so the check neither replicates the paper nor validates the implementation.
findings.evidence:
My reproduction (L6, PCA-20, k=12):
- Lung: 62 edges, 13 positive, AUROC 0.352, 95% CI [0.189, 0.534].
- Immune: 123 edges, 22 positive, AUROC 0.416, CI [0.293, 0.545].
- External-lung: 52 edges, 11 positive, AUROC 0.340, CI [0.162, 0.544].
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Report CIs, describe the result as 'directionally consistent but not significant', and do not use it as implementation validation. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: 'The compression is an emergent property of training, not architectural' is supported only by a single permutation of each feature column at the final layer. That permutation destroys all covariance between features, so any anisotropic representation, including an untrained transformer with RMSNorm, would show a lower effective rank than the shuffle. There is no random-init or untrained-weights control and no per-layer null. The final 'layer' (hidden_states[11]) is also taken after the final RMSNorm, unlike layers 0-10.
findings.evidence: null_feature_shuffle.json: observed effective rank 93.6 vs shuffled 573.1 (6.1×), one shuffle at the final layer only.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Extract a randomly initialised MaxToki with the same tokenization and compute the per-layer effective-rank trajectory. Restrict the claim to 'non-isotropic' unless the trained and random-init trajectories differ. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: CKA is computed between per-gene mean embeddings from disjoint 2000-cell samples with a fixed HVG list. This is compared with scGPT's CKA across fine-tuning seeds (different model weights) and scored '❌ stability much higher'. The two quantities measure different things. L0 is the context-free token embedding, so its CKA = 1.000 by construction, and averaging over 2000 cells makes per-gene means nearly invariant. The interpretation that the model 'was trained on ~175M cells ... converged' is unsupported.
findings.evidence: cka_per_layer: L0 1.000 → L11 0.991. Paper: 0.979 → 0.779 across fine-tuning seeds.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Relabel as 'cell-resampling stability', mark it not comparable with seed stability, and remove the training-regime interpretation. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: 'The paper's null does NOT replicate — alignment IS significant' is reached with a gene-label shuffle null, which any nonzero alignment beats. The paper's negative was against a shared-vocabulary null. Only static embeddings are compared. The second 'non-replication' (Geneformer static B-cell prec@10 = 0.273) uses an annotation-biased, marker-enriched HVG set, not the paper's gene set.
findings.evidence: cross_model_cosine.json: Pearson 0.382; null mean −0.000, sd 0.001; p = 0 with n_perm = 500.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Implement the paper's shared-vocabulary null, or state that the nulls differ and withdraw 'paper's null does not replicate'. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.description: Lineage-specific intrinsic dimension is estimated by TwoNN on 6 B-cell and 9 T-cell marker points in 1232 dimensions. With so few points the estimates (101 → 6) are noise-level, and they are not normalised against the global compression (effective rank 561→94) using random gene sets of the same size. 'B-cell compression replicated' and 'T-cell also compresses, likely due to trajectory training' are unsupported. Audit-table item #16 calls BATF/BACH2 distance-to-PAX5 with ρ = +0.979 / +0.888 (distances increasing, i.e. divergence) 'distance metrics replicate strongly'. Lines 97-103 of the same summary state the opposite.
findings.evidence: lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv: n_markers = 6 (B) and 9 (T). depth_correlations: dist_BATF_to_PAX5 ρ = 0.979.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Use a null of random gene sets of matched size, more markers or cell-level analysis, and correct item #16. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.description: The central negative '0% TF regulatory specificity, even more extreme than Geneformer' is uninformative. With true CRISPRi, only 4 of 100 perturbations (3 of 48 TFs) produced any responding feature, using 20 cells each, so '0/48' is effectively 0/3. The scorecard still counts the proxy '100% detection ✅', but the proxy uses natural gene-presence variation, not a perturbation. 'True CRISPRi confirms the proxy result' does not follow. The Phase-9 multi-tissue comparison (0/48 → 0/48) is equally powerless, and the layer mismatch of F05 also applies.
findings.evidence: perturbation_response.csv: detected = CDC5L, GATA1, MED1 (TFs) and AQR; n_cells = 20 for every target. Specificity requires at least 2 of a feature's top-20 genes to be known TRRUST targets of the perturbed TF.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Report specificity conditional on detection, with denominators. Increase the number of cells and do a power analysis. Remove the proxy from the scorecard. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.category: result fixed by construction / code bug
findings.description: leidenalg was not installed, so the code silently fell back to SpectralClustering with n_clusters=10, which assigns every alive feature to a cluster. '10 modules per layer at 99.9–100% coverage — matches the paper precisely (6–12 modules, 96–99.5%)' is therefore hard-coded, and it is repeated in all 12 layers ('120 modules'). In the 3-layer script the fallback also clusters pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive] (the first n_alive feature indices, not the alive ones) and assigns the labels to alive_idx[:len(labels)]. At L0, where 2430 features are dead, the labels are attached to the wrong features.
findings.evidence: Log: 'leidenalg not installed — skipping Leiden, using k-means instead'. Every layer reports exactly 10 modules.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Use Leiden or a modularity-optimising method and report modularity against a shuffled-PMI null. Drop the 'matches precisely' claim. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.location: runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/phases2_to_8.py:222-262 (L242 'alive' is a file-shape boolean), 286-300 (L292 n_src_alive by decoder norm); outputs/phase3/svd_comparison.csv, phase4/cross_layer_tracking.csv; summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:29-46,96-103; summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY_12layer.md:28-37; summaries/sae-atlas-crosslayer-analysis.log
findings.category: denominator bug / by-construction metric / contradictory claims
findings.description: Dead features are counted in two places. At L0, 2430 dead features count as 'novel' (4928/4928 = 100%) and as the persistence denominator (125/4928 = 2.5%; per alive feature it is 125/2498 = 5.0%). '99.9% invisible to SVD — massive superposition confirmed' is near-guaranteed by construction (|cos| > 0.7 against only 50 SVD directions) and does not test superposition. For persistence, the main summary matches MaxToki L0→L5 (2.5%) to the paper's L0→L1 (2.5%) and says 'features are layer-specific — replicates'. The 12-layer summary concludes the opposite ('dramatically higher persistence than Geneformer', 21.5% peak) and misreports L0→L1 as 0.5% (log: 0/4928). 'Information highways 99.6–100%' (≥1 of 4928 targets with PMI > 3) has no null. Smaller inconsistencies: L5 alive 4903 vs 4928, '50' vs '30' richly-annotated features, '~50% unannotated' vs 32%.
findings.evidence: svd_comparison.csv: L0 n_novel = 4928. cross_layer_tracking.csv: n_src_alive = 4928 at L0. Crosslayer log: L0→L1 0/4928, L6→L7 1059/4928.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Exclude dead features, add random-direction and shuffled baselines for novelty, persistence and highways, and reconcile the two summaries into one claim. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: Cell-type enrichment uses Fisher tests over token positions (about 1000 cells × about 1000-2000 positions). All positions in a cell share that cell's type label, so the p-values reflect positions rather than cells or donors, and nearly any feature that differs slightly between types becomes 'enriched'. Bonferroni corrects over the 32 types only, not over 4928 features. The cells are the first 1000 rows, not a random sample, and the layer mismatch of F05 applies. The 95.9% figure ('paper 99.0%, replicates') is uninformative.
findings.evidence: Code: active = h_ts[:, fi] > 0 over flattened positions; ct_array repeats the cell's type for every position; the threshold is p < 0.05/len(unique_cts).
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Aggregate activations per cell, test with cell (or donor) as the unit, correct across features, and sample cells randomly. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.description: The headline 'MaxToki-217M internally encodes a hematopoietic developmental manifold' and 'the first affirmative deployable result' are not qualified by the project's own Phase-12 LITE baseline. PCA-10 and SVD-10 on raw expression match or beat the extracted MaxToki head on branch and stage, with no significant difference on any endpoint. The sweep manifolds ('multi-axis biological hub', e.g. lymphoid vs myeloid) have no expression-PCA comparator at all.
findings.evidence: Phase 12 LITE branch: pca10 0.844, svd10 0.837, frozen avgpool 0.792, extracted_z10 0.756. 'no significant differences on any endpoint at BH-q < 0.05; extracted_z10 trends lower'.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify/re-run) Put 'Δ vs PCA-on-expression' in the headline and restate as 'recoverable from the MaxToki residual to the same degree as from expression PCA'. Run PCA baselines for the sweep rulers. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.location: runs/manifold-discovery-217M/reports/quality_gates_spec.json; reports/quality_gates_let_anchor.json; scripts/phase5_let_anchor.py:138-300; scripts/phase3a_revaluate_3gate.py; reports/hypothesis_registry_3gate.csv; reports/zeroshot_h103.json; FINAL_SUMMARY.md:41,194-196,330-345
findings.category: pre-registered gates not followed / post-hoc relaxation (P1/P5)
findings.description:
The frozen gate specification requires five gates, including a blocked permutation test (p ≤ 0.001, ≥ 2000 permutations, blocked by donor and tissue). It also states that loosening any gate 'invalidates the entire run'. In practice:
- The blocked permutation gate was never computed; no permutation code exists in phases 5, 7, 8, 9 or 10.
- Each null is a single precomputed shuffle with a single seed.
- The trust gate does not discriminate (positive 0.811 vs null 0.7985), and the null also passes the random (0.799) and donor (0.707) gates. H65 therefore rests on branch holdout alone.
- A post-hoc '3-gate fallback' re-labels sweep candidates from INCONCLUSIVE to POSITIVE. H95 passes trust by 0.0005 (0.8005).
- The H103 zero-shot run uses trustworthiness k=5 instead of the frozen k=15.
The summary nevertheless says gates were 'frozen at Phase 0, never relaxed'. Across the 18+ sweep candidates there is no multiplicity control.
findings.evidence: quality_gates_let_anchor.json lists only 4 gates. hypothesis_registry_3gate.csv: H95 original_verdict INCONCLUSIVE → revalued POSITIVE_3GATE_FALLBACK, trust_pos 0.800483. zeroshot_h103.json: 'Used k=5 for trustworthiness'.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Compute the blocked permutation test (≥2000 permutations), use multiple null shuffles and seeds, report the sweep under the frozen 4/5-gate rule with BH across candidates, and state the deviations explicitly. Effort: about half a day.

findings.description: The lung_nonhema 'negative control' assigns random H65 stage labels to non-hematopoietic cells. Any representation fails the rank-correlation gates on random labels, so the control cannot show that 'the manifold genuinely captures hematopoietic biology, not generic tissue covariance' or that 'the gates aren't too loose'. The trust gate still passes (0.800), which is further evidence that trust does not discriminate.
findings.evidence: FINAL_SUMMARY L39: 'Random H65 stage labels assigned (uncorrelated with cell biology)'. Results: random −0.016, donor 0.013, branch −0.147.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Add model-level controls on the same hematopoietic panel: random-init MaxToki, expression PCA, and a structure-matched scrambled ruler. Reword the claim. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: L10H6 is chosen as the best of 88 single-head variants on the internal panel, and the compaction chain is then evaluated on the same panel. 'Compact-top1 beats full-drift on every metric' (trust 0.882 vs 0.811) and rank-8 trust 0.956 are winner's-curse estimates. Non-monotone branch values across ranks (0.352 / 0.216 / 0.420 / 0.514) point to substantial noise, and no compact variant is evaluated on the external or zero-shot panels.
findings.evidence: Both scripts load anchors/centroids_internal.npy and d_target_internal.npy, and the head is selected by sort_values('score').
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Select heads on a training split or donor fold, evaluate compact variants on the external and zero-shot panels with seed and bootstrap CIs, and qualify the claims. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: 'Maturity' is defined from PC1 of log1p counts in 200 cells. The sign and the biological meaning of PC1 are never checked against maturation markers or a real pseudotime. The 5,767 'switch features' (|ρ| > 0.3, p < 0.01 with no FDR and no permutation null) are read as 'temporal information permeates every layer'. Gene interpretations are wrong or loose: FTL is described as a 'terminal erythroid marker', but it is the ubiquitous ferritin light chain, highest in macrophages. The summary also reports cos(g_early, g_late) ≈ 0.999, while the saved logit signatures give 0.881.
findings.evidence: Recomputed cos(g_early_logits, g_late_logits) = 0.881 (expression signatures 0.750). Per-cell clean score: early −0.115 ± 0.031, late +0.115.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run/qualify) Validate the pseudotime with diffusion pseudotime and known maturation markers, apply FDR and a permutation null to switch-feature counts, and correct the gene annotations. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: 'No run's attention beats any of the three trivial baselines' is false. In RPE1, attention significantly beats both mean expression and (1 − dropout). 'TF out-degree underperforms attention everywhere' is also not significant in Adamson. The overall C1 FAIL still holds because gene variance beats attention. The invariant claim 'attention information is a subset of gene-level univariate features' is not supported as stated for RPE1.
findings.evidence: RPE1: attention 0.603 vs mean expression 0.582 (Δ −0.021, p_BH 7.3e-8) and vs 1−dropout 0.500 (Δ −0.103, p_BH 4.1e-36). Adamson: TF out-degree vs attention p_BH 0.060.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Correct the text and report results per baseline. For RPE1, test attention against the combined gene-feature model; the Phase-2 ΔAUROC of −0.0003 can be cited. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: C3 ('residualized attention retains >50% of above-chance TRRUST signal') is undefined when the baseline TRRUST AUROC is below 0.5. For K562 it is 0.483, giving 'fraction retained' = −13,421, so the K562 FAIL is as vacuous as the acknowledged Adamson PASS. C4 runs ablation where the baseline TRRUST AUROC at L8 is 0.440, again below chance. There is then no TRRUST signal for the 'regulatory heads' to lose, and the heads were ranked on the same data. Three random draws span −0.018 to +0.005, a noise band equal to the 0.02 threshold, and no CI is given. 'The same causal null as the paper' and 'residualized AUROC collapses to chance in every run' (K562 and Adamson were at chance before residualization) are not supported.
findings.evidence: phase12_verdict.json: C3 fraction_above_chance_retained = −13421.31, baseline 0.4829. C4 baseline 0.4399, top5 0.4347, random-5 deltas [−0.0146, +0.0054, −0.0180].
findings.recommended_action: (qualify/re-run) Mark C3/C4 'not evaluable' when the baseline is ≤ 0.5. Bootstrap ablation CIs over cells and draw more random-head sets. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.location: project-wide: runs/attention-grn-217M (C2/C4), runs/sae-atlas-217M (TF specificity), runs/longevity-mechinterp-217M (G1), runs/circuit-tracing-217M (CRISPRi); grep for 'positive control|synthetic|planted' in runs/ found no such controls
findings.category: no positive control for null findings (P6)
findings.description: Every load-bearing negative in the project is reported without evidence that the pipeline can detect a planted or known signal. Examples: the attention-GRN incremental-value and causal-head nulls, SAE '0% TF specificity', longevity 'model does not encode age' and Stage-2 'circuits encode co-expression'. Given the confirmed implementation bugs (F01-F05), positive controls are especially needed before any negative is accepted.
findings.evidence: No synthetic or planted-edge experiment exists in any scripts/ folder. Negatives are framed as properties of MaxToki in all summaries (e.g., 'The limitation is in MaxToki's representations, not the SAE training data').
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Add a short positive-control phase per pipeline (checklist P6): a planted-edge synthetic graph or a known-strong real case (e.g., GATA1/TAL1 targets in K562) passed through the same metrics and nulls. Effort: about half a day per pipeline.

findings.location: project-wide: sae-atlas (single SAE training per layer, seed 42), manifold-discovery (SEED=42, single null shuffle), topology Phase 10 H139 (1 seed, layer 11), Phase 14 CCA, Phase 16 H-hub, exhaustive Exp 3 (50 cells), attention Phase 4 (300 cells), Phase 2 ΔAUROC
findings.description: Headline numbers are single point estimates without seed sweeps, bootstrap CIs or DeLong tests. Examples: CCA r=0.78; the H139 null-gap of +0.001 used as evidence that MaxToki 'mirrors' the paper's immune-only pattern; manifold gate values that sit within 0.001-0.01 of the thresholds; SAE variance explained and annotation rates; steering fractions; attention ΔAUROC ≤ 0.002 interpreted as scaling. Topology Phase 1 built 3 split seeds, but later phases do not use them.
findings.evidence: H139 immune null-gap +0.001; H95 trust 0.8005; positive trust 0.811 vs null 0.7985. Attention: '+0.002 at 1B vs +0.0007 at 217M ... scales 2.8×' with no CI.
findings.recommended_action: (re-run) Bootstrap at the inference unit (TF, donor, cell), use ≥3 seeds for SAE and LET training, and report 95% CIs for all summary-level numbers. Effort: ≥ half a day.

findings.description: The summary claims 'MaxToki L5 does beat HVG-PCA-50 (+10.3 pp) — it is encoding something beyond raw expression PCA', but both probes are below chance (balanced accuracy 1/3 for 3 classes; the permutation null mean is 0.332). Comparing two below-chance numbers says nothing about what is encoded. Age is a donor-level label: the 17 donors fall 10/4/3 across the bins, so 5-fold donor CV leaves at most 3 donors of the oldest class. The G1 test therefore has essentially no power, and its 'does imply' statement is too strong.
findings.evidence: probe_aggregate: MaxToki 0.2755 ± 0.035, HVG-PCA 0.1722 ± 0.037. null_mean 0.332. sampled_obs: 17 donors, one age per donor, bin counts 10/4/3.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Remove the 'encodes something beyond PCA' sentence and state that the test is underpowered at 17 donors, with donors as the inference unit. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description:
Several numbers and generalizations in the summary are wrong or unsupported:
- Phase 0b values are mis-transcribed: the summary gives VW 0.513 vs raw 0.532, while the log shows 0.4933 vs 0.5119.
- The 'architectural asymmetry' compares per-perturbation AUROC for raw attention (L1 0.553) with TRRUST AUROC for value-weighted attention (L9 0.588), which are different metrics.
- '1B has ~2.7× the improvement' should be ≈3.3× ((0.540−0.5)/(0.512−0.5)), and the 1B run used N=200 cells against 2000 for 217M, so scale is confounded with sample size.
- 'Specific to bidirectional BERT-style encoders' is asserted without any Geneformer run in this project.
- The README says Phase 0b was skipped, but its results are reported.
findings.evidence: phase0b.log: 'VW primary mean AUROC: 0.4933; attn primary mean AUROC: 0.5119; Δ = −0.0186'. FINAL_SUMMARY table: N_ctrl 200 for k562_1b.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Correct the numbers, compare like metrics, flag the N confound, and drop the BERT generalization. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: The headline says '22× denser' while the body says '41× denser'; the actual ratio is 41.1× (2,144,011 / 52,116). Biological coherence (36.1%) and the TRRUST match rate (0.01%) are compared with the paper without chance baselines such as random feature pairs or random gene pairs. 'Replicates' labels for inhibitory dominance, broadcast hubs and effect size rest on the artefact in F02. The run folder has no README or FINAL_SUMMARY, contrary to the expected layout.
findings.evidence: Lines 5 vs 53; computed ratio 41.1.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Fix the ratio, add random-pair baselines, and add run-folder documentation. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description:
FINAL_SUMMARY still says Phase 4 cross-model CCA, the Phase 11 autoloop and the H124-H138 chain were 'SKIPPED' and that 'Layer 1 cannot be evaluated'. The README and EXTENDED_FINDINGS report all three as run and Layer 1 as 'partially replicates'. Two numbers in the TL;DR are also wrong:
- 'Eucl ≈ Geo (≈0)', but the Layer-3 row of the same file gives euclidean −0.035 and geodesic −0.035.
- 'H91 Δ ≈ +0.01 over chance', but external-lung has mean AUC 0.545.
findings.evidence: FINAL_SUMMARY L39 'Phase 4 cross-model CCA: SKIPPED' vs README L17 'included'. L15 vs L63.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Regenerate FINAL_SUMMARY from current outputs. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: SV3 PPI significance appears both as '3/12 layers' and as '10/12 sig; L0 max z=5.62'. The data support 3/12 (BH q < 0.05 at L7, L9, L11), and SV3 at L0 has z = 0.01. The extracellular result is given as 'z=5.21' in one place and 'OR=5.21' in another. The Scope section says phases 8, 9a, 9b, 9c and 10 were skipped, yet results for them appear later in the document. The Phase-10 autoloop was actually run on 2026-05-05: iterations 2-5 produced hypotheses marked 'promising' (e.g., H01 persistence ratio, H3-BC STRING persistence) and then aborted after 2 failures. The FINAL_SUMMARY says Phase 10 was 'NOT run ... deferred pending explicit user authorization'.
findings.evidence: ppi csv: SV3 pairs_700 p_bh < 0.05 only at layers 7, 9, 11; L0 z = 0.013. autoloop_master_log: 'iters 2..9 ... ABORT after 2 consecutive failures'.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Reconcile the numbers and disclose the autoloop run and its outputs, including the negatives. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.location: summaries/exhaustive-mapping-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md (Exp 2 headline; 'Comparison to Stage 2'; validation table #7, #10, #12; 'None indicate a broken implementation')
findings.description: The Exp-2 headline says redundancy 'deepens monotonically', but the v1 numbers go from pairwise 0.165 to three-way 0.190, an increase. The summary says '~5K edges/feature in both experiments', but Stage 2 had 17,867 edges per feature. The validation table reports cos(g_early, g_late) ≈ 0.999, while the saved file gives 0.881. 'None indicate a broken implementation' is stated even though the across-triplet and α-invariance signatures pointed to F02/F03.
findings.evidence: Stage 2: 2,144,011 edges / 120 features = 17,867 per feature. Recomputed cosine 0.881.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Correct after the re-run in F02/F03. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: 'Ext-lung 4/4 lineages sig (all z > 3)' includes B-cell, which has 3 markers and an observed purity (0.0556) equal to the null p95 (0.0556). Its 'significance' comes from a Gaussian z (3.05) applied to a discrete, skewed null. Lineages with very few markers (3-8) make purity estimates rest on one or two neighbours.
findings.evidence: h_lineage_marker_purity.csv: external_lung B_cell obs 0.0556, null_p95 0.0556, z 3.05. Lung NK z = −0.55.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Use empirical permutation p-values (obs > p95), report n_markers, and state '3/4' for ext-lung. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: Verdicts such as '0–1/12 layers positive' treat 12 highly correlated layer states as independent replicates; cross-layer correlation of the feature is about 0.6-0.7. Per-pair AUROCs over 751-2544 pairs that share TF and target endpoints are tested with label permutations that are not grouped by endpoint. The inference unit (TFs, targets) is never stated.
findings.evidence: iter_04 mean cross-layer Pearson 0.60-0.68. phase1: n_pairs 1308 / 2544 / 751 over 382 / 350 / 380 genes.
findings.recommended_action: (annotate/qualify) Report the inference unit and use endpoint-grouped resampling for nulls and CIs. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.location: project-wide: runs/attention-grn-217M/README.md:46-58 (unpinned pip); BIOM_ROOT/GENEFORMER_DIR hard-coded in runs/*/scripts (e.g., topology phase14_cross_model_cca.py:39,45-48; phase4_scgpt external .pt); outputs/phases2_to_8.log:78; longevity FINAL_SUMMARY.md:94-106; summaries/*FINAL_SUMMARY vs runs/*/FINAL_SUMMARY diffs
findings.description:
Reproducibility scaffolding is missing:
- There is no requirements.txt, environment file or lock file, only lower-bounded pip specifiers in one README.
- Scripts hard-code absolute paths to external data and caches (<DATA_ROOT>, a ~/.cache Geneformer snapshot, a scGPT .pt from another subproject).
- Missing packages silently changed methods (leidenalg → spectral clustering) or crashed runs (tabulate).
- The circuit-tracing and sae-atlas run folders lack README/FINAL_SUMMARY.
- The summaries/ copies of the FINAL_SUMMARYs diverge from the run-folder copies for attention-grn, spectral-geometry and manifold-discovery.
- Wall-time logging is inconsistent, and no public repository or DOI is recorded.
findings.evidence: diff shows extra sections in summaries/ versions. grep finds 15+ hard-coded absolute paths.
findings.recommended_action: (annotate) Add a pinned environment file, make data and reference paths configurable, fail loudly on a missing method dependency, keep a single canonical FINAL_SUMMARY per run, and add RUNTIME.md. Effort: 1-2 hr.

findings.description: All runs tokenize with Geneformer's gc104M gene-median dictionary instead of MaxToki's own, on the stated assumption that the values are 'within noise'. No in-distribution check (e.g., next-token loss or accuracy on held-out cells) was reported. Truncation differs between runs (2048 vs 1024 genes). 'L11' everywhere is HF hidden_states[11], which comes after the final RMSNorm, unlike L0-L10. It is analysed as an ordinary residual layer (spectral effective rank, SAE L11, topology L11), and the exhaustive summary describes it incorrectly as pre-norm.
findings.evidence: README deviation #2. Adapter DEFAULT_GENE_MEDIAN_PKL points to gene_median_dictionary_gc104M.pkl. Truncation: longevity max_genes 1024 vs 2048 elsewhere.
findings.recommended_action: (annotate) Report the model's next-token loss on the tokenized inputs, document the post-norm status of the final layer, and treat L11 separately in depth trends. Effort: about 1 hr.

findings.description: TRRUST (curated literature, not specific to K562 or RPE1) and Replogle DE (direct plus indirect effects) are used as ground truth for 'regulatory signal'. Conclusions are phrased as the model 'does not encode causal regulatory logic' rather than in terms of what was measured: no incremental value over gene-level features for predicting perturbation DE (Objective B) and degree-explained TRRUST AUROC (Objective A). In the cross-pipeline synthesis, MaxToki 'is a trajectory generative model, not a regulatory-edge inference model' rests partly on invalid evidence (F01, F03).
findings.evidence: RPE1 TRRUST AUROC 0.6045 equals the curveball null 0.6043: degree explains everything. Phase-2 ΔAUROC ≤ 0.002.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Restate claims using the two-objective framing, tag the cell-type context of each database, and remove the synthesis statements that depend on F01/F03. Effort: ≤30 min.

findings.description: The README says the cohort has 24 donors; the data and FINAL_SUMMARY have 17. 'L5 is the canonical mid-stack tap used by every other MaxToki pipeline' is false: attention-GRN uses L8 as its primary layer; topology and spectral-geometry analyse all layers; manifold-discovery uses pooled drift and L10H6. The comparability argument built on that claim does not hold.
findings.evidence: extraction_stats.json n_donors_final = 17. attention-grn README: 'Primary layer L8'.
findings.recommended_action: (qualify) Correct both statements. Effort: ≤30 min.
