verdicts.reason: Confirmed in both phases2_to_8.py and full_12layer_pipeline.py: enrichments are kept only when x>=2 and p<0.1, and fdr_bh is then run on that pre-filtered subset only. I recomputed from the saved significant_enrichments.csv (max saved p is about 0.04). Using full-family BH (m = n_alive x 2369, from the log 'testing ... x 2369 terms'), the annotated features are 29/2498 (1.2%) at L0, 5/4928 (0.1%) at L5 and 0/4924 at L11. Per-feature BH gives 104 (4.2%), 84 (1.7%) and 55 (1.1%). The reported rates are 80.7%, 67.8% and 61.7%. The share of 'significant' rows resting on an overlap of 2 is 0.79, 0.83 and 0.85. The annotation rate, the U-shape, the 'more interpretable than Geneformer' claim and the annotated/unannotated splits used downstream (Stage-2 feature selection, the Stage-3 500/500 split) all depend on this.

Confirmed. cross_domain_alignment.csv has L0 Pearson 1.000 and top-1 1.0 for all three pairs, and best_layer=0 in phase15_summary.json. Excluding L0, the mean Pearson is 0.849, 0.746 and 0.717. Top-1 at L11 is 0.667, 0.250 and 0.299. The only null is a gene-label shuffle (z 6.6-100), and the script has no within-tissue split-half ceiling. So 'tissue-invariant' and 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel)' are not tested. The lowest L11 retrieval is lung vs external-lung (same tissue), so the divergence cannot be told apart from dataset or sampling noise. Cross-tissue similarity is still high beyond L0; the problem is the invariance claim and the 'strong' label, not that the numbers are wrong.

Confirmed. immune run_config.json has reused=true, with the spectral-geometry phase0 as source. The immune-reuse code ranks TFs first when capping at 350 and has no cap on TF count, while select_topology_gene_pool for lung and external-lung caps TFs at 80. As a result immune gene_features has is_trrust_tf=343/350, against 87/382 for lung and 86/380 for external-lung. Neither FINAL_SUMMARY nor EXTENDED_FINDINGS acknowledges this composition difference, apart from the missing lineage markers. It confounds the immune results and the cross-domain comparisons. In the pair table, immune negatives are 99.95% TF-containing versus about 40% in the other two domains.

The code matches the description: positives are TRRUST pairs, STRING-only pairs are labelled 0, and negatives are random. In the pair tables, 100% of positives contain a TF, against 41% (lung) and 39% (external-lung) of random negatives. Only 48, 24 and 61 negatives are STRING-only. The spec itself calls for coexpression-matched and TF/target-degree-matched negatives, so this is a real design confound. The impact on the claims is limited, though. ΔAUROC is taken against a coexpression baseline on the same pairs, which partly cancels the shared confound. The immune domain, where negatives are almost all TF pairs, gives the same negative verdicts. That makes it unlikely the confound drives the headline non-replications. Its main effect is on reading the below-chance values (e.g. triangle defect -0.055).

The numbers are confirmed: Spearman 0.060, 0.118 and 0.115; z 1.31, 2.34 and 2.36; 100 permutations; L6 and k=12 only; no correction and no expression or literature-degree control. In lung and external-lung, non-TFs get degree 0, so the statistic partly measures TF versus non-TF identity. Calling it 'strongest new result' and listing it among the things MaxToki encodes is an overclaim. The documents do report z of about 2.3 openly, say it is 'an order of magnitude smaller', and label it 'weak-positive' in the hierarchy table. The empirical p of about 0.01 might survive BH across 3 domains. So this is overinterpretation rather than an invalid number.

Reproduced exactly from pair_table.csv and the L6 PCA-20 embeddings. Lung: 62 edges, 13 positive, AUROC 0.352, bootstrap 95% CI [0.183, 0.530]. Immune: 123 edges, 22 positive, AUROC 0.416, CI [0.289, 0.542]. External-lung: 52 edges, 11 positive, AUROC 0.340, CI [0.159, 0.545]. The code declares replication purely as AUROC < 0.45. All three CIs include 0.5, so 'DIRECTIONAL REPLICATES ... Validates the spec implementation' is overstated. The point estimates are consistent with the paper's direction. This is a sanity-check overclaim that does not change any main verdict.

Confirmed. phase9b_cross_model.py compares a Pearson of off-diagonal similarity matrices (0.382) with a gene-label-shuffle null (mean -0.000, sd 0.001, p=0, n=500). The spec describes the paper's p>0.3 as reflecting a 'shared-vocabulary null', and its 0.825 is a raw cosine, so both the statistic and the null differ. MaxToki and Geneformer V2 share the identical tokenizer, so a gene-shuffle null cannot rule out vocabulary artefacts, despite the summary's wording. 'Paper's null does NOT replicate' is therefore unsupported. The B-cell prec@10 caveat (marker-rich HVG set) is already hedged in the text. Impact is limited to one or two scorecard rows.

Confirmed. lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv has n_markers 6 (B) and 9 (T), and TwoNN with the F<0.9 mask uses about 5-8 ratios. The B-cell estimates (101 to 6.2) almost exactly track the global TwoNN (102 to 6.7), so this is global compression, not a lineage effect, and there is no random-set normalisation. Audit item #16 says 'distance metrics replicate strongly' although depth_correlations gives BATF-to-PAX5 rho=+0.979 (divergence), which contradicts Key finding #10. The summary does already flag that lineage specificity fails (T-cell also compresses; item 19 is marked partial). So the net scorecard misstatement is modest.

Confirmed. The phases2_to_8.log says 'leidenalg not installed', and both scripts fall back to SpectralClustering(n_clusters=min(10, n_alive)), so every layer gets exactly 10 modules and covers all alive features by construction. Some modules have only 2 features (L0 sizes include 2 and 2). The summary still says the result 'matches precisely' the paper's 6-12 modules and 96-99.5% coverage, and the fallback is not disclosed. One part of the finding has no effect: the 3-layer script does mis-index pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive], but the module_labels.npy on disk come from the 12-layer run, which uses np.ix_(alive_mask, alive_mask). There, labelled features equal the 2498 alive features at L0, and the reported coverage numbers are unchanged.

Confirmed. svd_comparison.csv has L0 n_novel=4928 (dead features included), and cross_layer_tracking.csv has n_src_alive=4928 at L0, set by decoder norm. The main summary matches L0 to L5 (2.5%) against the paper's L0 to L1 and says features are 'layer-specific — replicates'. The 12-layer summary says the opposite ('dramatically higher persistence', 21.5% peak) and reports L0 to L1 as 0.5%, while the crosslayer log shows 0/4928. Highways (>=1 target with PMI>3) have no null. The smaller inconsistencies also check out: 4903 vs 4928 alive at L5, '50' vs '30' richly-annotated, and ~50% unannotated vs 32% implied. The novelty denominator does not change the near-100% figure, since 0 features are aligned at L0. The persistence contradiction and the misreported value are real.

The premise is wrong. In phase12_anchor_benchmark_lite.py, pca10 and svd10 are PCA and TruncatedSVD of avg_pool = centroids.mean(axis=1), and centroids_internal.npy holds MaxToki hidden-state centroids (290 x 12 x 1232) saved by phase1bc. They are not raw expression. Even 'raw_log1p' is log1p of the shifted MaxToki avg-pool. So Phase-12 LITE shows that simple PCA of the MaxToki residual recovers the manifold as well as the LET head, which supports 'recoverable from the residual' rather than undermining it. The summary's §11 already states there is no advantage over PCA/SVD/avg-pool. Separately, the summary mislabels raw_log1p as 'raw expression', and no actual expression baseline exists. That is a different issue from the one claimed here.

Confirmed. probe_aggregate.csv gives MaxToki 0.2755 and HVG-PCA 0.1722, both below 1/3 chance, with null mean 0.332. sampled_obs.csv has 17 donors, one age bin per donor, and bin counts 10/4/3. Comparing two below-chance balanced accuracies cannot show that MaxToki is 'encoding something beyond raw expression PCA', so that sentence is unsupported. The main conclusion (G1 fails, stop) is unaffected, and the summary already says the gate is built for at least 30-50 donors and this cohort had 17. The error is limited to one interpretive sentence.

Confirmed. The run-folder FINAL_SUMMARY.md still lists Phase 4 CCA, the Phase 11 autoloop and the H124-H138 chain as SKIPPED, and Layer 1 as 'cannot be evaluated'. README.md lists them as included or run, and EXTENDED_FINDINGS reports Layer 1 as partially replicating. The TL;DR says 'Eucl ≈ Geo (≈0)' while the L3 row of the same file gives -0.035 for both, and 'H91 Δ ≈ +0.01' while external-lung has a mean AUC of 0.545. The updated summaries/ copy keeps the stale 'SKIPPED' row and 'Δ ≈ +0.01'. These are documentation inconsistencies only.

Confirmed. In h_lineage_marker_purity.csv, external-lung B_cell has n_markers=3, obs_purity 0.0556 equal to null_p95 0.0556, and z=3.05. With 3 markers and k=12, this purity is just 2 of 36 neighbour slots, and the null is discrete and skewed, so a Gaussian z is inappropriate. The empirical one-sided p is at least about 0.05. The '4/4 lineages sig (all z>3)' claim should be 3/4. The other lineages have large margins, so the effect is small.

review.summary:
I audited all 8 runs (attention-GRN, spectral-geometry, topology-141, SAE atlas, circuit tracing, exhaustive mapping, manifold discovery, longevity) against CHECKLIST_DEPLOYED.md §6 (P1–P10 plus the 6.11 workflow). For each load-bearing claim I went from the claim to the CSV/JSON outputs to the script that produced them, and I recomputed key numbers in Python.

**Totals:** 38 findings — 7 critical, 26 major, 5 minor. A few issues are already acknowledged in the run docs: the Adamson C3 "trivial pass", the Phase-12 LITE baseline parity (mentioned in the body only), the spectral PH test being uninformative, and the longevity small-cohort caveat. Most others are unaddressed.

**Critical: code bugs that invalidate headline results**
1. **Circuit-tracing CRISPRi check ignores the model.** The Phase-11 "directional accuracy 54.6%" never uses the predicted edge sign; it just counts target LFC<0. Five run summaries cite this number as evidence against causal regulatory logic.
2. **Every SAE ablation and steering intervention skips a whole transformer block.** hidden_states[l] is injected as the output of block l. This affects Stage 2 and all of Stage 3 (edge counts, inhibitory %, redundancy, synergy, steering). The signature is visible in the outputs: L0 hub out-degrees 39,670–39,676, redundancy ratios identical to 4 decimals across distinct triplets, effects that do not change with α.
3. **L11 steering applies the final RMSNorm twice.** HF hidden_states[-1] is already normed.
4. **SAE annotation rates are inflated by a multiple-testing error.** BH was applied only to tests pre-filtered at p<0.1. With per-feature BH the 62–81% rates fall to 1.1–4.2%; with global BH to ≤1.2%.
5. **SAE causal patching (Phase 6) uses the wrong layer and replaces the full hidden state.** The L5 SAE is applied to hidden[6], and the whole SAE reconstruction is injected instead of a delta, so the 1.01× specificity mostly reflects reconstruction error common to every feature.
6. **SAE TF-specificity tests are not valid.** Perturbed cells are encoded from hidden[6] but compared with control activations from hidden[5]. The proxy test only tests token identity. The true-CRISPRi run detects just 3/48 TFs, and "0% vs 6.2%" is not significant (Fisher p=0.24).
7. **Spectral lineage intrinsic-dimension estimates use 6 and 9 points.** The B-cell and T-cell TwoNN "compression" verdicts rest on 6 and 9 marker genes.

**Major: wrong statistics, missing controls, misreporting**
- **Topology cross-model alignment (Phase 4/14):** CCA and Procrustes are fit in-sample with no refitted null. Random matrices of the same size give CCA mean r ≈ 0.40–0.43 and top-1 retrieval 4–8%, the same as the reported scGPT "alignment".
- **Other topology positives:**
  - Cross-tissue invariance includes a trivial layer-0 value of 1.0, and similarity actually declines with depth.
  - The autoloop "novel positive" was reclassified after the fact and tested against a hard-coded 0.3 instead of a null.
  - The TwoNN estimator has a bug that produces negative dimensions.
- **Attention-GRN:** the final summary misreports the 1B C3 result (it passed) and the RPE1 baselines. The C3, C4 and curveball tests were run at L8, where TRRUST AUROC is already below chance, while L1 reaches 0.684. Causal masking ties attention edges to expression rank.
- **SAE structural claims hold by construction:**
  - "10 modules per layer" is fixed by the clustering fallback.
  - "Massive superposition" comes from a novelty test that almost any direction passes.
  - Cell-type enrichment counts token positions as independent samples.
  - The two SAE summaries contradict each other on cross-layer persistence.
- **Circuit and exhaustive mapping:** circuit coherence has no chance baseline, and the hub-annotation claims rest on noise.
- **Manifold discovery:**
  - PCA on expression matches or beats the extracted manifold.
  - The pre-registered permutation gate was never computed, gates were relaxed for H95/H103, and the negative control did not meet its pre-registered signature.
  - The orthogonality result is explained by fit attenuation.
  - The best head was selected and then evaluated on the same panel.
- **Longevity:** the age bins are degenerate, both representations score below chance, and the claim that MaxToki "beats PCA" does not follow.
- **Spectral geometry:**
  - Its stability comparison measures something different from the paper's (cell samples, not training seeds).
  - "Learned compression" rests only on a feature-shuffle null.
  - Cell-type clustering relies on the static layer-0 embedding.
  - Several numbers are misreported.
- **Cross-run:** no run has a positive control or random-init model control, generalisation and stability checks are thin, and causal/mechanistic wording goes beyond the evidence.

**Patterns the project remains exposed to:** all ten (P1–P10). The worst are P1 (null models), P5 (selection), P6 (positive controls) and outright implementation bugs, which go beyond the catalogue as §10 pitfall 4 anticipates. Pipelines needing re-runs before any claims stand: circuit tracing and exhaustive mapping (fix the hooks and Phase-11 logic), SAE atlas Phases 2/6/8t/9/11, and topology Phases 14/15/16.

findings.pipeline: circuit-tracing-217M (propagated to attention-grn, topology-141, sae-atlas, exhaustive-mapping summaries)
findings.description: The Phase-11 'CRISPRi directional accuracy' never compares a predicted direction with the observed one. predicted_inhibitory is computed (and is always True because max_d is a max |d|) but never used. A pair counts as 'correct' whenever actual_lfc < 0. The 54.6% therefore only measures how often target genes go down after any knockdown in Replogle K562, independent of the circuit. The headline 'CRISPRi 54.6% near-chance, confirming circuits encode co-expression not causal regulation' is cited across pipelines as the main evidence against causal regulatory logic, and it has no bearing on the model.
findings.evidence: Lines 322-328: `predicted_inhibitory = info["max_d"] > 0` (unused); `if (actual_lfc < 0): n_correct_direction += 1`. phase11_crispri_validation.json: n_validated 1,458,016, n_correct 796,159 (0.5461). The 50% 'chance' reference is also not the right baseline for a sign-agnostic count.
findings.recommended_action: Re-run Phase 11 using each edge's signed effect, propagating the sign through the feature→gene mapping. Compute a chance baseline from the marginal sign distributions plus a pair-permutation null, and report CIs with bootstrap over source genes. Until then, remove the 54.6% claim from every summary that cites it.

findings.description: SAEs at layer l are trained on HF hidden_states[l], which is the input to block l (hidden_states[0] is the embedding output). Every ablation and steering script builds h_patched = hidden_states[l] + delta and installs it as the forward-hook output of model.layers[l]. That replaces block l's output with its own input, so each 'single-feature ablation' or 'steering' also deletes the entire transformer block l. Downstream effects are dominated by the missing block, not by the feature. Every Stage-2 and Stage-3 causal number is invalid: 2.14M edges, 88.2% inhibitory, mean |d| 1.84, depth attenuation, 'uniformly dense' circuits, redundancy 0.165/0.324/0.190, zero synergy, steering frac_mat by layer and α-saturation.
findings.evidence: The outputs show feature-independent effects. Top-5 L0 hubs have out-degrees of 39,676 / 39,674 / 39,672 / 39,672 / 39,670. All 1,000 Exp-1 features have >1,000 edges, with the top-20 between 4,990 and 5,400. Exp-2 v2 uses four distinct L0/L5/L9 feature triplets, yet AB/AC/BC/three-way ratios are identical to 4 decimals (0.1652–0.1656, 0.2189–0.2191, 0.5858–0.5861, 0.1896–0.1897), and v1 (different features) gives three-way 0.1897 vs v2 0.1896. Steering metrics are identical at α=2 and α=5 (L0 Δs +0.0963 vs +0.0962; |Δlogit| 0.4224 vs 0.4212). The summary itself argues this invariance is 'a real property of MaxToki, not a code bug'.
findings.recommended_action: Patch hidden_states[l] at its true source: the output of model.layers[l-1], or embed_tokens for l=0. Alternatively, hook a forward_pre_hook on layers[l]. Add a no-op control (delta=0 must give zero downstream change) and a random-direction control, then re-run Stage 2 and Stage-3 Exp 1–3. Withdraw all derived claims and cross-references (attention-GRN, SAE and topology summaries) until then.

findings.description: In HF LlamaModel, hidden_states[-1] (index 11 for this 11-block model) is taken after the final RMSNorm. The SAE 'L11' is therefore trained on post-norm states, and the summary's description of it as 'the final residual before RMSNorm + lm_head' is wrong. The 'final-residual hook fix' replaces layers[10]'s output with norm(h)+delta, and the model then applies the final norm again. Steered logits differ from clean logits even when delta=0. The L11 steering result ('~78–82% of early cells pushed toward maturity', presented as the project's 'first affirmative positive') reflects the double normalisation, not the SAE feature.
findings.evidence: |Δlogit| at L11 is 1.0861 (α=2) vs 1.0747 (α=5), the largest of any layer and insensitive to a 4× change in delta. frac_mat is 0.79 at both α values. setup/maxtoki_adapter.py:269-278 returns out.hidden_states unchanged (post-norm last element).
findings.recommended_action: For the final tap, either train the SAE on the pre-norm residual (hook the output of layers[10]) or steer post-norm and feed the result straight into lm_head without re-normalising. Add a delta=0 identity check and re-run Exp 3 at all layers after fixing F02.

findings.pipeline: sae-atlas-217M (feeds circuit-tracing source selection, coherence, and the exhaustive annotated/unannotated split)
findings.description: Feature annotation runs 4,928 features × 2,369 terms (about 11.7M hypergeometric tests per layer). Only tests with x≥2 and p<0.1 are kept, and BH is applied to that pre-selected subset only, which makes the correction far too lenient. The headline annotation rates (80.7% / 67.8% / 61.7%) and the U-shaped 12-layer profile collapse under a valid correction. So do the claims that 'MaxToki's features are more biologically interpretable than Geneformer (52.4%)' and 'excellent biological annotation (68–81%)'. Downstream uses are contaminated too: Stage-2 source selection by annotation score, circuit 'biological coherence', and the Stage-3 annotated/unannotated split.
findings.evidence: I recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv (median p_raw of the reported 'significant' enrichments is about 0.0067). With per-feature BH over 2,369 terms, annotated features are L0 104/2,498 (4.2%), L5 84/4,928 (1.7%), L11 55/4,924 (1.1%). With global BH over all tests: L0 29 (1.2%), L5 5 (0.1%), L11 0. Log: 'testing 4928 features × 2369 terms'.
findings.recommended_action: Apply BH (or Bonferroni) over all feature×term tests, or at least per feature over all terms, without p-value pre-filtering. Add a random-dictionary and shuffled-gene baseline for the annotation rate. Recompute all annotation-dependent downstream analyses and retract the cross-model interpretability comparison.

findings.description: Causal feature patching takes hidden_states[PROBE_LAYER+1] (= hidden[6]) and encodes it with the L5 SAE, which was trained on hidden[5] (phase0_extract_positions.py:40-42), so the SAE sees out-of-distribution input. It then injects the full SAE reconstruction decode(z with feature zeroed) instead of h + delta. Every patch therefore also injects the SAE's reconstruction error (at least 11% unexplained variance even in-distribution), which is the same for every feature. The resulting near-1 specificity is expected by construction, so the 'genuine non-replication' ('MaxToki features are NOT causally specific, 1.01× vs 2.36×') cannot stand.
findings.evidence: phase6/summary.json: median specificity 1.0149, mean_target_delta 1.414 vs mean_other_delta 1.395 (both large and almost equal, as expected from a feature-independent perturbation). Code at remaining_phases.py:182: `h5_patched = sae.decode(h_enc, mu)`. The source-feature count is also stated as 50 in one place and 30 in another (FINAL_SUMMARY lines 150 vs 185).
findings.recommended_action: Use the SAE of the same layer as the tapped state. Patch with h + (decode(z_abl) − decode(z)). Include a 'no-op reconstruction' control and random-feature controls, then re-run Phase 6.

findings.description: The headline 'TF specificity 0% vs paper's 6.2% — even more extreme' has no valid support, for three reasons. (1) The proxy test (Phase 8) compares SAE activations at a gene's own token positions with random other positions. That is a token-identity test, so 100% 'detection' is guaranteed and is not a perturbation response. (2) The 'true CRISPRi' test (8t) and multi-tissue test (9) encode perturbed cells from hidden[PROBE_LAYER+1] but compare them with control activations from phase0 layer_05 (hidden[5]): a layer mismatch. (3) 8t detects only 4/100 targets and 3/48 TFs, so specificity was effectively assessable for 3 TFs, not 48. The scorecard still counts 'perturbation detection 100% ✅' after the true test gave 4%.
findings.evidence: phase8_true/perturbation_response.csv: detected = CDC5L, GATA1, MED1 (TFs) and AQR. TFs detected 3 of 48. Fisher exact: 0/48 vs 3/48 p=0.24; 0/24 vs 3/48 p=0.55; 0/3 vs 3/48 p=1.0. Detection uses Mann-Whitney over pooled token positions (not cells) across 4,928 features with no multiplicity correction (p<0.05 & effect>0.5). Code: remaining_phases.py:390 (ctrl from layer_05) vs 418 (hidden[PROBE_LAYER+1]).
findings.recommended_action: Compare perturbed and control cells at the same layer tap and through the matching SAE. Use cell-level (pseudobulk) tests with FDR control. Report the number of TFs with detectable responses as the denominator and add a positive-control perturbation. Downgrade the verdict to 'untestable at current power' and drop 'more extreme than Geneformer'.

findings.description: The lineage-specific TwoNN intrinsic dimension, which underlies 'B-cell compression ρ=−0.867 ✅ replicated', 'T-cell compression ρ=−0.895 ❌ (MaxToki compresses both)' and the interpretation 'MaxToki's geometry encodes time rather than lineage identity', is computed on 6 B-cell and 9 T-cell marker genes. TwoNN on 6–9 points is not a meaningful estimate. There is no comparison with random gene sets of the same size, even though global TwoNN falls from 102 to 6.7 across depth, so any subset would show a decline.
findings.evidence: lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv: n_markers B cell 6, T cell 9, Myeloid 1 (NaN). B-cell values jump 101→34→34→62→34 (non-monotonic noise). phase1/per_layer_metrics.csv global TwoNN goes 102.0→6.7.
findings.recommended_action: Withdraw both lineage-compression verdicts and the 'time not lineage' interpretation, or recompute with ≥50 genes per lineage (marker-module expansion). Use a null of random gene sets of matched size and expression, and compare each lineage's depth slope with the null distribution of slopes.

findings.description: The cross-model 'Layer-1' claims rest on CCA (10 components on PCA-30, n≈350–382 genes) and orthogonal-Procrustes top-1 retrieval, both fit and scored in-sample. The permutation null re-uses the rotation fitted on the true pairing and only shuffles labels afterwards, so it is not a valid null. In-sample fitting on data this size gives sizeable values even for unrelated data. The scGPT result ('CCA r≈0.40 … alignment much weaker; top-1 5–8%, z=20–30') sits exactly at the random-data floor, so it shows no alignment rather than weak alignment. The Geneformer CCA 0.78 'within ±0.05 of paper 0.80' and top-1 z≈150–180 are inflated relative to a proper floor. Only static input embeddings are compared, although the docstring promises a per-layer analysis. The 'independent pre-training' premise (shared tokenizer and medians) was not checked.
findings.evidence: My simulation with independent Gaussian 380×1232 and 380×512 matrices, PCA-30 and the same CCA(k=10) and Procrustes code gives CCA mean r 0.399–0.433, top r 0.485–0.543, and in-sample top-1 3.9–7.6%. Reported scGPT values: CCA mean 0.401/0.438/0.406, top 0.476/0.547/0.506, top-1 5.0/6.6/7.6%, with pairwise Pearson −0.005 to −0.019. Code comment admits 'rotation R was fit on the unpermuted pair'.
findings.recommended_action: Use held-out-gene CCA and Procrustes (fit on 80% of genes, score on 20%) with a null that refits after permutation. Report the random-data floor next to each value, restate the scGPT result as 'no alignment above chance', and add per-layer comparisons. Treat pairwise Pearson with its valid null as the primary metric.

findings.description: The 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel)' cross-tissue invariance averages 12 layer states. Layer 0 (the static token embedding) is identical across tissues by construction (Pearson 1.000, top-1 1.000) and is included in the mean, and the only null is a gene-label shuffle. The data actually show cross-tissue similarity declining with depth: top-1 retrieval falls from 1.0 to 0.25–0.30 at L11, and Pearson to 0.45–0.69. That contradicts the stated interpretation that the 'trained transformer doesn't appear to introduce tissue-specific divergence'. Shared-gene counts are small (75, 77, 168).
findings.evidence: cross_domain_alignment.csv, layer 0 Pearson for all pairs: 1.0000. lung_vs_external_lung top-1 by layer: 1.0 at L0–L5, 0.97 at L6, 0.70, 0.49, 0.42, 0.35, then 0.25 at L11. immune_vs_external_lung Pearson at L10 is 0.448. The 'top-1 median 93–99%' quoted in the summary is driven by early layers.
findings.recommended_action: Use layer-0 (static) similarity as the floor and report each layer as a change from it. Drop L0 from the means. Restate the finding as 'context-dependent divergence grows with depth', and add an expression-matched null.

findings.description: 'H-cross' was promoted from the automated INCONCLUSIVE to 'NOVEL POSITIVE' by manual review after the fact. The 'null' in the code is a hard-coded constant (delta_vs_null_p95 = mean_off_diag − 0.3); no permutation or shuffled-layer null exists. Representations in adjacent layers of a residual stream are trivially correlated, and the feature is non-zero only for TRRUST pairs. A cross-layer Pearson of 0.60–0.68 also means substantial change, not 'essentially fixed'. The interpretation that 'the residual stream does not reorganise gene similarities' contradicts the project's own Phase 15 result (similarity declines with depth) and spectral Phase 1 (effective rank 561→94).
findings.evidence: report.json decision INCONCLUSIVE, 'mean Δ_vs_null=0.345' = mean Pearson − 0.3. Per-layer AUROC 0.377–0.533, mostly below chance.
findings.recommended_action: Restore the pre-registered INCONCLUSIVE verdict, or build a real null (for example, cross-layer correlation of the same feature computed on a random-init model or on label-permuted TRRUST pairs) and re-test. Remove the 'novel positive' from README and EXTENDED_FINDINGS.

findings.description: The TwoNN estimator permutes the empirical CDF (`F = F[np.argsort(mu)]`) and then pairs it with sorted μ, which scrambles the CDF–μ relationship. The slope becomes noise, and the reported intrinsic dimensions are impossible values (negative). 'dim_compression_l0_to_l_last' (for example −22.3) is meaningless. The H-depth narrative ('compression-then-decompression') is supported only by unnormalised H1 totals. For immune, H1 at L11 (231) exceeds the L5 'peak' (210), so 'partial recovery' is also wrong.
findings.evidence: external_lung twonn: 2.01, 0.105, −0.133, −0.342, …; immune: −0.678, 1.77, … I checked on synthetic data: true dimension 2/5/10 gives 0.18/−0.07/0.04 with the buggy code vs 1.87/4.58/8.83 with the fix.
findings.recommended_action: Remove line 107 (or use the spectral run's correct _twonn), re-run phase 16 depth, and correct the H-depth row.

findings.description: (a) H-lineage z-scores come from discrete, zero-heavy nulls with only 3–8 markers in the pool. The ext-lung B-cell 'significant' lineage has observed purity equal to the null p95 (0.0556), so the '4/4 lineages sig' claim does not hold empirically. The null is random gene sets; it does not control for co-expression or expression level, although lineage markers are co-expressed. (b) H-hub, called the 'strongest new result', is a Spearman ρ of 0.115–0.118 (z≈2.3) across 3 uncorrected tests. The null permutes TF degree across all genes without controlling for expression or study bias, and the immune pool is 343 TFs out of 350 genes. The conclusion 'MaxToki does place regulatory hubs at central positions' goes too far. (c) H23 'validates the spec implementation' rests on AUROC computed over 52–123 edges with no CI.
findings.evidence: h_lineage: external_lung B_cell obs 0.0556, null_p95 0.0556, z 3.05, n_markers 3. h_hub: lung ρ 0.060 (z 1.31), immune 0.118 (z 2.34, n_tfs 343), ext-lung 0.115 (z 2.36). h23: n_pair_edges 62/123/52.
findings.recommended_action: Use empirical p-values (obs > null p95/p99) with expression- and co-expression-matched gene-set nulls and correct across lineages and domains. Add degree- and expression-stratified permutation for H-hub, and bootstrap CIs for H23. Downgrade the wording to 'weak/exploratory'.

findings.description: The final summary contradicts the run's own outputs in several places. (1) k562_1b C3 is shown as FAIL, but phase12_verdict_k562_1b.json and run_report_k562_1b.md give PASS (fraction retained 0.784). (2) 'No run's attention beats any of the three trivial baselines' is false for RPE1: attention 0.603 beats mean expression (0.582, p_BH 7e-8) and 1−dropout (0.500, p_BH 4e-36). (3) 'Residualized AUROC collapses to chance after OLS cross-fit in every run' is false for 1B (0.555→0.543) and Adamson (0.5195→0.5202). (4) The C3 metric is degenerate when the baseline AUROC is below 0.5: the denominator is clipped to 1e-6, giving −13,421 for K562-217M, so that FAIL reflects the formula rather than the data. The overall FAIL verdict survives (C1 and C2 fail everywhere), but the per-run table and narrative are wrong.
findings.evidence: phase3_k562_1b/residualization_results.csv attention OLS: 0.5554→0.5434, frac 0.7839. phase3/residualization_results.csv: frac −13421.3 (baseline 0.4829). Formula: (auc−0.5)/max(baseline−0.5,1e-6).
findings.recommended_action: Correct the table and narrative. Define C3 as N/A when the baseline is ≤0.5 plus the label-shuffle p95, and state that RPE1 attention beats two trivial baselines but not gene variance.

findings.category: P6 no positive control / layer selection
findings.description: The primary layer L8 was chosen by depth-ratio analogy, and at L8 attention has no TRRUST signal (AUROC 0.483 on 2,000 cells; 0.440 at the ablation baseline). The C3 residualization, curveball null and C4 head ablation are all evaluated at L8, so there is no above-chance signal to residualize or ablate and the tests are uninformative. The same ablation log shows a TRRUST AUROC of 0.684 at L1. That layer was never tested against the curveball null, residualization or ablation, and the summary does not report it. 'Regulatory heads are not a causal bottleneck' rests on three random-5 draws at a below-chance layer with 300 cells and no CI.
findings.evidence: phase4.log: 'TRRUST AUROC @primary L8 = 0.4399 best layer L1 = 0.6840'. top5 heads are at layers 1, 2 and 4. At the best layer, top5 ablation raises AUROC (+0.013). Per-pert AUROC profile peaks at L1 (0.553).
findings.recommended_action: Repeat Phase 3 (curveball, residualization) and Phase 4 at L1/L2, where signal exists, or pre-specify the layer on an independent dataset. Add more random-ablation draws with CIs and qualify C4 as uninformative at L8.

findings.description: Edges are edge[A,B] = mean over cells of attn[query=A, key=B] in a causal decoder whose input tokens are sorted by normalized expression rank. attn[A,B] can only be non-zero when B ranks above A in that cell, so the per-perturbation attention score is mechanically coupled to the target's relative expression rank, and zeros are averaged in when B ranks lower. That alone makes gene-level expression baselines dominate. The replication of 'attention captures co-expression, not regulation', and the claim that the shallow-layer profile is 'specific to bidirectional BERT-style encoders', cannot be separated from this masking artefact. The README acknowledges the directed form but not the rank confound. No symmetrized or key-side edge and no rank-matched control was run.
findings.evidence: phase0_extract.py: attn_sum[li,:,A,B] += sub (query rows, key cols); pair_counts denominators include cells where the edge is masked. k562 gene_mean_expr baseline 0.560 vs attention 0.512; Adamson mean_expr 0.712 vs 0.508.
findings.recommended_action: Repeat Phase 1–3 with symmetrized edges (0.5·(attn[A→B]+attn[B→A])), with per-cell rank-conditioned normalization (only pairs where both orders occur), and with a rank-matched null. Remove the BERT-specificity claim.

findings.description: '10 co-activation modules per layer at 99.9–100% coverage — matches [paper's 6–12, 96–99.5%] precisely' is an artefact of the fallback code. leidenalg was not installed, so the script used SpectralClustering(n_clusters=10), which always returns 10 clusters and assigns every alive feature. Module count and coverage are not measured properties of MaxToki.
findings.evidence: phases2_to_8.log: 'leidenalg not installed — skipping Leiden, using k-means instead'; 'modules: 10 coverage: 0.507/1.000/0.999'; spectral-embedding warning 'Graph is not fully connected'.
findings.recommended_action: Install leidenalg (or use igraph/networkx community detection) with modularity-chosen k and a null (shuffled co-activation), then re-run Phase 5. Remove the ✅ until then.

findings.category: P1 null absent / trivially satisfied criterion
findings.description: '99.9–100% of features invisible to SVD — massive superposition confirmed' uses the criterion that a decoder direction counts as 'SVD-aligned' only if |cos| > 0.7 with one of the top-50 singular vectors in 1,232-d space. Almost any direction fails this test: a random unit vector's expected maximum |cos| with 50 orthonormal vectors is about 0.1. So ~100% 'novel' is expected for any dictionary, including a random one, and says nothing about superposition.
findings.evidence: Code: `if max_cos > 0.7` with `cos_vals = np.abs(top50_Vt @ dec_norm)`. Novel 4928/4923/4927. Rough estimate: sqrt(2·ln(100)/1232) ≈ 0.12.
findings.recommended_action: Add a random-decoder baseline and a projection-energy metric (fraction of each decoder norm inside the top-k SV subspace), and drop 'massive superposition confirmed'.

findings.description: The two SAE summaries contradict each other and the outputs. (1) The 3-layer scorecard marks 'features overwhelmingly layer-specific — no persistent scaffold ✅ replicates' (L0→L5 2.5%). The 12-layer summary of the same SAEs reports 'dramatically higher cross-layer persistence than Geneformer (21.5% peak)… differs from paper'. The ✅ was never revised. (2) The 3-layer text calls annotation 'declining with depth', the 12-layer text calls it 'U-shaped', and both rest on inflated rates (F04). (3) Alive L5 is 4,903 (Phase 1) vs 4,928 (Phase 2 and 12-layer). (4) The Phase-6 feature count is 50 vs 30. (5) The cross-reference states 'unannotated features carry a disproportionate share of downstream causal influence' right after reporting top-20 hubs at 55% annotated vs a 50% design base with Fisher n.s., so the data do not support it.
findings.evidence: phase4 csv: 0→5 persistence 0.0254, 5→11 0.0053. 12-layer: L6→L7 21.5%, L0→L8 13.3%. Exhaustive overall_annotation_rate 0.5 by design (500+500).
findings.recommended_action: Reconcile into a single summary, mark persistence as a non-replication, fix the counts, and delete the 'disproportionate share' sentence.

findings.description: The cell-type enrichment ('4,724/4,928 features (95.9%) enriched for ≥1 of 32 cell types') runs Fisher's exact tests over ~2M token positions from 1,000 TS-immune cells, treating positions as independent even though every position in a cell shares that cell's label. With this many units almost any activation difference becomes 'significant'. The activations are also hidden[PROBE_LAYER+1] encoded with the L5 SAE (trained on hidden[5] of K562 cells), which is a layer and domain mismatch. The comparison with the paper's 99.0% is not meaningful.
findings.evidence: Lines 606, 640-651: per-position 2×2 tables, Bonferroni only across cell types (not features); `ts_cell_types_per_pos.extend([cell_types_ts[ci]] * h_l5.shape[0])`.
findings.recommended_action: Aggregate to cell level (fraction of active positions per cell), test with cell as the unit (Mann-Whitney or logistic regression with donor random effects), apply FDR across features × cell types, and use the matching layer.

findings.category: P1 no chance anchor / inconsistent numbers / P9
findings.description: 'Biological coherence 36.1% (vs paper 53%)', the fraction of edges whose source and target features share an ontology term, has no chance baseline (random feature pairs with the same annotation sizes). It also depends on the inflated annotations from F04. 'Match TRRUST 361 (0.01%)' has no base-rate anchor. The headline gives density as '22× denser' while the body says 41×; 2,144,011/52,116 is 41.1×. The 'Architectural insight' paragraph ('dependency-dominated', 'deeply entangled', 'less feature redundancy than Geneformer's BERT') is cross-study speculation built on the buggy ablations (F02).
findings.evidence: phase9_knowledge.json: n_annotated_both 1,416,229, n_shared 511,466, coherence 0.3611. No null anywhere in remaining_phases.py (grep finds no shuffle or permutation for coherence).
findings.recommended_action: After fixing F02 and F04, compute coherence and TRRUST-match against a feature-pair permutation null that preserves annotation set sizes. Fix 22×→41× and remove the architectural speculation.

findings.description: 'Annotation bias replicates … selective tracing (Stage 2) systematically missed the most important hubs' is not supported. Every traced feature has ~5,000 edges (top-20 between 4,990 and 5,400), so hub rank is essentially noise. Top-20 are 55% annotated vs a 50% design base (Fisher n.s.), and the annotated/unannotated labels come from the inflated annotation (F04). 'Per-feature density is consistent: ~5K edges/feature in both experiments' is false: Stage 2 averages 17,867 edges per feature (39,653 at L0). FTL is described as a 'terminal erythroid marker' in immune cells; it is a ubiquitous ferritin gene, highest in macrophages. Switch features used a much lower bar (|ρ|>0.3 vs PC1 pseudotime), yielding 5,767 vs the paper's 14.
findings.evidence: exhaustive_summary.json top-20 edges 5400…4990; circuit_summary.json edges_per_feature 39653.1/20668.2/8514.3/2631.
findings.recommended_action: Restate as 'no hub/annotation relationship detectable; circuit uniformly dense (pending the F02 fix)', correct the density comparison, and fix the FTL annotation.

findings.category: P2 trivial baseline / P5 label-derived rulers
findings.description: The headline ('MaxToki-217M internally encodes a hematopoietic developmental manifold … first affirmative deployable result') is not qualified by the run's own trivial-baseline comparison. PCA-10 on expression matches or beats the extracted manifold on branch, stage and pseudotime with no significant difference, and the frozen average-pooled MaxToki embedding also matches it. 'Extracted beats raw' is shown only against degenerate raw_log1p (branch 0.142). The same anchors and labels give a branch-holdout pass to PCA. The sweep positives (H95 effector modality, H103 B-cell maturation, H38 categories) are rulers derived from cell-type labels on cell-type-centroid anchors, which any representation that separates cell types would satisfy. The spec explicitly requires 'ground truth independent of co-expression'.
findings.evidence: phase12 LITE: branch pca10 0.844 vs extracted_z10 0.756 vs avgpool 0.792; stage 0.595/0.551/0.665; pseudotime 0.509/0.262/0.537. Pairwise vs PCA-10 all n.s. (BH q≥0.26). n_test only 3–32 per split, 9 splits.
findings.recommended_action: Put the PCA/expression baseline into the headline table and restate the claim as 'recoverable from MaxToki at parity with expression PCA'. Run all quality gates on PCA-10 and avg-pool features with the same LET head, and drop 'first affirmative deployable result' unless the extraction beats them.

findings.description: The frozen gate specification, which states 'never loosen; violation invalidates the run', was not followed. (1) The fifth gate (blocked permutation p ≤ 0.001, ≥2,000 permutations blocked by donor and tissue), required before Phase 5, was never computed for any branch; no script implements it. (2) For H95 and H103, a '3-gate fallback' introduced after the fact drops the category or branch-holdout gate. That is exactly the gate that separated H65 from its within-branch null, whose random and donor holdouts also pass (0.799/0.707). (3) The pre-registered expected negative-control signature ('trustworthiness < 0.80 AND clade correlation < 0.20') was not met (trust 0.800), yet the summary reports the control 'FAILS as required'. The lung control uses random labels, so its failure only shows the method rejects random labels.
findings.evidence: quality_gates_spec.json gates include blocked_permutation_p_max 0.001 and n_permutations_min 2000; quality_gates_let_anchor.json reports only four gates. Null H65 random 0.7986, donor 0.7071. lung_nonhema trust 0.800.
findings.recommended_action: Implement and report the blocked permutation gate for all positives. Re-adjudicate H95 and H103 under the full gate set with a within-category null. Record the negative-control deviation honestly and add a stronger control (biologically structured but non-hematopoietic ruler).

findings.description: The 'PARTIALLY_ORTHOGONAL … first quantitative support for the multi-axis-hub claim' reading is not supported. The cross-head correlation (0.642) being below the ruler overlap (0.814) is what imperfect self-fits alone produce: 0.814×0.986×0.825 ≈ 0.662. The 'null check' cannot show that H95 is 'genuinely encoded': the scrambled-ruler head fits its meaningless target exactly as well as the real head (self-fit 0.82479 vs 0.82479), so in-sample self-fit is non-discriminative. The low cross-head ρ for the null (0.022) follows from the scrambling, not from the model.
findings.evidence: phase17 json: ruler_overlap 0.8144, self_fit_h65 0.9861, self_fit_h95 0.8248, head_overlap 0.6418, null_self_fit 0.8248, null_trust 0.666.
findings.recommended_action: Compare cross-head overlap against the attenuation-expected value using held-out anchors. Use out-of-sample self-fits, and build a null by refitting the H95 head on permuted features. Retract the 'multi-axis hub' quantitative support claim.

findings.category: P5 double dipping / P8 single seed
findings.description: L10H6 was chosen as the best of 88 heads by composite score (trust + random + branch) on the internal panel. Phase 10 then evaluates 'compact_top1' on the same internal panel and concludes it 'beats full-drift on every metric'. That is winner's-curse selection. The compaction variants are single-seed and non-monotonic (branch: rank8 0.352, rank16 0.216, rank32 0.420, rank64 0.514), so 'all seven variants pass … 2,400× compression' has no stability estimate. The 'late-layer dominance' divergence from scGPT is likewise selected on the internal panel.
findings.evidence: phase10 loads centroids_internal.npy and d_target_internal.npy; phase9 ranks on the same.
findings.recommended_action: Select the head on the internal panel and report compaction metrics on the external or zero-shot panels only. Run ≥3 seeds per variant with mean ± SD, and remove 'beats full-drift'.

findings.description:
The G1 result is not interpretable as an age signal test.
- **Degenerate age bins:** quantile bins on cell-level ages give (22,56], (56,60], (60,74]. The middle bin is 4 donors aged 59–60, and the old bin has 3 donors, with 17 donors in total.
- **Both representations score below chance:** MaxToki 0.276 and HVG-PCA 0.172 vs 1/3. This indicates donor–age confounding under GroupShuffleSplit, not 'no age signal'.
- **Invalid inference:** 'MaxToki L5 does beat the trivial HVG-PCA-50 baseline … encoding something beyond raw expression PCA' compares two below-chance scores and is not valid.
- **Null not auditable:** the null (cell-level vs donor-level permutation) and the evaluation helpers are imported from an external repo not in the project.
- **False layer claim:** 'L5 is the canonical tap used by every other MaxToki pipeline' is false. Attention-GRN uses L8 as primary, topology and spectral use all 12 states, and manifold uses pooled drift with L10H6.
findings.evidence: sampled_obs donor ages: TSP1/14/17/25 = 59/59/60/60 → (56,60]; TSP2/6/7 = 61/67/69 → (60,74]. probe_aggregate: 0.2755 ± 0.035 vs 0.1722 ± 0.037; null mean 0.332 ± 0.010. UPSTREAM_SCRIPTS path outside the project.
findings.recommended_action: Use donor-level age (regression or clinically meaningful bins), leave-donor-out CV with class-presence checks, and a donor-level label permutation. Report n_donors as the inference unit, remove the 'beats PCA' inference, and vendor the helper code.

findings.description: The paper's Phase 8 compares models trained with different fine-tuning seeds. This run compares three cell samples through one fixed checkpoint, a different quantity. It then concludes 'MaxToki representations are vastly more stable than scGPT' and scores two ❌ 'non-replications'. L0 CKA = 1.000 is trivial (static, context-independent embedding). The run's own summary.json gives the opposite verdict ('qualitatively reproduces the paper's CKA pattern').
findings.evidence: summary.json interpretation 'across-cell-sample stability (no fine-tuning seeds available)'; verdict text 'qualitatively reproduces the paper's CKA pattern'; FINAL_SUMMARY: 'does not replicate … ❌ stability much higher'.
findings.recommended_action: Mark Phase 8 as 'not testable (no seed replicates)', report cell-sample CKA only as a sampling-stability check, and remove the cross-model stability comparison and its ❌ entries.

findings.description: 'Depth-wise dimensionality compression is learned, not architectural' rests only on a feature-shuffle null. Independently permuting each column destroys all inter-dimension correlation, so effective rank (ER) near the maximum is guaranteed for any correlated matrix. No random-init or untrained model, which is what separates learned from architectural, was run. 'All change monotonically with depth' is false for ER: L1 332→L2 338, and L6 169→L7 174→L8 202→L9 202. The final drop (L10 172 → L11 94; SV1 fraction 0.105→0.173) coincides with HF hidden_states[-1] being post-final-RMSNorm, so the last point is partly a normalisation effect.
findings.evidence: per_layer_metrics.csv ER: 560.8, 332.6, 338.1, 297.6, 231.7, 212.1, 169.4, 174.4, 201.7, 201.9, 172.1, 93.6. Shuffle null computed only at the final layer.
findings.recommended_action: Add a random-init MaxToki (same architecture) extraction as the architectural null. Use pre-norm final residuals, report per-layer nulls, and restate 'monotonic' as 'overall decreasing (ρ=−0.895)'.

findings.category: P2/P3 claim relies on static layer; misreported numbers
findings.description: 'Cell-type marker clustering is strong … replicated (0.779 vs paper 0.851)' uses layer 0, the static, context-independent token embedding. All contextual layers are 0.54–0.66. The L2-norm control is misreported. '0.580' is the mean over all 12 layers of the post-regression AUROC, compared against the L0 raw 0.779; at L0 the residual is 0.648. '~25% of signal is magnitude-driven' uses the wrong denominator: 53% of the above-chance L0 signal is removed, and 71% by the summary's own mean-vs-L0 comparison. Several layers fall to chance after regression (L4 0.473, L11 0.522).
findings.recommended_action: Report clustering per layer, state that it is a property of the static embedding, compare like with like (L0 raw vs L0 residual), and correct the magnitude fraction.

findings.description:
Multiple numeric claims disagree with the outputs or with each other.
- **TF-vs-target depth claim:** 'SV2-SV7 jumps to 0.62 at L11 after being ~0.53 at L0' underpins 'peak at different depth' and 'the depth-regime hypothesis is scGPT-specific'. In fact L0 = 0.596 (perm p=0.0099, significant), L6 0.610, L11 0.620, so the profile is flat with a dip, not a late peak. Only 100 permutations were run and the null mean is 0.54, not 0.5.
- **SV3 PPI significant layers:** reported as '3/12' in one place and '10/12' in another. With BH the count is 4 layers (L7, L9, L10, L11); 10/12 holds only uncorrected.
- **BATF distance:** validation row 16 calls BATF dist-to-PAX5 ρ=+0.979 'distance metrics replicate strongly', but a positive ρ means divergence, contradicting Key finding #10.
- **GC–plasma angle:** reported as 72°→~52°; the L11 value is 46.4°.
- **Score tally:** '11 ✅/5 ⚠️/13 ❌' does not match the table, which has 10/5/14.
- **Stale scope note:** the 'Phases skipped: 8, 9a, 9b, 9c' line contradicts the later sections reporting those phases as completed.
findings.recommended_action: Correct these numbers and verdicts, and rerun the TF-vs-target probe with ≥1,000 permutations and BH across layers. Regenerate the summary tables directly from the CSVs.

findings.description: Every load-bearing negative lacks evidence that the implementation can detect a true signal. This covers H123, persistent homology and the strict max-null (0–1/12 layers), the attention-GRN null (curveball z≈0), SAE TF specificity 0%, circuit CRISPRi, and the longevity G1 fail. No synthetic graph or embedding with planted signed-motif or regulatory structure, no planted-edge attention test, and no real-data positive control (for example GATA1/TAL1 ChIP targets in K562) exists anywhere in the project. No random-init model was used to separate learned from architectural effects. Given the implementation bugs found (F01–F06, F11), the lack of positive controls is especially consequential.
findings.evidence: grep across all scripts for 'synthetic|planted|positive.control|random.init|untrained|from_config' returns only an unrelated lung-panel script.
findings.recommended_action: Add a short positive-control phase per pipeline: a planted-structure synthetic embedding through the same H123/PH/null harness, planted attention edges, and a known-effect SAE feature injection. Add a random-init MaxToki extraction. Report detection power before keeping any negative verdict.

findings.description:
Several gaps in generalisation and stability remain:
- **Single cell line:** all SAE, circuit and exhaustive results come from K562 control cells (an immortalized line), a single SAE training seed, and a single condition (K562/K562).
- **Single dataset:** spectral geometry uses one dataset (TS immune, 2,000 cells).
- **Fixed hyperparameters:** topology fixes PCA-20 and kNN k=12 with no sweep.
- **Single-seed manifold results:** the manifold compaction and sweeps are single-seed.
- **No CIs on headline numbers:** none are bootstrapped or reported with CIs. Examples: attention-GRN ΔAUROC +0.0007 vs threshold 0.005 (no DeLong or bootstrap), H123 layer counts, H91 AUCs, the 1B-vs-217M scale comparison (1B used N=200 vs 2,000 cells, so it is confounded), and the C4 ablation with 3 random draws.
findings.evidence: Configs: sae-atlas Scope '500 K562 control cells'; circuit_summary n_cells 200; phase0_k562_1b run with N_ctrl 200 vs 2000; topology scripts PCA_DIM/KNN constants.
findings.recommended_action: For headline claims, add bootstrap CIs (resampling TFs, perturbations or donors), ≥3 seeds for SAE training and LET heads, and 3-point sweeps of PCA dim and k. Match N when comparing model sizes, and add one non-K562 condition for the SAE and circuit stages.

findings.description:
The summaries use causal and mechanistic language the evidence does not support:
- 'causal edges'
- 'dependency-dominated architecture … deeply entangled'
- 'single-cell foundation models … have not internalised causal regulatory wiring'
- 'MaxToki is a trajectory generative model … the geometric invariants it preserves are the ones useful for trajectory generation'
- 'MaxToki encodes a tissue-invariant gene geometry'
- 'MaxToki does place regulatory hubs at central positions'
- 'multi-axis biological hub'
- 'first affirmative deployable result'
- 'SCFMs can encode a latent progenitor→mature axis amplifiable via activation addition'

The underlying experiments are correlational (CCA, kNN, probes) or affected by implementation bugs (F01–F06). Cross-pipeline narratives ('two stories are not contradictory') chain these claims together.
findings.evidence: See cited lines. For example, the attention-GRN cross-reference presents the exhaustive steering result (F02/F03) as the 'first affirmative positive mechanistic-interpretability finding'.
findings.recommended_action: Do a verb-swap pass ('encodes' → 'is consistent with', 'causal circuit' → 'model-internal ablation graph') and state the claim level (decoding / agreement / intervention-consistent / mechanism) for each claim. Remove cross-pipeline syntheses that depend on F01–F06 until those are re-run.

findings.description: Phase 0b reports 'At primary L8, VW per-pert AUROC = 0.513 vs raw attention 0.532'; the outputs show 0.493 vs 0.512 (Δ −0.019, p=0.012 is correct). The README still lists 0b and 5–11 as skipped, although the final summary reports 0b and CSSI.

- **'Eucl ≈ Geo (≈0)':** the computed means are −0.035 for both.

- **Phase-0 block:** omits the immune domain.

findings.description: The immune domain re-uses spectral-geometry embeddings (2,000 cells, gene pool selected with TRRUST priority: 343 of 350 pool genes are TRRUST TFs). Lung and ext-lung are fresh 1,500-cell extractions with a different pool rule, so cross-domain contrasts (immune 1/12 vs 0/12; H-hub immune; H124/H127 'ticks immune') are confounded. The pool was also selected with the same database used for evaluation (annotation circularity). The Phase-1 TF/target-disjoint splits are only used by Phase 9; Phases 6, 7+8 and 12 compute AUROC in-sample on the full pair table, so per-layer counts are compared with the paper's per-domain-split counts in a different unit.
findings.evidence: immune run_config: reused=true, source=spectral-geometry phase0. h_hub immune n_tfs_in_pool 343. grep: splits.json only read in phase9_stability_selection.py.
findings.recommended_action: Re-extract immune with the same pool rule and cell count as the other domains, evaluate H123/H141 on the TF-disjoint splits, and report counts in the paper's unit.

findings.description: 'STRING confidence gradient NOT replicated … MaxToki encodes PPI binarily, not with graded confidence' rests on a single two-point comparison of nested sets (pairs_900 ⊂ pairs_700; mean z 2.62 vs 2.46, Δ −0.16) with no uncertainty, whereas the paper uses 5 quintiles. The run's own autoloop (iter_0003) found a significant graded effect (layer-persistence vs 900-tier ρ=0.083, p=0.015; gene-shuffle z=6.93). That result is not mentioned in the FINAL_SUMMARY, and the autoloop's abort after two failed iterations is not reported either.
findings.evidence: confidence_gradient.json z_mean_700_SV2 2.625, z_mean_900_SV2 2.464. autoloop_master_log: 'ABORT after 2 consecutive failures'.
findings.recommended_action: Use disjoint confidence bins (700–900 vs ≥900, or quintiles) with bootstrap CIs, and report the autoloop result and abort status.

findings.description:
The project cannot be reproduced as it stands:
- **External absolute paths:** ~20 scripts hard-code paths outside the project (<DATA_ROOT>/…, ~/.cache/huggingface Geneformer snapshot, biomi_automation/repos/longevity-mechinterp), and core longevity evaluation code lives only in that external repo.
- **No environment lock:** the install line pins 'transformers>=4.44', yet forward-hook return semantics (tuple vs tensor) differ across versions. circuit_trace.py and experiment1_exhaustive.py return bare tensors while experiment2/3 handle tuples, and the saved config says 4.44.2.
- **Unvalidated inputs:** Geneformer gc104M gene medians are used in place of MaxToki's own, with no check that tokenized inputs are in-distribution (no next-token accuracy or perplexity check; the smoke test only runs a forward pass).
- **Missing run documents:** three run folders have no README or FINAL_SUMMARY (they exist only under summaries/).
- **Missing commits:** pinned-commit repos (repos/*/PINNED_COMMIT.txt) are absent.
- **No per-phase wall time:** it is missing for several runs.
findings.evidence: grep finds 20+ scripts referencing <LOCAL_VOLUME>/MacBook/biomechinterp. setup/MaxToki-217M-HF/config.json transformers_version 4.44.2. README: 'numerical values should be within noise' (unverified).
findings.recommended_action: Add a lockfile (pip freeze or environment.yml), vendor the helper code, and parameterize paths. Add a tokenization sanity check (next-token top-k accuracy on held-out cells), restore run-level README and FINAL_SUMMARY files, and record per-phase runtime.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. phases2_to_8.py:184-195 (and full_12layer_pipeline.py:246-251) keeps only tests with x>=2 and p<0.1, then runs BH on that pooled subset. The spec (01-sae-atlas.md:182) requires BH 'across all terms tested for that feature'. The largest p_raw among the reported 'significant' enrichments is about 0.04, so the step is effectively uncorrected. I recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv with per-feature BH over m=2369 terms: L0 104/2498 (4.2%), L5 84/4928 (1.7%), L11 55/4924 (1.1%). With global BH: 29, 5 and 0 features. Both match the finding exactly. The 80.7/67.8/61.7% rates, the 12-layer profile, and the 'more interpretable than Geneformer 52.4%' comparison all rest on this inflated annotation. So do the downstream annotated/unannotated selections.

Confirmed. phases2_to_8.log says 'leidenalg not installed — skipping Leiden'. The fallback is SpectralClustering(n_clusters=min(10,n_alive)), which forces exactly 10 clusters and labels every alive feature. The full_12layer_pipeline.py except-ImportError branch does the same, and every one of the 12 layers reports modules=10. The '10 modules, 99.9–100% coverage matches precisely' ✅ is set by the code, not measured. The 3-layer fallback also slices pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive] (the first n_alive indices) rather than the alive features, and spectral embedding warns that the graph is not fully connected.

Confirmed from phase12_anchor_benchmark_lite(.csv/_pairwise.csv). Mean branch accuracy: pca10 0.844, extracted_z10 0.756, avgpool 0.792. Pseudotime: 0.509, 0.262, 0.537. Every pairwise comparison against PCA/SVD/avgpool is n.s. (q≥0.26), and the only wins are against degenerate raw_log1p (branch 0.142). §11 of FINAL_SUMMARY does disclose this. However, the headline (lines 13-28) and the §10 synthesis ('first affirmative deployable result') are not qualified. The spec (§9 items 17-18 and line 600) requires showing value beyond simple baselines and rulers independent of co-expression. The quality gates were never run on PCA-10 or avg-pool features.

Confirmed. phase17 json: null_self_fit 0.8247876 equals self_fit_h95 0.8247876 to 7 decimals. The LET head therefore fits a scrambled ruler exactly as well as the real one, so in-sample self-fit is at the tie ceiling and does not discriminate. A cross-head ρ (0.642) below the ruler overlap (0.814) is what attenuation predicts (0.814×0.986×0.825≈0.662). The null's low overlap with the H65 head (0.022) follows from scrambling and does not show that H95 is 'genuinely encoded'. The PARTIALLY_ORTHOGONAL verdict and the 'quantitative support for the multi-axis hub' claim in §17.3 are not supported.

Data confirmed. Layer-0 Pearson and top-1 are 1.000 for all pairs. lung_vs_external_lung top-1 falls 1.0→0.97→0.70→0.49→0.42→0.35→0.25 from L6 to L11. immune_vs_ext Pearson is 0.448 at L10. The only null is a gene-label shuffle. The interpretation that the 'trained transformer doesn't appear to introduce tissue-specific divergence' contradicts the monotone divergence with depth. Cross-tissue similarity is largely inherited from the shared static embedding, so the 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel) tissue-invariant geometry' framing is overclaimed. One part of the finding is weak: dropping L0 lowers the mean Pearson only slightly (0.74–0.86 → 0.72–0.85), so the overclaim lies in the interpretation and the baseline rather than in the mean.

Confirmed. lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv uses n_markers 6 (B) and 9 (T), and the _twonn fit uses F<0.9, so only about 5 points enter the regression. Values such as 101→34→34→62→34 are noise. There is no matched random-gene-set null, even though global TwoNN falls 102→6.7, so any subset would appear to 'compress'. The B ✅ / T ❌ verdicts and the 'time rather than lineage identity' interpretation are not supported. Mitigation: the spec itself prescribes this test with n=7/12 markers, so the replication is like-for-like and the weakness is partly inherited. That is why I rate it major rather than critical.

Confirmed. The 3-layer scorecard marks persistence/layer-specificity ✅ by comparing L0→L5 (2.5%) with the paper's adjacent L0→L1. The crosslayer log for the same SAEs gives adjacent L0→L1 0.0%, L6→L7 21.5% and L0→L8 13.3%, and the 12-layer summary calls this 'differs from paper', so the ✅ verdict is wrong. The 3-layer text says 'declining' and the 12-layer text says 'U-shaped'. phase6.log has 50 features, while the cross-reference says 30. The 'disproportionate share of causal influence' sentence contradicts the exhaustive summary: top-20 55% annotated vs a 50% base, top-100 45%, Fisher n.s. The 4903 vs 4928 alive count is trivial: the eval set differs from all positions.

Each item verified. tf_vs_target_classifier.csv joint AUROC at L0 is 0.596 (perm p=0.0099), not '~0.53'. SV3 PPI: BH q<0.05 holds only at L7, L9, L10 (pairs_900) and L11 (pairs_700), i.e. 4 layers, while the summary reports '3/12' in one place and '10/12' in another. dist_BATF_to_PAX5 ρ=+0.979 means divergence (the paper reports −0.972), yet row 16 says 'distance metrics replicate strongly'. So the summary's '0.580 (down from 0.779)' compares a 12-layer mean with the L0 raw value, and '~25%' uses the raw AUROC rather than above-chance signal as denominator; like-for-like at L0 it is 47%. L4 (0.473) and L11 (0.522) fall to chance. A random dictionary would therefore also be about 100% 'novel', so this metric cannot show 'massive superposition'. Rated minor because the code reproduces the paper's own criterion (cos>0.7; paper 99.8% novel), so the replication number is like-for-like. The flaw is in the inherited interpretive claim, not in a computational error.
