verdicts.reason: Confirmed in phases2_to_8.py:182-196 and in full_12layer_pipeline.py:245-251. Rows are kept only if p<0.1, and BH is then run on that pooled subset across all features. The spec (01-sae-atlas.md:182) asks for per-feature BH over all terms tested. Log: 4928 features x 2369 terms (~11.7M tests at L5, so 'tens of millions' is a slight overstatement). Recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv: BH over all feature x term tests gives annotation rates of 1.2% (L0), 0.1% (L5) and 0% (L11). Per-feature BH with m=2369 gives 4.2%, 1.7% and 1.1%. Even if only 100 terms per feature are counted, rates are 20-36%. The largest significant p is ~0.04, and q≈1.5×p, so the procedure is effectively raw p<0.05. The 62-81% rates, the claim that MaxToki is 'more interpretable than Geneformer (52.4%)', and the depth-trend scorecard item are unsupported.

Confirmed. Line 242 sets `alive` from an array shape > 0, so it is always True and never used. Decoders are unit-normalised after every step (setup/topk_sae.py:7,38), so the `norm<1e-8` check never excludes dead features. svd_comparison.csv: L0 0 aligned + 4928 novel, although only 2498 are alive. cross_layer_tracking.csv: n_src_alive=4928 for L0. Restricted to alive features, L0→L5 persistence would be about 125/2498 ≈ 5%, not 2.5%. The 12-layer L0→Lx rates are also halved. With max|cos| against 50 orthonormal SVs in 1232-d at ~0.08-0.1 for a random direction, the 0.7 threshold makes '99.9% novel' nearly automatic. It is the paper's own metric, so it is fine as a procedural replication, but it cannot support 'massive superposition confirmed'.

Confirmed. The 3-layer summary says 'Features are overwhelmingly layer-specific — no persistent scaffold. Replicates' (scorecard ✅) using only L0→L5 and L5→L11. The 12-layer summary and crosslayer log show L6→L7 1059/4928 (21.5%), L8→L9 18.0% and L0→L8 13.3%, and call this 'dramatically higher than Geneformer'. Alive counts differ (Phase 1 L5 4903 / L11 4813 vs Phase 2 4928 / 4924). The 12-layer adjacent numbers in the summary also do not match the log (summary L0→L1 0.5%, L1→L2 3.3% vs log 0.000 and 0.002). The 'declining vs U-shaped' point is weaker, since the three common layers agree, but the persistence verdict contradiction is real and flips a scorecard item.

Confirmed against exhaustive_summary.json: top20_annotation_rate 0.55 vs overall 0.5, by design 500/500; the summary reports Fisher n.s. Unannotated features are therefore 45% of hubs vs 50% of the pool, which is at or below parity, not a 'disproportionate share'. Top-100 hubs are 55% unannotated, also n.s. The atlas L5 annotation rate is 67.8%, not ~50%. Phase 6 summary.json n_features=50, not 30 (30 is the Stage-2 per-layer count). The section uses this to say the Phase-6 causal-patching null is 'not a statement about SAE feature quality in general', and its own numbers do not support that.

Confirmed. Heads are masked through o_proj forward-pre-hooks (setup/maxtoki_adapter.py:215-243). The readout is TRRUST AUROC of layer-mean L8 attention, whose baseline is 0.4399, below chance, so there is no signal to degrade. run_config n_ctrl=300. There is one draw per condition and no CI; random-5 deltas range from −0.005 to +0.018. Best-layer AUROC went up for top5 (0.697 at L2). The spec (attention-grn md:80) calls for 13 conditions, orthogonal interventions, hidden-state/logit fidelity diagnostics and 2000 cells, none of which were run. The test cannot support 'Regulatory heads are not a causal bottleneck' or 'the same causal null the paper reports'. The overall FAIL verdict still rests on C1/C2.

Confirmed. FINAL_SUMMARY:42 says 'VW per-pert AUROC = 0.513 vs raw attention 0.532'. phase0b/run_config.json gives mean_auc_vw 0.4933 and mean_auc_attn 0.5119; Δ −0.0186 and p 0.012 are quoted correctly, so the direction holds. VW TRRUST AUROC at L9/L10 (0.588/0.587) has no curveball or label null, while raw-attention TRRUST equalled its curveball null, so 'rules out value-pathway explanations' is overstated. The 'asymmetry' sentence pairs per-pert raw L1 (0.553) with VW TRRUST L9 (0.59). VW per-pert also peaks late (L9 0.515), so the late-peak observation partly survives a like-for-like check, but the magnitudes compared are not comparable. Reporting errors and an overclaim, without changing the negative verdict.

The mechanism is confirmed in code. phase0_extract.py adds attention over all ordered (A,B) HVG position pairs, which under the causal mask are non-zero only when key B precedes query A in rank order, and divides by pair_counts over all co-occurrences. Phase 1 scores attn[pert_hvg,:]. Each edge therefore equals P(target ranked above pert) × attention, which ties the score to the target's relative expression rank, a gene-level property. README 'Known deviations' #1 notes the directed form, but no transpose, symmetrised or rank-conditioned analysis exists. The effect size cannot be checked because the edge tensors are not in the snapshot. It plausibly affects the central 'attention ⊂ gene-level features' interpretation.

Confirmed: phase3_residualization.py:206-208 gives −13421.3 for K562 (baseline 0.4829 < 0.5), so C3 'FAIL' there is undefined or not evaluable. However, there was no above-chance signal to retain, and the overall FAIL verdict is set by C1/C2 regardless. No result changes. (A related C3 issue: the summary table lists k562_1b C3 as FAIL, but phase12_verdict_k562_1b.json says pass=true, fraction 0.78.)

Confirmed. cluster_sizes are [814,1,261,1,1,1,3,14,310,594]. per_cluster_trrust.csv shows oracle_cluster_max 0.5017 coming from cluster 3 (size 1). CSSI-max (max over clusters) and CSSI-mean (unweighted mean) both give singleton clusters full weight, which likely explains why they are 'significantly worse'. Only the size-weighted SCENIC version ties the baseline. The summary already concedes the skew and limits the claim to 'homogeneous NT controls', so the effect is limited. Still, the 'oracle upper bound at chance' and 'two of three aggregations worse' statements are artefacts of degenerate clusters.

Confirmed. FINAL_SUMMARY states that the depth hierarchy 'is specific to bidirectional BERT-style encoders' and that the VW asymmetry is 'likely specific to causal Llama decoders'. Only MaxToki-217M and 1B were run, and phase1_k562_1b peaks at L4-L5 (0.580/0.581), not at L1. These are generalisations from one model family, and the 1B profile already departs from the 'shallow L1 peak' pattern.

Confirmed in cross_domain_alignment.csv. Layer 0 Pearson is 1.0 for every pair and is included in the 12-layer mean; phase15_summary best_layer is 0 for all pairs. Excluding L0 lowers the means to about 0.85, 0.75 and 0.72. Similarity falls with depth (lung-vs-ext 0.795 at L1 → 0.61-0.69 at L10-11; immune-vs-ext 0.45-0.58), and top-1 retrieval drops to 0.25-0.67 at L11. The only null is a gene-label shuffle, with no within-tissue resampling floor; within-tissue CKA in spectral-geometry stays ≈0.99 to L11. The claims 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel) tissue-invariant geometry' and 'the trained transformer doesn't appear to introduce tissue-specific divergence' overstate what is largely inherited from the static embedding.

Confirmed. In gene_features.csv, immune has is_trrust_tf 343/350 and is_marker 6, lung 87/382 and 43, external_lung 86/380 and 39. The immune run_config shows reused=true from spectral-geometry phase0. h_hub n_tfs_in_pool is 87/343/86. Comparisons between domains (immune vs lung H123 counts, H139 'only immune passes', H-hub in immune) are therefore confounded by pool composition. Within-domain results and replication across heterogeneous pools are not invalidated, and the immune marker limitation is acknowledged for H-lineage, so the impact is on secondary cross-domain contrasts.

Confirmed. phase16_lineage_hub_depth.py uses n_perm=100 and a uniform permutation of TF degree, with no stratification or residualisation by expression, token frequency or norm. h_hub_tf_degree.csv: z 1.31, 2.34, 2.36 (ρ 0.06-0.12). In immune the 'TF' set is 343/350 genes. It is presented as 'POSITIVE 2/3 domains (novel)' and 'the strongest new result', and as Positive #3 in summaries/. The multiplicity point is weaker than stated: with p≈0.01 in two of three domains, BH within the domain family would still pass. The real problem is the missing confound control and the overstated framing of a weak, exploratory effect.

Confirmed. The run FINAL_SUMMARY.md says Phase 4 cross-model CCA is SKIPPED, Phase 11 is SKIPPED, the annotation chain is SKIPPED and 'Layer 1 cannot be evaluated'. README and EXTENDED_FINDINGS report Phase 14/Phase 4 vs Geneformer and scGPT, the Phase 11 substitute and the H124-H138 chain as done. The summaries/ copy says Layer 1 'PARTIALLY REPLICATES' (line 12-15) but its own table (line 44) says 'SKIPPED' and line 89 says these were 'not run'. This is a stale, inconsistent summary; no numbers change.

phase9b_cross_model.py does use a gene-label shuffle (Mantel-type) null, with null mean −0.000 ± 0.001. The spec only says the paper ran a 'permutation test of representation alignment' with p>0.3 and calls the result 'not surprising under a shared-vocabulary null'. It does not define that null, and neither the paper nor its code is in the snapshot (reference_data has only data files). Whether the paper's null differed, making the 'non-replication' a mismatched comparison, cannot be checked. The statistic also differs (paper raw cosine 0.825 vs Pearson of cosine matrices 0.382). The B-cell gene-set/version caveat is already acknowledged in the summary. 'PPI convergent' uses the paper's own type of test, so lacking a frequency null is a shared limitation, not a replication error.

Partly confirmed. tf_vs_target_classifier.csv shows null_mean 0.539-0.546 on every layer, from an in-sample centroid classifier (phases_345.py). The headline mean 0.572 is therefore only ~0.03 above the null, and the summary compares it with 0.5 and with the paper's 0.744. The 5/12 count (L0, L6, L7, L8, L11) is correct and survives BH: sorted p 0.0099×4 and 0.0198 ≤ 5×0.05/12 = 0.021. The multiplicity criticism therefore does not hold. Expression and token frequency are not controlled, and the HVG set is TRRUST-enriched. The claim that the distinction is 'non-trivially represented' is overstated, but the direction of the verdict ('weaker') stands.

Confirmed in ppi_copole_per_axis_per_layer.csv. For SV3 pairs_700, 3/12 are BH-significant and 9/12 nominal. The '10/12 sig' in the updated table and the §8 audit matches remaining/phase4_hub_confound.csv 'all' group with z>2 at 10 layers (uncorrected). The L0 maximum z=5.62 is on SV7 pairs_900, while SV1's maximum over all layers is 3.34, so 'MaxToki SV1 z=5.62 at layer 0' mislabels the axis. These are inconsistencies in reported counts and axis labels.

Partly confirmed. The summary says Phase 10 'NOT run... deferred pending explicit user authorization'. autoloop_master_log.md shows a run on 2026-05-05: iter_0002 and iter_0003 completed with results (H01/H02/H03; H3-BC 'PROMISING' built on an 'early' stratum of N=14, H3-DEL, H3-G). These are not reported. The finding overstates iterations 0004 and 0005: both failed (no report, no artefacts; 'ABORT after 2 consecutive failures'). The summary statement is stale and exploratory results are omitted. No reported number changes.

Confirmed in phase12_anchor_benchmark_lite.json. Branch: pca10 0.844, svd10 0.837, avgpool 0.792, extracted_z10 0.756, raw_log1p 0.142. Pseudotime: z10 0.262 vs pca10 0.509. In the pairwise BH tests, z10 beats only raw_log1p and has no significant difference against PCA, SVD or avg-pool, mostly trending lower. §11 discloses this, but the headline ('internally encodes a hematopoietic developmental manifold', 'compressible 2,400×') and the §10 synthesis ('first affirmative deployable result') do not. The paired within-branch shuffle null controls the ruler but not whether the result is specific to MaxToki. PCA of expression recovers the ordering at least as well, and the 0.14 raw baseline looks degenerate.

Confirmed. phase17_cross_axis_h65_h95.json gives ruler overlap 0.814, H95 self-fit 0.825, H65 self-fit 0.986 and cross-head 0.642 from a single training run per head. If the H95 head's error were independent of the H65 axis, attenuation alone would predict a cross-head ρ of about 0.814×0.825×0.986 ≈ 0.66. The observed 0.642 is only ~0.02 below that, so most of the −0.173 'active rotation away' is explained by imperfect self-fit. There is no seed or bootstrap baseline. The claim 'actively rotates AWAY ... by 0.173' and the 'PARTIALLY_ORTHOGONAL' verdict are overstated.

Confirmed. In steering_F0284_L11.json the top upregulated genes are FTL, then MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO1, FTH1, PABPC1, UBC: a generic list of highly expressed housekeeping and mitochondrial genes. FTL is a ubiquitous iron-storage gene, highest in macrophages, not a terminal erythroid marker, and the cells are TS immune. SOD3 is extracellular superoxide dismutase, not a progenitor or stemness factor. These labels support 'biologically coherent' claims in the exhaustive and attention-grn summaries. The Δs maturity metric itself is unaffected.

review.summary:
I audited all eight pipeline runs against the ten-pattern checklist: attention-grn, circuit-tracing, exhaustive-mapping, sae-atlas, spectral-geometry, topology-141, longevity-mechinterp and manifold-discovery. I also checked the shared setup code. For each load-bearing claim I went from the claim to its numbers to the code, and recomputed numbers where the files allowed it.

The most serious problems are code bugs that invalidate headline results.
(1) The SAE intervention harness has a hook bug, used in Stage-2 circuit tracing and Stage-3 Experiments 1, 2 and 3. The patch is built on hidden_states[l], which is the input of block l, but it replaces the output of block l. So every "feature ablation" or "steering" also deletes block l. Recomputed signatures confirm this: 1000 different features give 4970±25 edges each, 99.3% overlapping targets and d=-5.009±0.014 on a shared target. The first downstream layer has 0 edges for every feature. Experiment 2's ratios satisfy AB=B, AC=C, BC=C, ABC=C exactly. Steering results are identical across features and across α=2 vs 5.
(2) The Phase-11 "CRISPRi directional accuracy" of 54.6% is just the base rate of negative LFC; the circuit's prediction is never used.
(3) SAE annotation applies BH only after a p<0.1 prefilter. Correct BH collapses the reported 62-81% annotation rates to about 0-4%.
(4) The attention-GRN curveball null barely mixes: in simulation 94% of K562 replicates are identical to the observed graph, so "z≈0 in every run" holds by construction.
(5) SAE Phase 6 patching and Phases 8, 8t and 9 compare mismatched layers or SAE reconstruction error, so the "1.01× specificity" and "0% TF specificity" results are artefacts.

Several summaries also misreport their own outputs:
- In RPE1, attention significantly beats 2 of the 3 trivial baselines.
- The 1B C3 verdict is PASS in the JSON but FAIL in the summary.
- The spectral PPI result is "10/12 significant" in the summary but 3/12 after BH.
- The CCA values have no null; the scGPT r≈0.40 sits at the in-sample noise floor of ≈0.41.
- Cross-tissue "invariance" includes layer 0, which is identical by construction.

The manifold headline is not distinguished from PCA on raw expression.

Per-pattern verdicts:
- P1 (null anchoring): present and unaddressed in most runs (broken curveball; unanchored coherence, annotation and CCA numbers; manifold null passes 2-3 of 4 gates; feature-shuffle-only null in spectral).
- P2 (trivial baseline): handled well in attention-GRN; present and unaddressed for manifold (PCA-10 ≥ extracted head), spectral TF-vs-target (expression baseline 0.565 vs 0.572), and the static-embedding floor for cross-tissue and cross-model claims.
- P3 (endpoint–object mismatch): present (head-ablation readout, Phase-8 proxy, manifold rulers that encode cell-type identity, CKA vs fine-tuning seeds).
- P4 (pseudoreplication): present (TRRUST with n=8-32 TFs; SAE position-level tests; longevity has 17 donors with age bins confounded with donor; anchor leakage in manifold).
- P5 (selection / double-dipping): present (annotation-selected sources, head and layer selection on the same panel, post-hoc 3-gate fallback, annotation-biased HVGs).
- P6 (positive controls): absent project-wide, including no check that the model runs in-distribution on the constructed inputs.
- P7 (generalization): partly addressed in attention-GRN (3 datasets plus 1B); otherwise single atlas, single seed, and within-family model comparisons.
- P8 (stability): mostly point estimates without CIs (only 3 random head draws, curveball n=50, no CIs on ΔAUROC).
- P9 (overclaiming): widespread ("causal edges", "confirming", "first affirmative positive", "multi-axis biological hub"), and invalid Stage-3 results are propagated into other runs' summaries.
- P10 (reproducibility): no pinned environment, hook behaviour that depends on the transformers version, external absolute data paths, upstream code missing from the snapshot, and inconsistent summary copies.

findings.description: The feature-ablation patch is built on hidden_states[src_l] (the residual stream entering transformer block src_l; the SAE for 'layer l' was trained on hidden_states[l]). A forward hook then substitutes it for the OUTPUT of model.layers[src_l]. Every 'single-feature ablation' therefore also deletes the entire computation of block src_l (attention + MLP). The measured downstream effects mostly reflect block deletion, not the feature. All Stage-2 headline numbers are invalid: 2,144,011 edges, 88.2% inhibitory, mean |d|=1.84, L0 'broadcast hubs', depth attenuation, 77.8% coverage, and the 'dependency-dominated / deeply entangled architecture' interpretation.
findings.evidence: In HF Llama, hidden_states[i] is the input to block i (hidden_states[0] = embeddings) and the last entry is post-final-norm. The code sets h_patched = clean_hidden[src_l] + delta and calls register_forward_hook on layers[src_l] that returns h_patched. Effects are nearly feature-independent. In circuit_trace.log the top-10 L0 sources have out-degree 39,676…39,658 (all within 18 of each other; mean over 30 sources 39,653). Every top convergent L11 target has in-degree 120, i.e. all 120 sources. The same signature recurs in Stage 3 (F02-F04).
findings.recommended_action: Patch at the correct location: a forward_pre_hook on layers[src_l] (or a hook on the output of layers[src_l-1]), or compute the delta on the state the hook replaces with an SAE trained on that state. Sanity checks: ablating a feature that is inactive must give zero effect, and edge counts must vary across features. Re-run Stage 2 and retract the current summary numbers.

findings.description: Experiment 1 uses the same block-deleting patch as Stage 2, and the outputs show the result is feature-independent. The first downstream layer (L6) also records zero change for every feature: the recorded hidden state does not reflect the patch (a hook/recording interaction that depends on the transformers version). These claims cannot stand: 'every traced feature has >1000 edges', 'uniformly dense circuit', 'top-20 hubs 55% annotated' and 'annotation bias replicates'. Hub ranking is noise around a constant.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the 1000 experiment1/feature_F*.json files. Total edges per feature: mean 4970.1, SD 25.2, min 4900, max 5400. edges_by_layer: L6 = 0 for all 1000 features, L8 = 2532.6±12.1, L11 = 2437.5±14.2 (out of 4928). Mean overlap of top-50 target sets between features is 99.3%. Target (L8, F1586) appears in all 1000 features' top-50 with d = -5.009±0.014. The summary does not report the L6 zeros ('not recomputed per-downstream-layer').
findings.recommended_action: Fix the hook (see F01) and verify that the immediate downstream layer changes. Report per-layer edge counts and between-feature variance. Re-run before drawing any annotation-bias or hub conclusions.

findings.description: In multi-feature conditions, each hook replaces its block's output with the CLEAN hidden state of that layer plus a delta. The deepest hook therefore overwrites every upstream perturbation: AB equals B, AC and BC equal C, and ABC equals C. The 'redundancy ratios' (0.165/0.219/0.586/0.190) are arithmetic consequences of this, and 'zero superadditive synergy' is guaranteed by construction. The summary explicitly claims the across-triplet equality is 'not a code bug' and derives 'feature-invariant ablation magnitudes' and 'no higher-order logical gates' from it.
findings.evidence: From AB = B/(A+B) = 0.1652, B/A = 0.1979; from AC = C/(A+C) = 0.2189, C/A = 0.2802. The predicted BC = C/(B+C) = 0.5861 (observed 0.5861) and predicted ABC = C/(A+B+C) = 0.1896 (observed 0.1896). Ratios are identical (SD < 0.0003) across 4 triplets with entirely different features (combinatorial_summary.json, v1 and v2).
findings.recommended_action: Implement combined ablations by propagating the perturbed stream, not overwriting it. Apply each delta to the current (already perturbed) block input via pre-hooks. Verify that AB ≠ B. Retract the redundancy, synergy and 'feature-invariance' claims until re-run.

findings.description: Steering uses the same block-deleting hook. For li<11, block li is skipped. For li=11 the hook is put on layers[10] and replaced with hidden_states[11], which is already post-final-RMSNorm, so the final norm is applied twice. The summary says hidden_states[11] is 'before RMSNorm', which is wrong for HF Llama. The steering effects are therefore feature- and α-independent. The 'layer-dependent directionality', 'L6 counter-differentiation basin', 'L0 largest effect' and 'α saturation' are artefacts. The 'top upregulated gene' biology (SOD3, KITLG, C1QB, FTL) is also artefactual. This 'first affirmative positive finding' is cited in the attention-GRN, SAE-atlas and topology summaries.
findings.evidence: Per-feature JSONs: the three different L0 features give Δs 0.0961/0.0962/0.0968 and mean logit delta 0.424/0.413/0.426. All L3 features give Δs 0.0177-0.0179. All L6 features give -0.0079. All L9 features give 0.0139-0.0142. All L11 features give logit delta -1.06 to -1.08. Results at α=2 and α=5 agree to within <1% for every feature (summary lines 193-199), although the injected delta scales with (α-1).
findings.recommended_action: Fix the hook placement (pre-hook on the block input; for the final residual, hook before the norm). Add a control showing that α=1 gives zero change and that the effect scales with α. Re-run, and remove the steering claims from all cross-referencing summaries.

findings.description: The 'toward maturity' endpoint is undefined. 'Pseudotime' is the min-max-scaled PC1 of log1p expression over 200 randomly sampled Tabula Sapiens immune cells of mixed types. PC1 sign is arbitrary and it most likely tracks a lineage or cell-type axis, not differentiation. Early and late quartiles are not oriented to any maturity marker. The early and late logit signatures are almost collinear (cos≈0.999). Switch features are selected (|ρ|>0.3) and steered on the same 200 cells. The summary also misdescribes FTL as a 'terminal erythroid marker' in immune cells.
findings.evidence: pca1 = PCA(n_components=1).fit_transform(X_log); early_mask = pseudotime < 25th percentile. Spec signature #10 notes cos(g_early, g_late) ≈ 0.999. The scope section concedes 'PC1-based pseudotime, not … diffusion pseudotime'. 5,767 switch features at a lower bar than the spec (Cohen's d > 0.9).
findings.recommended_action: Use a lineage-restricted, marker-oriented pseudotime (e.g. diffusion pseudotime rooted at HSPC). Select switch features on held-out cells. Report Δs against a random-feature and random-direction null. Remove the maturity interpretation until this is done.

findings.description: The Phase-11 'CRISPRi directional accuracy' never uses the circuit's prediction. A pair counts as 'correct' whenever the target's knockdown LFC is negative. predicted_inhibitory is computed and ignored, and edge sign is lost because only max |d| is stored. The 54.6% is the base rate of negative LFC among 1.46M (source, target) pairs. The conclusion 'confirming circuits encode co-expression, not causal regulation' is unsupported. It is repeated as evidence in the attention-GRN FINAL_SUMMARY (line 141) and topology FINAL_SUMMARY (line 24).
findings.evidence: Code: predicted_inhibitory = info['max_d'] > 0 (unused); if (actual_lfc < 0): n_correct_direction += 1. gene_predictions[key]['max_d'] = max(..., abs(e['cohens_d'])). phase11_crispri_validation.json: 796,159/1,458,016 = 0.5461.
findings.recommended_action: Carry the signed effect per gene pair. Compare the predicted sign with the observed LFC sign only for DE targets, and report accuracy against the base rate and a shuffled-pair null with a CI. This should be done after fixing F01, since the edges themselves are invalid.

findings.description: The remaining circuit metrics are not anchored to chance. 'Biological coherence 36.1%' (shared enrichment term between endpoints) and the 'TRRUST match 0.01%' have no random-feature-pair or random-gene-pair baseline. The disease-centrality Mann-Whitney treats overlapping domain degrees as independent. Annotations are themselves inflated (F09). Comparisons with the paper's 53% and 0.15% are therefore uninterpretable.
findings.evidence: coherence = n_shared/n_annotated_edges with no null. n_known/len(filtered) = 361/5,442,818 with no random-pair expectation. Domain degrees are sums over shared edges.
findings.recommended_action: Compute the same metrics for random (source, target) feature pairs with matched annotation counts, and for random gene pairs. Report observed vs null mean ± SD.

findings.description: There are internal inconsistencies and an untracked dependency. The model is described as having '12 layers' (it has 11 blocks plus the embedding state). The density ratio is given as both '22×' and '41×' (2,144,011/52,116 = 41.1). The Phase-7 PMI validation reads <TMP>/maxtoki-atlas-data-12/cross_layer_graph.json, which is outside the project, and its null outcome is spun as 'as expected'.
findings.evidence: Line 5: '22× denser'; line 53: '41× denser'. Line 103: '12 layers'. config.json: num_hidden_layers 11. remaining_phases.log: 'no overlapping layer pairs for PMI validation'.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the numbers and layer description. Read the PMI graph from atlas-data/cross_layer_graph.json in the project, and report Phase 7 as 'not evaluable'.

findings.description: Feature-annotation BH-FDR is applied only to the tests that already passed raw p<0.1 (and overlap≥2), not to all feature×term tests. The effective threshold becomes about raw p<0.04 with no multiplicity control. The reported annotation rates are therefore grossly inflated: L0 80.7%, L5 67.8%, L11 61.7%, a mean of ~69% across 12 layers, and 'MaxToki more interpretable than Geneformer'. Everything built on these annotations inherits the error: Stage-2 source-feature selection and 'biological coherence', Stage-3 annotated/unannotated split, Phase-10 unannotated characterisation, and the domain meta-graph.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv. Maximum raw p among 'significant' rows: 0.042 (L0), 0.040 (L5), 0.039 (L11). Median overlap is 2 of 20 genes. BH over all tests (features × 2,369 terms; about 11.7M at L5): annotated features 29/2498 (1.2%) at L0, 5/4928 (0.1%) at L5, 0/4924 at L11. Even per-feature BH (m=2,369): 104/2498 (4.2%), 84/4928 (1.7%), 55/4924 (1.1%).
findings.recommended_action: Apply BH over the full family of tests, with the per-feature or global family stated. Recompute annotation rates and anchor them to a null of random 20-gene sets. Re-select circuit sources and re-run all annotation-dependent analyses.

findings.description: Causal patching is invalid in three ways. (a) The L5 SAE, trained on hidden_states[5], is applied to hidden_states[6], so it is off-distribution. (b) The block output is replaced by the full SAE reconstruction instead of clean + delta, so every patch injects the full reconstruction error. (c) The 'target' readout is the mean |logit change| at sequence positions whose input token is one of the feature's top-20 genes, which is a next-token prediction change, not an effect on those genes. The patch effect is dominated by feature-independent reconstruction error. The 'median specificity 1.01×' and 'genuine non-replication: MaxToki features are NOT causally specific' do not stand.
findings.evidence: phase6/causal_patching.csv: mean_other_delta = 1.3948 ± 0.0045 (min 1.3937, max 1.4255) across 50 different features. mean_target_delta = 1.414 ± 0.025. The code is h_patched = sae.decode(h_enc_with_feature_zeroed, mu) on h_probe = hidden_states[PROBE_LAYER+1].
findings.recommended_action: Use the SAE matching the patched state. Inject only (decode(z_ablated) − decode(z)) into the clean stream, and include a reconstruction-only control (decode(z) with no ablation). Measure effects on the logits or ranks of target genes, not on positions.

findings.description:
None of the perturbation-response tests measures a perturbation response.
- Phase 8 'proxy': compares SAE activations at positions whose token is gene G against random other positions, i.e. token identity. It runs 4,928 uncorrected Mann-Whitney tests per gene, so '100% detection' is guaranteed.
- Phase 8t: perturbed-cell activations come from hidden_states[6], while control activations come from the Phase-0 file (hidden_states[5]), so it compares different layers.
- Phase 9: the multi-tissue SAE is trained on pooled K562 hidden_states[5] and TS hidden_states[6], and the test repeats the layer mismatch, giving 95% 'detection'.
TF specificity (0/48) is conditional on detection, and only 4/100 were detected in 8t, so it is uninformative. The claims 'perfect sensitivity', 'central negative replicates: 0% TF specificity' and 'limitation is in MaxToki's representations' cannot stand.
findings.evidence: Phase-0 controls: np.load(PHASE0/'layer_05_activations.npy'), extracted as hidden[5] (phase0_extract_positions.py:107). Perturbed cells: hidden[PROBE_LAYER+1]. phase8_true/summary.json: detection 0.04, specificity 0/48. phase9/summary.json: detection 0.95. Detection uses p<0.05 per feature with no correction, on pooled positions.
findings.recommended_action: Extract perturbed and control cells through the same layer with the same SAE. Aggregate per cell, test at the cell level with FDR control, and compare against non-targeting controls. Define specificity among detected perturbations against a random-target null.

findings.description: 'L0' is the static token-embedding output (hidden_states[0]). It is a deterministic function of the gene token, with no cell context, but it is interpreted as a computational layer. L0 SAE features are partitions of gene identity. The 49% dead rate follows from only about 6.3k distinct input vectors. The interpretations 'early layers = molecular machinery', 'L0 features are globally necessary broadcast hubs' and 'L0 steering pushes toward maturity' describe embedding properties or the block-deletion artefact. Summaries also call the model '12 layers' although it has 11 transformer blocks.
findings.evidence: TARGET_LAYERS comment: 'L0 = post-embedding'. config.json: num_hidden_layers 11. Circuit tracing describes 'L0 features are essential for the entire computation'. The spectral FINAL itself notes L0 is the 'static gene embeddings'.
findings.recommended_action: Label L0 explicitly as the input embedding in all summaries. Exclude it from 'layer computation' claims, or present it as a static-input baseline (P2 floor) for every layer-wise result.

findings.description: '10 co-activation modules per layer with 99.9-100% coverage' is hard-coded. leidenalg was not installed, so the code fell back to SpectralClustering(n_clusters=10), which always returns 10 clusters covering every alive feature. The claim 'matches precisely' the paper's 6-12 modules is an artefact. The 3-layer fallback also clusters pmi[:n_alive, :n_alive] (the first n_alive feature indices, not the alive features) and then maps labels onto alive indices, so L0 labels (2,498 alive of 4,928) are attached to the wrong features.
findings.evidence: Log: 'leidenalg not installed — skipping Leiden'. full_12layer.log reports modules=10 for every layer L0-L11. Coverage = fraction labelled ≥0, which is 1.0 for alive features by construction.
findings.recommended_action: Install leidenalg, or report module count from a data-driven method with a resolution sweep. Fix the alive-index bug. Anchor modularity against a degree-preserving null.

findings.description: '95.9% of features enriched for ≥1 cell type' comes from Fisher tests over token positions. Every position (about 1,000 per cell) is labelled with its cell's type and treated as an independent observation, with Bonferroni over cell types only. The inference unit should be the cell, and ideally the donor. The test also uses hidden_states[6] with the L5 SAE (layer mismatch). With this N almost any feature becomes 'significant'.
findings.evidence: ts_cell_types_per_pos.extend([cell_types_ts[ci]] * h_l5.shape[0]); h_l5 = hidden[PROBE_LAYER+1]; fisher_exact per feature × cell type at p < 0.05/32.
findings.recommended_action: Aggregate feature activation per cell (or per donor), test cell-level enrichment with FDR over features × cell types, and use the layer-matched SAE.

findings.description:
There are contradictory and unanchored structural claims.
- Cross-layer persistence: the 3-layer summary says features are 'overwhelmingly layer-specific — no persistent scaffold. Replicates'. The project's own 12-layer analysis reports 'dramatically higher cross-layer persistence than Geneformer' (21.5% adjacent peak; L0→L8 13.3%).
- '99.9-100% of features invisible to SVD, massive superposition confirmed' compares 4,928 features with only 50 SVD directions at cos>0.7, so near-100% 'novelty' is guaranteed by construction and no null is given.
- 'Information highways 99.6-100%' (≥1 partner with PMI>3 among thousands of candidates) also has no null.
findings.evidence: 3-layer: L0→L5 2.5%, L5→L11 0.5% ('Replicates'). 12-layer: L6→L7 21.5%, L0→L8 13.3%. phases2_to_8.py Phase 3: max_cos > 0.7 against top-50 SVD components.
findings.recommended_action: Reconcile the persistence claims. Retract 'layer-specific/replicates' or explain the difference. Compare SVD-alignment and highway rates against random-direction and shuffled-activation nulls.

findings.description: The degree-preserving curveball null is degenerate. Row pairs are drawn uniformly from all 1,500 HVG rows, but only about 8-45 rows carry TRRUST edges, and the run uses only n_iter = 5×n_edges swaps. Almost no swaps between two non-empty rows occur, so the 'null' graphs are nearly identical to the observed graph. The invariant 'curveball z ≈ 0 in every run (−0.14/+0.17/+0.16/−0.04)' holds by construction and does not show that attention is explained by degree. Meanwhile, in RPE1 the label-shuffle null gives z = +4.18 (TRRUST AUROC 0.6045 vs null 0.502), a positive that is not reported.
findings.evidence: Simulation with the project's sizes (G=1500, 50 replicates). 66 edges over 15 rows: 0.06 effective swaps per replicate and 94% of replicates unchanged. 173 edges/25 rows: 84% unchanged. 96 edges/18 rows: 92% unchanged. 281/45: 42% unchanged. null_results.json: curveball SD 0.0011/0.0015/0.0031/0.0007 vs label-shuffle SD 0.043/0.025/0.018/0.032, with the curveball null mean equal to the observed value to 3 decimals.
findings.recommended_action: Run the curveball only among TF rows (or use a proper bipartite edge-swap) with enough swaps to mix (e.g. ≥10× edges among non-empty rows, checked by edge-overlap with the original). Use n=200 as the spec requires. Report all null z-scores, including the RPE1 label-shuffle positive.

findings.description: The summary states 'No run's attention beats any of the three trivial baselines'. In RPE1, primary-layer attention significantly beats two of them, and RPE1 layer-1 attention reaches 0.707. C1 still fails on gene variance, but the stated universal claim is false. It hides an RPE1 attention advantage, which the pipeline spec lists as a source-paper finding.
findings.evidence: phase1_rpe1: attention 0.6033 vs gene_mean_expr 0.5822 (Δ = −0.021 in attention's favour, BH p = 7.3e-8) and vs 1−dropout 0.5002 (BH p = 4.1e-36). phase12_verdict_rpe1.json: attention_won = true, significant = true for both.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the sentence and report the RPE1 per-baseline outcomes, including the attention-over-mean/dropout advantage and the L1 profile.

findings.description:
The scale claim ('replicates across a 5× model-size increment', 'Scale helps marginally') is misreported and confounded.
- The 1B C3 criterion actually PASSES (OLS residual keeps 78% of above-chance TRRUST signal), but the summary table says FAIL and the text says residualized AUROC 'collapses to chance in every run'.
- 1B propensity-matched incremental value is ΔAUROC +0.046 (0.503→0.549), which is not reported.
- The 1B run uses 200 cells (vs 2000), a different HVG set, and primary layer L8. That is 40% depth for a 20-layer model, contrary to the stated 72-75% depth rule (L14 would be 0.526; L4-L7 peak at 0.58).
- The run is labelled 'MaxToki-217M-HF' in its config and report.
findings.evidence: phase12_verdict_k562_1b.json: C3 pass = true, fraction 0.784 (0.5554→0.5434). Matched GKF: gene_only 0.5028, gene+attn 0.5485. phase1_k562_1b run_config: primary_layer 8. phase0_k562_1b run_config: n_ctrl 200, model 'MaxToki-217M-HF', n_layers 20. '~2.7×' is actually (0.5398−0.5)/(0.5119−0.5) = 3.3×.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the verdict table and text. Re-run 1B with N_ctrl=2000, the same HVG set and a depth-matched or pre-specified layer. Report the propensity-matched result with a CI before making any scale claim.

findings.description: TRRUST-based conclusions (C3, C4, curveball, CSSI) rest on very few TFs: 8 TFs and 66 edges in K562, 16/173 in RPE1, 32/281 in Adamson, 12/96 in 1B. Edges sharing a TF are pooled as if independent. The label-shuffle null SD is up to 0.043, so differences of 0.01-0.04 are noise. The C3 statistic (auc−0.5)/(baseline−0.5) is undefined when the baseline is below 0.5. In K562 (baseline 0.483) it equals −13,421, so FAIL is forced by construction, not by evidence.
findings.evidence: n_tfs_evaluated: 8/16/32/12. K562 C3 fraction −13421.3 and GBDT −2956.6. Adamson C3 'passes' with 1.03 on a 0.5195 baseline (acknowledged).
findings.recommended_action: Report the number of TFs and edges with every TRRUST number, and bootstrap by TF for CIs. Pre-specify that C3 is 'not evaluable' when the baseline CI includes 0.5. Use a larger reference (TRRUST+DoRothEA, or more HVGs and TFs) to reach adequate power.

findings.description: The verdict battery evaluates only L8, which is the weakest or near-weakest layer for per-perturbation AUROC (0.512) and below chance for TRRUST (0.483 / 0.440). Shallow layers carry the strongest signal and were never put through C1-C3 or the nulls: K562 per-pert L1 0.553; RPE1 L1 0.707; layer-mean TRRUST at L1 0.684; heads L2H5 0.769, L2H1 0.708, L1H1 0.706. Pre-specifying L8 is legitimate, but 'No context, no scale, no post-hoc remedy rescues it' and 'attention information is a subset of gene-level features' are claimed for attention in general.
findings.evidence: Phase-4 baseline best layer L1, TRRUST AUROC 0.684 vs L8 0.440. Per-head ranking top-5 all in L1-L4. Phase-1 per-layer profiles for K562 and RPE1.
findings.recommended_action: Restrict the conclusion to L8, or run the full battery on all layers with nested CV or Bonferroni across layers (as the spec requires). Report whether the shallow-layer TRRUST signal survives a properly mixing degree-preserving null and gene-level residualization.

findings.description: The C4 'causal head ablation' measures whether masking the o_proj contribution of heads in L1/L2/L4 changes the TRRUST AUROC of attention patterns at L8, which is itself below chance (0.440). This does not test whether the heads are causally needed for model behaviour or regulatory prediction. Masked heads' own attention patterns are unchanged by o_proj masking. The null is only 3 random 5-head draws, with no CI, on 300 cells. 'Regulatory heads are not a causal bottleneck' is not supported by this design.
findings.evidence: Masked heads (2,5),(2,1),(1,1),(1,6),(4,2); readout trrust_auroc_primary at L8. Deltas −0.005 vs random −0.015/+0.005/−0.018. Best-layer AUROC rose +0.013 under top-5 masking.
findings.recommended_action: Measure an output-level endpoint (e.g. model predictions or perturbation-response prediction) or the TRRUST signal at the layer where the selected heads live. Use ≥100 random and entropy-matched draws with CIs, and select heads on held-out cells.

findings.description: README says Phase 2 used 'logreg + GBDT', but LightGBM was not installed. has_gbdt=false in every run, so incremental value was tested only with a linear logistic model, which cannot detect non-linear attention × gene-feature interactions. C2 is a point-estimate threshold (Δ > 0.005) with no CI. The spec requires the lower 95% CI > 0 under both linear and nonlinear models and all three splits. The 'joint' split is not a joint split: its groups encode pert × target//10, which leaks both pert and target.
findings.evidence: run_config.json has_gbdt: false (K562, RPE1, Adamson, 1B). The spec (attention-grn pipeline line 722) gives criterion (b). In Adamson, gene+corr adds +0.006 to +0.008 (above threshold) while attention does not; this is not discussed.
findings.recommended_action: Install LightGBM and re-run Phase 2. Report bootstrap-by-perturbation CIs for ΔAUROC and a true joint (pert-and-target disjoint) split. Correct the README.

findings.description: In the causal decoder, attn[A→B] exists only when B is ranked above A in that cell. Gene-space edges average over all co-occurring cells, including structurally zero entries, so edge[A,B] is roughly P(rank_B < rank_A) × E[attention | allowed]. The 'attention GRN' is therefore heavily confounded by relative expression rank and position (attention scales roughly with 1/position), which gene-level mean/variance residualization does not remove. The headline claim that attention 'captures co-expression structure' is also never tested. No attention-vs-Spearman edge correlation is reported, and attention and Spearman AUROCs diverge in opposite directions across runs.
findings.evidence: Accumulator adds the full (H,k,k) sub-matrix and divides by symmetric pair_counts. Attention vs Spearman per-pert AUROC: K562 0.512 vs 0.510; Adamson 0.508 vs 0.608 (p = 2.9e-5); 1B 0.540 vs 0.492 (p = 1e-5).
findings.recommended_action: Normalise only over cells where the direction is allowed, or symmetrise. Residualize edges on relative rank and position. Directly report the edge-level correlation between attention and Spearman before claiming attention 'captures co-expression'.

findings.description: Several numbers and labels are misreported. The value-weighted comparison is quoted as 'VW 0.513 vs raw attention 0.532', but the outputs give 0.493 vs 0.512 (the Δ matches). The summary also omits that VW beats raw attention on TRRUST at every layer except L0. Verdict JSONs for RPE1 and Adamson carry copy-pasted scope_notes ('Replogle K562 non-targeting controls only'). The 1B report is titled 'MaxToki-217M run report'.
findings.evidence: phase0b run_config: mean_auc_vw 0.4933, mean_auc_attn 0.5119; VW TRRUST L8 0.532 vs attention L8 0.483.
findings.recommended_action: Regenerate the summary tables directly from output files, and fix the metadata fields.

findings.description: 'Depth-wise compression is learned, not architectural' rests on a feature-shuffle null computed only at the final layer. Independently permuting each hidden dimension across genes destroys all covariance and trivially gives near-full rank (ER 573). It cannot separate learned structure from architectural effects such as anisotropy, RMSNorm or residual accumulation. That would require a random-initialised or weight-shuffled model. The summary also says metrics change 'monotonically', but ER is non-monotonic (L6 169 → L8 202 → L9 202 → L10 172).
findings.evidence: null_feature_shuffle.json: only the final layer. per_layer_metrics.csv: ER 560.8, 332.6, 338.1, 297.6, 231.7, 212.1, 169.4, 174.4, 201.7, 201.9, 172.1, 93.6.
findings.recommended_action: Add a random-init / weight-permuted MaxToki baseline at all layers. Report the shuffle null per layer, and replace 'learned, not architectural' and 'monotonic' with what the evidence supports.

findings.description: The TF-vs-target 'joint SV2-SV7 AUROC 0.572 (peak 0.620)' comes from a centroid classifier fit and scored on the same genes. The in-sample permutation null mean is about 0.54, but the summary anchors to 0.5 ('non-trivially represented'). No gene-level baseline is given: one expression statistic separates TFs from target-only genes about as well. The SV1 axis correlates with mean expression (|r| 0.44-0.50 at L2-L8), yet the GO-CC, PPI and TF results are not residualized for expression.
findings.evidence: null_mean 0.539-0.546 across layers. Recomputed on the same 343 TFs vs 595 target-only genes: 1−dropout AUROC 0.565, mean_expr 0.549. Recomputed |corr(SV1, mean_expr)|: L2 0.44, L5 0.50, L8 0.43.
findings.recommended_action: Use cross-validated classifiers and report excess over the permutation null. Add expression, dropout and token-frequency baselines, and residualize SV coordinates on them before biological interpretation.

findings.description: The PPI encoding significance is misreported. The updated status table and spec audit claim 'SV3 10/12 significant', but under the run's own BH correction (168 tests) SV3 is significant in only 3/12 layers (pairs_700: L7, L9, L11). 'MaxToki layer-0 SV1 STRING PPI max z=5.62' is actually SV7. The 'PPI axis' (SV3) was chosen post hoc as the best of 7 axes, with no correction for that selection. The 'hub confound' analysis shows the signal is driven by high-degree pairs.
findings.evidence: Recomputed: SV3 pairs_700 BH-significant layers [7, 9, 11] (raw-significant 9/12). Layer-0 maximum z = 5.62 is axis SV7 (pairs_900). The headline table (line 25) and run_report give 3/12, contradicting line 269 and audit #7.
findings.recommended_action: Report the BH-corrected counts consistently, correct the axis label, and pre-specify the axis or correct for axis selection. Use a degree- and expression-matched pair null.

findings.description: 'MaxToki representations are vastly more stable than scGPT' compares stability of per-gene mean embeddings across resampled cell sets with the paper's stability across fine-tuning seeds, which are different perturbations. L0 CKA = 1.000 holds by construction because L0 is the static embedding. Averaging 2000 cells per gene makes high CKA expected. The interpretation that MaxToki's larger training corpus explains the difference is unsupported. The phase8 summary.json verdict ('qualitatively reproduces the paper's CKA pattern') contradicts the FINAL_SUMMARY ('does not replicate').
findings.evidence: phase8/summary.json: interpretation 'across-cell-sample stability (no fine-tuning seeds available)'; layer_0 CKA 1.0; verdict string as quoted.
findings.recommended_action: Mark the comparison 'not testable' (no seeds). If a stability statement is wanted, compare against a cell-resampling stability estimate for scGPT or Geneformer computed the same way, and resolve the contradictory verdicts.

findings.description: MaxToki-Geneformer static-embedding alignment (Pearson 0.382) is declared a non-replication of the paper's null ('the paper's null was architecture- or gene-set-specific'). But both models share the same Ensembl tokenizer and a closely related pretraining corpus and rank-value encoding (the Geneformer gene-median file is even reused). Significance is tested only against a gene-label shuffle (null SD 0.001), which ignores shared gene-level properties such as token frequency or expression that both embeddings may encode. The paper's comparison was across tokenizers, so the two results are not comparable.
findings.evidence: cross_model_cosine.json: null_mean −0.0, null_sd 0.001, n_perm 500. The README and adapter use Geneformer's gene_median_dictionary_gc104M and token set.
findings.recommended_action: Use a null that preserves gene frequency and expression strata (stratified shuffle), and partial out shared gene-level covariates. Compare against an out-of-family model on the same genes, and describe the result as within-family alignment.

findings.description: The headline 'clean negative' (PH 1/12 layers, H123 0-1/12, strict max-null −0.050) has no positive control. The test battery was never run on scGPT or Geneformer embeddings over the same small gene pools (~350-380 genes; 138-504 TRRUST and 24-61 STRING positive pairs, PCA-20), and never on a planted-signal synthetic graph. The negative cannot be attributed to MaxToki rather than to limited power or the gene-pool construction. The Forman-curvature direction check is a sanity check, not a positive control for H01/H123.
findings.evidence: phase1_summary: n_pos_string 48/24/61, n_genes 382/350/380. No positive-control or synthetic run exists in outputs. Persistent-homology observed values fall significantly below the shuffle null at several layers (e.g. lung L0 z = −4.9), which is not discussed.
findings.recommended_action: Run the identical harness on Geneformer and scGPT embeddings for the same gene pools, and on a synthetic embedding with planted TRRUST-aligned structure at known SNR. Report detection power before calling MaxToki negative.

findings.description: 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel): MaxToki encodes a tissue-invariant gene geometry' averages over all 12 states, including L0, where the static embeddings are identical across tissues (Pearson 0.99999, top-1 1.0, chosen as 'best_layer'). Against the trivial L0 floor, the contextual layers show progressive tissue-specific divergence. This contradicts the stated interpretation that 'the trained transformer doesn't appear to introduce tissue-specific divergence'. The gene-label-shuffle null (null mean ≈0) is too weak to support 'invariance'.
findings.evidence: lung_vs_external_lung: L0 0.99999 falling to L9 0.638, L10 0.608, L11 0.689; top-1 1.00 → 0.25. immune_vs_external_lung: L10 0.448, L11 0.582; top-1 0.30.
findings.recommended_action: Exclude L0 (or report it as the floor) and report per-layer change relative to it. Compare against within-tissue split-half reliability, and restate the finding as 'similarity decreases with depth'.

findings.description: CCA 'mean r' is computed in-sample (fit and scored on the same ~350-380 genes, 30 PCA dims per model, top-10 components) with no null. Pure noise of this size gives a mean top-10 canonical correlation of about 0.41. So the scGPT result (0.40-0.44) is at chance, not 'weaker alignment'. The Geneformer value 0.78 'within ±0.05 of the paper's 0.80' is uncalibrated, and the static embeddings again share a tokenizer (see F29).
findings.evidence: Simulation of independent Gaussian matrices, n=380, p=q=30, exact canonical correlations, 30-50 replicates: mean of top-10 = 0.411 ± 0.010, top-1 = 0.516. Observed scGPT: cca_mean_r 0.401/0.438/0.406, top 0.476/0.547/0.506.
findings.recommended_action: Use held-out-gene CCA (fit on one half, score on the other) and a gene-shuffle CCA null. Report CCA as observed − null with a CI, and rewrite the Layer-1 cross-family conclusion accordingly.

findings.description: The exploratory 'positives' are reported without multiplicity correction. They come from ~10 hypotheses × 3 domains × several layers, plus a 6-hypothesis autoloop, and 'H-hub' (z = 2.34 and 2.36) is called the 'strongest new result'. The lineage and hub tests are run at a single chosen layer (L6) with no layer-selection correction and a single seed.
findings.evidence: H-hub Spearman 0.06/0.12/0.11 with z = 1.3/2.34/2.36. The layer choice is not pre-registered.
findings.recommended_action: Apply FDR across the exploratory family, report all layers, and label these as exploratory.

findings.description: The Stage-1 G1 test is structurally uninformative. Age is constant within donor, and there are only 17 donors. The three cell-level quantile age bins hold 10, 4 and 3 donors, with boundaries at 56 and 60 years, so 'age bin' is nearly donor identity. Under donor-held-out CV whole bins are scarce in training. Both MaxToki (0.276) and HVG-PCA (0.172) score below the 3-class chance level of 0.333. The summary nevertheless says the result 'does imply' that MaxToki L5 does not separate cells by age, and that L5 'beats HVG-PCA … encoding something beyond raw expression'. Comparing two below-chance anti-learning scores supports neither claim.
findings.evidence: Recomputed donors per bin: (22,56] 10 donors; (56,60] 4 donors (ages 59-60); (60,74] 3 donors. Null mean 0.332 ≈ 1/3. Observed values are below chance for both representations.
findings.recommended_action: Treat the result as not evaluable rather than as evidence of no age encoding. Use a donor-level regression of age on donor-aggregated representations (n=17, with CIs) or a larger cohort, and remove the 'beats HVG-PCA' interpretation.

findings.description: The load-bearing permutation null, CV splitting and subsampling are imported from an upstream repo (repos/longevity-mechinterp/implementation/scripts/run_stage1_longevity_mechinterp.py) that is not in the snapshot. Whether labels are permuted at the donor or cell level cannot be verified. The README parameters (8,000 cells, 600/donor, 24 donors, 1,024 tokens with 'effectively no truncation') disagree with the script (3,000 cells, 200/donor) and the outputs (2,974 cells, 17 donors). A mean sequence length of 998 against a 1,024 cap implies frequent truncation. The claim that 'L5 is the canonical tap used by every other MaxToki pipeline (incl. attention-GRN)' is false: attention-GRN used L8.
findings.evidence: run_stage1.py imports _permutation_null_for_best etc. from UPSTREAM_SCRIPTS. TARGET_N_CELLS = 3000, MAX_CELLS_PER_DONOR = 200. extraction_stats.json: n_donors_final 17, mean_seq_len 998.2.
findings.recommended_action: Vendor the upstream functions into the run, document the permutation unit, correct the README and summary parameters, and report the truncation rate.

findings.description: The headline 'MaxToki-217M internally encodes a hematopoietic developmental manifold … first affirmative deployable result' is never compared with a trivial baseline in the headline. The run's own Phase-12 LITE shows PCA-10 on raw log expression matches or beats the extracted head on every endpoint, so the manifold is recoverable from expression without MaxToki. The ΔAUROC-over-baseline (negative) is the finding but appears only in §11.
findings.evidence: Branch balanced accuracy: PCA-10 0.844 vs extracted_z10 0.756 (Δ −0.088). Stage: 0.595 vs 0.551. Pseudotime: 0.509 vs 0.262 (Δ −0.247). Frozen MaxToki avg-pool ≈ PCA. Only the raw_log1p comparison (BH-q 0.049) is significant.
findings.recommended_action: Restate the headline as 'recoverable from MaxToki embeddings, no advantage over expression PCA'. Run the full gate stack on PCA-10 and avg-pool features as baselines.

findings.description:
The quality gates do not separate signal from null.
- Anchors are (donor, tissue, cell type) centroids, and the stage ruler is a function of cell-type label, so random and donor holdouts leak cell-type identity. The within-branch shuffled null passes both (random 0.799, donor 0.707) and nearly passes trust (0.799 vs 0.811). Only branch-holdout discriminates, from a single null shuffle.
- The frozen 'blocked-permutation p ≤ 0.001 with ≥2000 permutations' gate is never computed.
- External and zero-shot panels have no null head evaluated.
- The lung_nonhema 'negative control' assigns random labels, which no head can predict, so it cannot show the gates 'aren't too loose' or that the manifold captures hematopoietic biology.
findings.evidence: quality_gates_spec thresholds include blocked_permutation_p_max 0.001 and n_permutations_min 2000; phase5 code evaluates only 4 gates. anchor_meta_internal: 290 anchors, 28 cell types, 24 stages, 11 donors.
findings.recommended_action: Implement the permutation gate with ≥2000 blocked permutations. Evaluate several null shuffles and apply null heads to the external and zero-shot panels. Use cell-type-held-out splits, and a negative control with a real biological ruler that should not be encoded.

findings.description: The 'multi-axis biological hub' claim selects 2 positives (H95, H103) from 18 swept rulers plus H65 and H38, with no multiplicity control. It uses a '3-gate fallback' introduced after the fact when the category-holdout gate is undefined, effectively relaxing the frozen gates. All rulers are functions of cell-type labels on the same cell-type centroids and are strongly inter-correlated (H65 vs H95 ruler ρ = 0.814). Recovering several of them is expected from cell-type separability alone. L10H6 and the compaction variants were also selected and scored on the same internal panel ('compact beats full drift').
findings.evidence: Sweeps #1-#3: 6+6+6 candidates. H95 and H103 are 'POSITIVE (3-gate)'. Phase-17 ground-truth ruler overlap 0.814. Head screen: 13/88 heads pass trust, and the top-1 is chosen by the composite score on the internal panel.
findings.recommended_action: Pre-register rulers or apply FDR over the sweep, and keep the 4-gate rule. Test whether a cell-type-identity ruler explains each 'manifold'. Select heads and compaction variants on a split separate from the one used for evaluation.

findings.description: The 'external', 'zero-shot' and 'completely separate cohort' panels are disjoint donors from the same Tabula Sapiens immune atlas (same protocol and annotation), so the generalisation claim is within one dataset. The summaries/ copy of FINAL_SUMMARY differs from the run copy (H38/H95 external and zero-shot listed as 'n/t' in one and as passes in the other).
findings.evidence: Phase 0 panels are all 'TS immune'. diff of the two FINAL_SUMMARY copies at lines 245-246.
findings.recommended_action: Validate on an independent atlas (e.g. a different hematopoietic dataset or technology) before using 'completely separate cohort', and synchronise the summary copies.

findings.description:
No run verifies that MaxToki is operated in-distribution. The setup has several unverified choices:
- Gene medians are borrowed from Geneformer, assumed 'within noise'.
- Single-cell inputs are wrapped as <bos> genes <eos>, although MaxToki is a trajectory model with <boq>/<eoq> and time tokens.
- Inputs are truncated to 2,048 tokens over restricted gene panels (K562 6,546 genes, Adamson 4,888).
- The code never checks whether h5ad .X holds raw counts. The Adamson file is a GEARS 'perturb_processed' object (typically log-normalized), which would make rank encoding and DE-calling operate on doubly transformed data.
No model-level positive control (e.g. next-token rank-prediction accuracy or loss on held-out cells against a shuffled-input baseline) exists. Negative findings in every pipeline could therefore reflect off-distribution inputs.
findings.evidence: token_dictionary.json contains <boq>, <eoq> and 1,500 time tokens (ids 20275+). There is no grep hit for perplexity or next-token checks in any run. ADAMSON_H5 = '.../perturb_processed_symbols.h5ad'. tokenize_cell divides .X values by count-scale medians without a scale check.
findings.recommended_action: Add a sanity phase: next-gene prediction accuracy or loss on real vs rank-shuffled inputs, and compare <bos>/<eos> against the native MaxToki prompt format. Assert integer counts or use the raw layer. Report these as the project-wide positive control.

findings.description:
The scaffolding for reproducibility is missing.
- No pinned environment: the README pip-installs with '>=' ranges and there is no requirements/lock file in the project.
- Results depend on transformers-version behaviour: hooks return bare tensors vs tuples, hidden_states recording interacts with hooks, and the 1B log's 'rope_parameters' warning indicates a much newer transformers than the config's 4.44.2.
- All datasets are read from absolute external paths (<DATA_ROOT>/...) and are not archived or hashed.
- Compute footprint is reported only for some runs.
- Pipeline specs reference environment files in external repos/.
findings.evidence: README: "pip install 'torch>=2.3' 'transformers>=4.44' …". F02 shows hook semantics changed the measured L6 state. No RUNTIME.md or environment lock exists in runs/.
findings.recommended_action: Freeze an environment lock (pip freeze or conda env) per run with versions of torch, transformers, sklearn and lightgbm. Record dataset checksums and access instructions. Add per-phase wall time and hardware to each run.

findings.description:
The cross-pipeline syntheses carry invalid results forward and use causal and mechanistic language beyond the evidence:
- 'first affirmative positive mechanistic-interpretability finding' (Stage-3 steering, F04).
- 'MaxToki represents cell identity along a differentiation axis, not the regulatory mechanism'.
- 'switch features generalise causally'.
- 'Zero higher-order synergy … no gate of any order recovers it' (F03).
- 'CRISPRi 54.6% … confirming co-expression' (F06).
- '2.1M causal edges', 'dependency-dominated architecture' (F01).
- 'The limitation is in MaxToki's representations' (F11).
Negative results are also overgeneralised to 'no context, no scale, no post-hoc remedy rescues it' (F18, F20).
findings.evidence: Quoted passages at the listed lines. Each rests on F01-F06, F10, F11, F16 or F18.
findings.recommended_action: After fixing the bugs, do one global pass. Replace 'causal edges', 'confirms' and 'encodes' with evidence-grade verbs, state the claim level (decoding / cross-model agreement / intervention-consistent / causal mechanism), and remove claims that depend on invalidated analyses.

findings.description: 'Fisher not significant' for annotation enrichment among the top-20 hubs is a hard-coded string. No Fisher test is computed anywhere in the scripts, and with feature-invariant edge counts (F02) the hub ranking is noise.
findings.evidence: grep finds 'Fisher' only inside the synthesis text literal; experiment1_exhaustive.py computes only proportions (11/20 vs 500/1000).
findings.recommended_action: Compute and report the test (or drop the p-value language) after the tracing is fixed.
