verdicts.reason: Confirmed in phases2_to_8.py and full_12layer_pipeline.py. Tests are kept only if overlap>=2 and p<0.1, and BH is then applied to that pooled survivor set only. The spec (pipelines/sparse-autoencoders/01-sae-atlas.md step 3) asks for BH across all terms tested per feature. I recomputed from significant_enrichments.csv. Full-family BH (m = n_alive x 2369) gives L0 29 features (1.2%), L5 5 (0.10%), L11 0. The spec's per-feature BH over 2,369 terms gives 4.2% / 1.7% / 1.1%, and per-feature Bonferroni gives 3.7% / 1.4% / 1.0%. Every kept p_raw is <=0.042, and 79-85% of hits have overlap = 2. The reported 62-81% rates, the 333,623 enrichments (sum checked), the U-shape and the claim of being 'more interpretable than Geneformer' all rest on this flawed correction.

phases2_to_8.log says 'leidenalg not installed'. Every layer in both the 3-layer and 12-layer logs reports modules=10, which is exactly the SpectralClustering n_clusters=min(10,n_alive) fallback. The spec requires Leiden and says 6-12 modules is non-trivial only under Leiden. 3-layer coverage is 0.507 = 2498/4928, i.e. the alive fraction. In the 3-layer script the fallback clusters pmi_pos[:n_alive,:n_alive] and maps labels onto alive_idx, which scrambles L0 (49% dead). The 12-layer script subsets alive features correctly. The 'matches precisely' scorecard row is therefore an artefact, and Phase 10 inherits it. Major rather than critical because it is one structural metric.

The 12-layer summary lists L0->L1 0.5%, L1->L2 3.3% and L2->L3 1.6%. crosslayer_full.log and sae-atlas-crosslayer-analysis.log show 0/4928, 8/4928 (0.2%) and 45/4928 (0.9%). The denominator is decoder-norm>1e-8, so all 4,928 features count, including the 2,430 dead L0 features. With alive features only, L0->L5 is 125/2498 = 5.0%, not the 2.5% the 3-layer summary says 'matches' the paper. One summary concludes 'layer-specific, replicates' and the other 'dramatically higher persistence than Geneformer'. Neither has a seed-matched null. Alive counts are also inconsistent: 3-layer Phase 1 gives L5 4903 vs 4928 in Phase 2, and the 12-layer table mixes the two definitions.

Confirmed in remaining_phases.py. Phase 7 sets PMI to 0 only when cooc==0 and has no minimum count, then takes the max over ~4,928 targets with threshold >3. There is no null, and the rates are 99.6-100%. Phase 11 runs Fisher tests on token positions, which share their cell's type (pseudo-replication), with Bonferroni over cell types only; the spec asks for BH. Phase 10's co-activation rate depends on 10 spectral modules of ~490 features each and on the inflated annotation set. With ~65% of features 'annotated', every module contains an annotated feature, so 99.8-100% holds by construction. Three scorecard 'replicates' rows are uninformative.

Valid: phase1a_lung_nonhema_panel.py line 91 assigns rng.choice(STAGE_NODES) uniformly at random to non-hema anchors, so any feature set would fail the control. It cannot support 'gates aren't too loose' or 'not generic tissue covariance' (summary §5 and §10). No model-free (raw-expression) baseline was run. One piece of the evidence is wrong: in phase12_anchor_benchmark_lite.py, pca10, svd10 and even 'raw_log1p' are all built from MaxToki avg-pooled hidden-state centroids (shape 290x12x1232), not raw expression. PCA-10 matching the extracted head therefore does not show the result is model-independent. Model-specificity is untested, not disproven.

Confirmed. At line 242, 'alive = (np.load(...).shape[0] > 0)' is never used, so all 4,928 L0 features (2,430 dead) are counted as novel. full_12layer_pipeline.py hard-codes n_svd_aligned=0 and n_novel=n_alive (comment 'computed below', never computed) and writes svd_comparison.json with 0 aligned. Random unit vectors in 1232-d would also be ~100% 'novel' against 50 SV axes, so 'massive superposition confirmed' is unsupported. The metric does follow the spec/paper, and the numbers barely change (actual 99.9-100%), so the impact is minor.

Confirmed. MaxToki is LlamaForCausalLM with genes rank-ordered by expression/median (maxtoki_adapter.tokenize_cell). phase0 accumulates attn[query=A, key=B] and divides by pair_counts over all co-present cells, so attn[P,T] is structurally zero whenever T ranks below P. Phase 1 uses only the row attn_primary[pert_hvg,:], and no transposed or symmetrised edge is evaluated. The README acknowledges the lower-triangular structure and deliberately uses the raw directed form. This is a real confound and a gap in the 'replicates in a causal decoder' claim. However, it is unlikely to flip a verdict where gene variance beats attention by 0.06-0.20 AUROC, so minor.

Confirmed. lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv has n_markers = 6 (B) and 9 (T). The TwoNN fit runs on 5 points after the F<0.9 mask, and values jump around (B: 101, 34, 34, 62, ...). There is no size-matched random-gene null while global TwoNN falls 102->6.7. Spec audit row #16 says 'distance metrics replicate strongly', but dist_BATF_to_PAX5 has rho = +0.979 (divergence), and summary §10 itself says the attractor does not hold. rank_BATF rho = 0.371, p = 0.23. The B-cell 'replicated' tick is uninterpretable, but this is limited to Phase 7 rows.

phases_345.log gives SV3 significant_layers=3/12 using p_bh<0.05, and that is what summary §7 reports. remaining.log gives 'SV3 all sig_layers(z>2)=10/12', which the scorecard (line 269) and spec audit (line 325) report. The hub-degree and GO-split comparisons also use uncorrected z>2 counts. SV3 was picked as the best of 7 axes. This is inconsistent reporting of significance; the qualitative claim of a 'weaker' PPI signal is unchanged.

phase0b.log shows VW primary 0.4933 vs attention primary 0.5119 (delta -0.0186, p=0.0125). The summary states 0.513 vs 0.532 (delta and p are correct). The 'architectural asymmetry' line compares VW TRRUST AUROC (peak 0.588) with attention per-perturbation AUROC (L1 0.553), which are different metrics. Attention TRRUST rests on 66 edges with label-shuffle null SD 0.043 (phase3.log). The conclusion that VW underperforms is unaffected, but the numbers and the interpretation are wrong.

phase15.log shows max Pearson = 1.000 and best_layer = 0 for all three pairs, so L0 static embeddings are included in the 12-layer mean. The only null is a gene-label shuffle, with no within-tissue split-half or model-free baseline. EXTENDED_FINDINGS concedes 'of course the static layer is tissue-invariant' yet keeps 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel)'. Even without L0, Pearson stays around 0.45-0.87, so similarity is high. The problem is the novelty and meaning claim, not the numbers. Small evidence slips: mean Pearson is 0.74-0.86 and median top-1 0.93-0.99.

phase16 log: H-hub z = 1.31 / 2.34 / 2.36 at the fixed layer L6, with 100 permutations and no expression or frequency control. The FINAL_SUMMARY says Forman AUROCs 0.34/0.42/0.35 are 'exactly in range' 0.34-0.39, but immune 0.42 is outside. The immune pool is described as 1,500 cells, but spectral-geometry phase0 used N_cells=2000 (1500 is the HVG count). Mitigating: the layer was pre-specified, and z~2.3 roughly survives Bonferroni over 3 domains. Impact is limited to an overclaimed weak positive.

The nearest-centroid AUROC is in-sample, and the permutation null averages 0.539-0.546 (tf_vs_target_classifier.csv). The permutation null refits centroids on permuted labels, so perm_p already accounts for in-sample optimism, and 5/12 layers remain significant. The summary already calls the signal 'weaker' than the paper's 0.744/0.789; correcting for the ~0.54 baseline would only strengthen that. The recomputed mean is 0.567 vs the reported 0.572, a negligible difference.

review.summary:
I reviewed all 8 pipeline runs: attention-GRN, SAE atlas, circuit tracing, exhaustive mapping/steering, spectral geometry, manifold discovery, topology-141 and longevity. I read the code, re-derived numbers from the output files and re-ran key computations in Python. Several headline results come from code bugs.

(1) Stage-2 and Stage-3 ablation and steering are off by one layer. Each SAE for layer ℓ is trained on hidden_states[ℓ], the input to block ℓ, but the patch is written as the output of model.layers[ℓ]. Every "single-feature ablation" therefore also deletes a whole transformer block. The outputs confirm this:
- All 1,000 Exp-1 features have 4,900–5,400 edges, with 0 edges at L6 and exactly 2,534 at L8.
- Top-target sets overlap with Jaccard 0.96 across features.
- Steering gives the same top gene and Δs for every feature at a layer, and α=2 equals α=5.

(2) In Exp-2, later hooks overwrite earlier ablations. The redundancy ratios follow exactly from the single-layer effects (BC=0.587 and ABC=0.190 predicted from AB and AC), so "zero synergy" holds by construction.

(3) The CRISPRi "directional accuracy" (54.6%) never uses the predicted sign. It is just the fraction of targets with negative fold change.

(4) In the SAE atlas, Phase 6 patching and the true-CRISPRi, multi-tissue and cell-type tests use the wrong layer: the SAE is trained on hidden_states[5] but applied to hidden_states[6]. Phase 6 also lacks a reconstruction-error control. The "1.01× specificity" and "0% TF specificity" results cannot stand. Separately, the "10 modules" result is hard-coded by a clustering fallback, and the annotation false-discovery-rate correction is applied only after pre-filtering p<0.1.

(5) In attention-GRN, the curveball (degree-preserving) null does not permute anything. Re-running it gives 0 edges moved, so z≈0 by construction. The verdict table contradicts the verdict JSON (the 1B run passes C3), and RPE1 attention does beat two trivial baselines. The 1B-vs-217M comparison is confounded (200 vs 2,000 cells, 40% vs 73% layer depth).

(6) The spectral, manifold, topology and longevity runs make overclaims that lack controls:
- No random-init model or model-free baseline is run through the same tests.
- The manifold "trust" gate measures how well the latent preserves the input-feature neighbourhoods, not agreement with the biology.
- The headline 6× compression comes mostly from the static embedding layer (L0) and the final norm (L11).
- TwoNN dimension is estimated on 6 genes.
- The tissue-invariance mean includes layer 0, which is identical across tissues by construction.
- The longevity probe's accuracies are below chance.

(7) The tokenizer uses Geneformer's gene medians, restricted gene panels and 2,048-token truncation, and does not check that inputs are raw counts. The transformers version is unpinned even though results depend on version-specific hook behaviour.

Cross-pipeline summaries repeat the broken results as established evidence.

findings.description: Each SAE for 'layer l' is trained on hidden_states[l], which is the INPUT to transformer block l (l=0 is the embedding output). The ablation builds h_patched = hidden_states[l] + delta and returns it as the OUTPUT of model.model.layers[l], whose true output is hidden_states[l+1]. So every single-feature 'ablation' also deletes the whole computation of block l. The measured downstream effects are dominated by this perturbation, which does not depend on the feature. The pipeline spec explicitly warns about this off-by-one (pipelines/sparse-autoencoders/02-causal-circuit-tracing.md:174,609). Every Stage-2 headline therefore reflects block deletion, not feature circuits: 2,144,011 edges, '22x/41x denser', 88.2% inhibitory, L0 broadcast hubs, depth attenuation, 77.8% target coverage, 'dependency-dominated architecture'.
findings.evidence: Code: clean_hidden[l] = out_clean.hidden_states[l]; h_patched = clean_hidden[src_l] + delta; hook on xt.model.model.layers[src_l]. circuit_summary.json: each L0 source has 39,653 edges, about 73% of all 54,208 possible downstream targets. The top-5 hubs have out-degree 39,670-39,676, identical to within 6. The same code path in Stage 3 is shown to be feature-independent in F02 (identical edge sets across features).
findings.recommended_action: Hook block l-1 (or train SAEs on, and patch at, hidden_states[l+1]) so the patch replaces the tensor the SAE was trained on. Add a delta=0 control that must give zero effect. Rerun Stage 2 and retract the edge, hub, inhibition, density and coherence claims until then.

findings.description: Exp 1 uses the same off-by-one patch: block 5 is skipped for every source feature. The outputs show that the measured 'circuits' do not depend on the feature. These claims therefore cannot stand: 4,970,096 edges; '100% of features have >1000 edges, uniformly dense, no hub/tail split'; 'annotation bias replicates (top-20 hubs 55% annotated)'. The hub ranking is noise over a spread of about 1%. Every feature also has 0 edges at L6. The recorded hidden_states[6] is the un-hooked output of block 5, so the direct downstream layer is never measured. The summary does not mention this.
findings.evidence: Computed from the 1,000 outputs/experiment1/feature_F*.json files: total_edges min 4,900, 5th-95th percentile 4,960-4,978, median 4,967, max 5,400 (the summary says 'range 0-5,400'). edges_by_layer for the first, middle and last features is {L6: 0, L8: 2534, L11: 2434-2443}. Mean Jaccard of top-50 target sets over 60 features is 0.956. 19 targets appear in the top-50 of all of the first 200 features; e.g. target (L8, F3475) has d = -3.78 +/- 0.03 across those 200 features.
findings.recommended_action: Fix the hook index and add delta=0 and random-direction controls. Re-trace, then recompute the hub and annotation-bias statistics from feature-specific effects.

findings.description: In the multi-feature conditions, each hook replaces its block's output with clean_hs[al] + delta, computed from the CLEAN run. The hook at the deepest ablated layer therefore overwrites everything the earlier ablations did: AB = B, AC = C, BC = C and ABC = C, each plus block skips (F01). The pairwise and three-way 'redundancy ratios' are just ratios of single-layer effect sizes, and 'zero superadditive synergy' holds by construction. The summary explicitly concludes that the identical ratios across 4 different triplets are 'a real property of MaxToki, not a code bug'. It also claims that L0 contributes small effects, but the data imply the L0 effect is about 5 times larger than the others.
findings.evidence: Solving AB = b/(a+b) = 0.1652 and AC = c/(a+c) = 0.2189 gives b = 0.198a and c = 0.280a. These predict BC = c/(b+c) = 0.587 (reported 0.5861), ABC = c/(a+b+c) = 0.190 (reported 0.1896) and marginal_C_given_AB = 1 - b/c = 0.295 (reported 0.2938). Ratios are identical to +/-0.0003 across 4 triplets with entirely different L0/L5/L9 features (experiment2_v2/combinatorial_summary.json).
findings.recommended_action: Apply ablations cumulatively within the ablated forward pass (compute each delta from the already-perturbed residual), fix the layer index, and report per-feature effect magnitudes. Retract 'redundancy 4.5x deeper', '0/2980 synergy' and 'feature-invariant ablation magnitudes'.

findings.description: Steering at SAE layer li writes hidden_states[li] + delta as the output of block min(li, 10), so block li is skipped. For li = 11, hidden_states[11] is already the post-final-RMSNorm state in HF Llama. Injecting it as the output of block 10 applies the final norm twice. The summary wrongly calls hidden_states[11] 'the final residual before RMSNorm'. The measured 'steering' effects are therefore artifacts that depend on neither the feature nor alpha. There is no alpha=1 (delta=0) or random-feature control. These claims cannot stand: 'layer-dependent directionality', 'L6 counter-differentiation basin', 'L0 pushes toward maturity, frac_mat 0.98', 'L11 pushes 78-82% of cells toward maturity'. The 'alpha-saturation by RMSNorm' explanation is likewise unsupported.
findings.evidence: Log lines 19-33: all three features at each layer give the same top up-regulated gene (L0 SOD3/KITLG, L3 C1QTNF3-AMACR, L6 C1QB, L9 PAQR3, L11 FTL). Their Δs agree within 0.001 regardless of the feature's pseudotime sign: L0 F40 (negative) and F1657 (positive) both give Δs of about +0.096; L11 F1949 (positive) and F3924 (negative) both give Δlogit of about -1.07. alpha=2 and alpha=5 metrics agree within 1% (summary table lines 193-199), although delta scales with (alpha-1), which goes from 1 to 4.
findings.recommended_action: Fix the hook index. For L11, hook block 10 with the pre-norm residual. Add delta=0, random-feature and random-direction controls, and verify that effects scale with (alpha-1) before interpreting directionality.

findings.description: 'Pseudotime' is PC1 of log1p expression over 200 random Tabula Sapiens immune cells of mixed lineages, rescaled to [0,1]. 'Early' and 'late' are PC1 quartiles. This axis mostly reflects cell-type composition, not differentiation. The early and late logit signatures are nearly identical (cos ≈ 0.999), so Δs is a difference of nearly collinear vectors. 5,767 'switch features' come from |rho| > 0.3 with no multiple-testing correction. FTL (ubiquitous ferritin light chain) is described as a 'terminal erythroid/mature marker' in immune cells.
findings.evidence: experiment3_rerun.py:127 pseudotime = rescaled pca1. Summary item 10: cos(g_early, g_late) ≈ 0.999. Switch-feature counts per layer are 610-1371. Spec deviation acknowledged at line 135.
findings.recommended_action: Use lineage-resolved pseudotime (diffusion pseudotime within a lineage) validated with maturation markers, apply multiplicity control, and drop the biological labels for the top genes.

findings.description: 'Directional accuracy' counts a predicted (source, target) pair as correct whenever the observed knockdown fold change of the target is negative. The circuit's predicted sign is never used: predicted_inhibitory = info['max_d'] > 0 is always True because max_d stores |d|, and the variable is not used anyway. The 54.6% is therefore just the fraction of targets with negative fold change in Replogle K562, a property of the data. The claim 'both near-chance, confirming circuits encode co-expression, not causal regulation' cannot stand. The 1.46M pairs are also highly non-independent.
findings.evidence: Code lines 322 and 327: 'if (actual_lfc < 0): n_correct_direction += 1'. phase11_crispri_validation.json: 796,159 / 1,458,016 = 0.5461. The result is cited as evidence in the topology FINAL_SUMMARY.md:24, EXTENDED_FINDINGS.md and the attention-GRN summary cross-reference.
findings.recommended_action: Compare the sign of each edge's mean delta (or the gene-level aggregate) with the sign of the observed fold change. Use a per-source permutation baseline, aggregate per source gene, and only then interpret.

findings.category: code-bug (wrong layer + reconstruction overwrite) / wrong metric
findings.description: Three problems. (i) The 'L5' SAE was trained on hidden_states[5] but is applied to hidden_states[6] (PROBE_LAYER+1), then written as block-5 output. (ii) The residual is overwritten by the SAE reconstruction with the feature zeroed, so the measured logit change contains the full reconstruction error; spec 03 pitfall #5 warns against this, and there is no reconstruction-only control. (iii) 'Target' positions are where the INPUT token is a target gene, but in a causal LM the logits at that position predict the next token. The 'median specificity 1.01x, a genuine non-replication: features are not causally specific' is an artifact.
findings.evidence: phase6/summary.json: mean_target_delta 1.414 vs mean_other_delta 1.395. causal_patching.csv shows the same ~1.39 mean |Δlogit| for every feature (F3594 1.3943 vs 1.3941; F3554 1.3976 vs 1.3939). This is a feature-independent perturbation size. The pipeline spec explicitly warns against overwriting with the reconstruction.
findings.recommended_action: Encode and patch the same hidden_states index. Add delta = recon(z_ablated) - recon(z) to the clean residual. Measure the change in the logits of target-gene tokens, and include an error-only baseline.

findings.location: runs/sae-atlas-217M/scripts/remaining_phases.py:385-470 (ctrl from layer_05 file at 390; perturbed hidden[PROBE_LAYER+1] at 418); scripts/phase9_multitissue.py:52,78,239; summaries/sae-atlas-217M-FINAL_SUMMARY.md:5,94,113-120,160-172
findings.description: Control activations come from the Phase-0 layer_05 file (hidden_states[5]). Perturbed-cell and Tabula Sapiens activations are taken at hidden_states[6]. The 'multi-tissue L5 SAE' is trained on a 50/50 mixture of these two layers. Phase 8t uses positions as samples: the first 10,000 control positions (about 5 cells) against pooled positions from 20 perturbed cells, with uncorrected p<0.05 over 4,928 features. TF specificity is reported as 0/48 although only 3 TFs had any responding feature. The central headline '0% TF specificity, even more extreme than Geneformer's 6.2%' and 'multi-tissue does not rescue (+0.0pp)' are not interpretable.
findings.evidence: phase8_true/perturbation_response.csv: detected 4/100 (TFs CDC5L, GATA1, MED1; non-TF AQR), is_specific 0. phase9/summary.json: detection jumps to 95% with the mixed-layer SAE, while specificity stays 0/48.
findings.recommended_action: Extract control and perturbed activations at the same hidden-state index (re-extract controls with the same code). Compare cell-level or pseudobulk activations with FDR control, and report specificity among detected perturbations. Rerun Phase 9 with single-layer pooling.

findings.description: The 'proxy perturbation' compares SAE activations at positions whose token IS gene G against random other positions. That tests token identity, not perturbation response. With uncorrected p<0.05 and |effect|>0.1 across 4,928 features, at least one 'responding feature' is essentially guaranteed, giving 100% detection. The TFs are the alphabetically first 48 TRRUST TFs, and only the first 200k positions (about 98 cells) are used. The updated scorecard still lists 'Perturbation detection 100% ✅ replicates' after true CRISPRi gave 4%. The claim that the proxy 'establishes the upper bound for what the representations encode about regulatory logic' is unsupported.
findings.evidence: phase8/perturbation_summary.json: 60/60 detected and 24 TFs tested. phase8_true/summary.json: detection 0.04. Scorecard rows at summary lines 85 and 141.
findings.recommended_action: Remove the proxy from the replication scorecard and report the true-perturbation detection rate (after fixing F08).

findings.description: leidenalg was not installed, so the code fell back to SpectralClustering(n_clusters=min(10, n_alive)). Every layer therefore has exactly 10 modules by construction. The claims '10 modules ... matches [paper's 6-12] precisely' and '120 modules / 10 per layer' are artifacts. In addition, the fallback clusters pmi_pos[:n_alive, :n_alive] (the first n_alive feature indices, not the alive features) and assigns the labels to alive_idx. At L0, where 2,430 features are dead, module labels go to the wrong features and coverage numbers are meaningless.
findings.evidence: Log line 78: 'leidenalg not installed — skipping Leiden'. Modules = 10 for every one of the 12 layers. Code lines 373-381.
findings.recommended_action: Install Leiden (or another method that chooses the number of clusters from the data), restrict to alive features with correct indexing, and re-report modules and coverage.

findings.description: BH-FDR is applied only to feature x term tests that already had p<0.1 and overlap >=2. The BH denominator therefore excludes most of the tests performed, which makes the significance threshold far too lenient and inflates annotation rates. There is no shuffled-gene-set null. The claim 'MaxToki's rates are higher than Geneformer's (52.4%), suggesting MaxToki's features are more biologically interpretable' and the depth-trend comparisons with the paper are unsupported. Denominators are also inconsistent: L5 annotation uses 4,928 alive versus 4,903 in Phase 1, and L11 uses 4,924 versus 4,813.
findings.evidence: Code: 'if p < 0.1: annotations.append(...)', then multipletests(ann_df['p_raw']). The 12-layer pipeline repeats this. Annotation rates are 80.7/67.8/61.7% (and a different 'U-shaped' profile in the 12-layer summary).
findings.recommended_action: Apply BH across all tested (feature, term) pairs, add a random top-20 gene-set null, and recompute rates before any cross-model comparison.

findings.description: Dead features (2,430 at L0, whose decoder vectors are effectively random normalised directions) are counted as 'novel/invisible to SVD' (L0: 4,928/4,928 novel). They are also included in the cross-layer-persistence denominators. The two summaries interpret the same metric in opposite ways. The 3-layer summary says 'Features are overwhelmingly layer-specific — no persistent scaffold. Replicates'. The 12-layer summary says 'MaxToki has dramatically higher cross-layer persistence than Geneformer ... features persist across depth'. The annotation profile is called 'declining with depth, consistent with paper' in one and 'U-shaped, matching the paper' in the other.
findings.evidence: Code: alive = (np.load(...).shape[0] > 0) is a scalar True. n_src_alive = count of decoder norms > 1e-8 = 4,928. Logs: L0->L5 125/4928; the 12-layer log gives L6->L7 1059/4928 (21.5%).
findings.recommended_action: Exclude dead features from the novelty and persistence statistics, add a random-decoder null, and reconcile the two summaries.

findings.description: A 'highway' is a source feature whose maximum PMI across 4,928 target features exceeds 3, measured on co-activation at the same token position in two layers. There is no null and no minimum co-occurrence count. For low-frequency features, the maximum of thousands of noisy PMI values easily exceeds 3, and same-token identity drives co-activation across layers. The 99.6-100% rate is therefore close to guaranteed. 'Replicates exactly' and 'features form dense computational cascades across depth' are unsupported.
findings.evidence: n_highways = (max_pmi_per_src > 3).sum(). Rates: 2498/2498 (L0->L5), 4915/4927, and 99.6-100% for all 11 adjacent pairs.
findings.recommended_action: Compare against a position-shuffled or frequency-matched null and require minimum co-occurrence counts.

findings.description: Fisher tests treat roughly 1-2M token positions from 1,000 cells as independent observations, although cell type is a cell-level label. Bonferroni correction covers only the 32 cell types, not the 4,928 features. Activations are taken at hidden_states[6] but encoded with the hidden_states[5] SAE. The 95.9% enrichment rate and its comparison with the paper's 99.0% are inflated and uninterpretable.
findings.evidence: Code: p < 0.05/len(unique_cts) applied per feature. Positions are pooled with per-position cell-type labels; h_l5 = hidden[PROBE_LAYER + 1].
findings.recommended_action: Aggregate per cell (e.g., activation frequency per cell), test at cell level with FDR across features x cell types, and use the matching layer.

findings.description: The curveball (degree-preserving) null trades pairs of rows drawn uniformly from all 1,500 HVG rows, with only 5 x E trades (E = 66 TRRUST edges for K562). Only about 27 rows contain edges, and any trade involving an empty row is a no-op. The 'null' matrices are therefore essentially the observed TRRUST matrix, so the null mean equals the observed AUROC and z is about 0 by construction. The 'invariant finding' that the curveball z-score is 'at null in every run' (−0.14/+0.17/+0.16/−0.04), repeated in the SAE and attention cross-references as 'curveball z≈0', is an artifact.
findings.evidence: I re-ran the exact curveball_permute on the K562 HVG/TRRUST grid built from the project's gene_features.csv and reference_data trrust_human.tsv (66 edges, 27 non-empty rows). Effective trades = 0 and edges moved = 0 in 5/5 trials. Reported curveball null SDs are 0.0011/0.0015/0.0031/0.0007, versus label-shuffle SDs of 0.043/0.025/0.018/0.032. Null means equal the observed values to the third decimal (e.g., K562 0.4831 vs 0.4829).
findings.recommended_action: Run the curveball on the TF x target bipartite submatrix (non-empty rows only) with enough trades. Verify mixing (fraction of edges moved), then recompute z.

findings.description: C3's 'fraction of above-chance signal retained' divides by max(baseline − 0.5, 1e-6). For K562 (baseline 0.483) this gives −13,421, so the FAIL there is meaningless. Adamson 'passes' because the residual (0.5202) exceeds the baseline (0.5195). For the K562-1B run the verdict JSON records C3 pass=True (0.784 retained: 0.5554 -> 0.5434), but FINAL_SUMMARY reports C3 FAIL. Its claim 'Residualized AUROC collapses to chance after OLS cross-fit in every run' is false: only RPE1 shows a collapse (0.6045 -> 0.4922).
findings.evidence: residualization_results.csv: K562 fraction −13421.3; 1B 0.7839; Adamson 1.035. phase12_verdict_k562_1b.json: C3 'pass': true. FINAL_SUMMARY table row k562_1b shows C3 FAIL.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the table and the claim. Define C3 only when the baseline is significantly above 0.5 and report bootstrap CIs.

findings.description: The summary states that 'No run's attention beats any of the three trivial baselines (variance, mean expression, 1-dropout)'. In RPE1, attention significantly beats two of the three. C1 fails there only because of gene variance.
findings.evidence: RPE1 attention per-perturbation AUROC is 0.6033, versus mean expression 0.5822 (BH p = 7.3e-8) and 1−dropout 0.5002 (BH p = 4.1e-36). The verdict JSON lists attention_won=True and significant=True for both.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the statement and discuss the RPE1 result.

findings.description: All TRRUST-based conclusions rest on very few TFs: 8 TFs with 66 edges (K562), 16 (RPE1), 32 (Adamson) and 12 (1B). The label-shuffle null SD is 0.043 for K562. Phase 4 used 300 cells, and the code comment claiming these are 'the same cells as Phase 0' is wrong because the choice size differs. Baseline TRRUST AUROC at L8 moves from 0.483 (2,000 cells) to 0.440 (300 cells), a sampling shift larger than any ablation delta (−0.005 to +0.018). There is one run per condition and no CIs, and head (0,6) appears in all three random sets. 'Ablating top-5 TRRUST heads does nothing different from random — the same causal null' is not supported by a test with this little power.
findings.evidence: phase3 logs: 'TFs with >= 3 TRRUST targets in HVG: 8/16/32/12'. null_results.json label-shuffle SD 0.0429. phase4 run_config n_ctrl 300; ablation deltas −0.0051…+0.0180. Best-layer AUROC rises from 0.684 (L1) to 0.697 when the top-5 heads are masked.
findings.recommended_action: Bootstrap over cells and TFs, draw many random head sets, use the same cells as Phase 0, and add larger reference networks (STRING/ChIP) before claiming a causal null.

findings.description: The '217M -> 1B' comparison changes several variables at once. 1B used 200 control cells versus 2,000. It has a different HVG set (1,259/1,500 overlap) and only 40 shared cells. Its 'primary layer' is L8 of 20 layers (40% depth), whereas the 217M choice was justified by depth parity (L8 of 11, 73%). The 1B layer profile peaks at L4-L5 (0.580-0.581). 'Replicates across a 5x model-size increment' and 'scale helps marginally' are therefore not supported. Arithmetic and metadata errors: '~2.7x improvement' is actually (0.5398−0.5)/(0.5119−0.5) = 3.3x; the gene-variance baseline is called 'identical' although it is 0.5961 vs 0.5957 on different gene and perturbation sets (155 vs 174 perturbations); run_config labels the 1B run as 'MaxToki-217M-HF'.
findings.evidence: run_config n_ctrl 200, model_n_layers 20. gene_features overlap 1,259 genes, control-cell overlap 40/200. phase1_k562_1b per-layer AUROC: L4 0.580, L5 0.581, L8 0.540.
findings.recommended_action: Rerun 1B with matched cells, HVGs and a depth-matched layer (about L14), or report the full layer profiles side by side. Fix the metadata and numbers.

findings.description: MaxToki orders tokens by normalized expression and its attention is causal. attn[A->B] is therefore structurally zero whenever B ranks below A in a cell. Gene-space edges average over all co-occurring cells, including these structural zeros. The edge value thus largely encodes how often B outranks A, i.e. relative expression, which is a gene-level property. The finding that attention adds nothing beyond gene-level features (C1/C2/C3) and the 'co-expression, not regulation' interpretation are partly built in by this construction. The README only notes that the raw directed form is used.
findings.evidence: Code: attn_sum[li, :, A, B] += sub over all HVG pairs present; denominator = pair_counts (all co-occurrences). Tokenizer sorts by expr/median descending (setup/maxtoki_adapter.py:139-146).
findings.recommended_action: Average attention only over cells where B precedes A (or symmetrize). Add a rank-only baseline, P(B outranks A), and test whether attention adds information beyond it.

findings.description: The summary misreports the Phase 0b numbers. It also compares raw attention's per-perturbation AUROC peak (L1, 0.553) with the value-weighted TRRUST AUROC peak (L9-L10, ≈0.59) and calls the difference an 'architectural asymmetry'. It claims the shallow-layer peak is 'specific to bidirectional BERT-style encoders' without any comparison model.
findings.evidence: run_config: value-weighted L8 per-perturbation AUROC 0.4933 vs attention 0.5119 (the summary says 0.513 vs 0.532). Value-weighted per-perturbation AUROC is below 0.5 at L0-L8 (0.458-0.493) and peaks at 0.515 (L9).
findings.recommended_action: Correct the numbers, compare like with like, and remove the unsupported architectural claims.

findings.description: The K=10 KMeans produced 4 singleton clusters and 2 tiny ones. Per-cluster attention edges from one cell dominate the CSSI-max and CSSI-mean aggregations, and TRRUST evaluation uses 8 TFs. 'Two of three aggregations significantly worse' and 'CSSI fails to rescue' reflect a degenerate stratification, not a test of the method.
findings.evidence: cluster_sizes [814, 1, 261, 1, 1, 1, 3, 14, 310, 594]. CSSI-max TRRUST 0.445, oracle 0.502.
findings.recommended_action: Enforce a minimum cluster size (or choose K by silhouette) and use a stratifiable dataset before drawing conclusions.

findings.description:
Every result depends on an unvalidated re-implementation of MaxToki tokenization:
(1) Geneformer's gc104M gene-median dictionary is used instead of MaxToki's own, assumed 'within noise' without a check.
(2) Ranks are computed only over each dataset's restricted gene panel (Replogle concat has 6,546 genes, 6,332 in vocab; Adamson 4,888, only 3,769 in vocab), not transcriptome-wide as in pretraining.
(3) Sequences are truncated to 2,048 tokens although the context is 4,096. K562 cells have 3,223 non-zero genes on average and a mean sequence length of 2,039, so most cells are truncated.
(4) Nothing checks that X holds raw counts. GEARS-processed Adamson and Tabula Sapiens files may be log-normalized, which changes the ranking.
(5) There is no in-distribution check, such as next-token loss or perplexity compared with published values.
findings.evidence: phase0.log: 'total genes: 6,546', 'mean nz/cell: 3223', 'mean seq_len: 2039 max: 2048'. phase0_adamson.log: 'var in MaxToki vocab: 3769/4888'. The tokenizer divides X directly by medians with no count check.
findings.recommended_action: Obtain MaxToki's official tokenizer and medians, verify raw-count inputs, report model loss on the tokenized cells, and re-run key analyses with full gene panels and the 4,096 context (or show the results are insensitive).

findings.description: The software environment is not pinned, yet results depend on version-specific transformers internals. The hooks return a bare tensor from LlamaDecoderLayer, which would break on the 4.44 tuple API but works on newer versions. Newer versions record output_hidden_states before forward hooks, which produces the 'L6 = 0 edges' pattern in F02. Data paths are absolute paths outside the project. The longevity probe and permutation-null helpers are imported from an upstream repo that is not included. The large outputs (attention tensors, SAE weights, circuit edges, activations) are absent, so many numbers cannot be re-derived. Runs are on MPS without determinism settings.
findings.evidence: The crosslayer log shows the 'Loading weights ... 102' progress bar of newer transformers. The README pins only lower bounds. run_stage1.py imports _permutation_null_for_best from external code. _large_files_listing.tsv lists the missing artifacts.
findings.recommended_action: Ship a lockfile (exact torch/transformers versions), vendor all helper code, record data checksums and seeds, and add unit tests for hook semantics.

findings.description: The headline '561 -> 94 effective-rank collapse (6.0x)' includes L0, the static token embeddings, and L11. L11 is hidden_states[-1], which in HF Llama comes after the final RMSNorm with learned per-dimension weights; the largest single drop (172 -> 94) is this normalization, not a transformer block. Across blocks (L1 -> L10) the ratio is 1.93x. The 'learned, not architectural' conclusion rests only on an independent per-column shuffle, which destroys all correlations and gives near-full rank for any correlated data. That cannot separate learned compression from architecture; a randomly initialized MaxToki is needed. The same post-norm caveat applies to the SAE 'L11'.
findings.evidence: ER: L0 560.8, L1 332.6, L10 172.1, L11 93.6. Shuffle null ER 573.1 (null_feature_shuffle.json).
findings.recommended_action: Report pre-norm L1-L10 metrics separately and add a random-init model null (same tokenization and cells).

findings.description: The lineage 'TwoNN compression' is computed on 6 B-cell marker genes and 9 T-cell markers; Myeloid has 1, which gives NaN. A TwoNN intrinsic-dimension estimate from 6 points is meaningless; the values jump 101 -> 34 -> 34 -> 62 -> 35. There is no size-matched random gene-set control, although global TwoNN itself falls from 102 to 6.7, so any gene set will 'compress'. T cells do too (rho = −0.895). 'B-cell compression replicated' and the inference that 'MaxToki encodes time rather than lineage identity' are unsupported.
findings.evidence: lineage_twonn_by_layer.csv: n_markers B=6, T=9, Myeloid=1. Global TwoNN in per_layer_metrics.csv: 102.0 -> 6.7.
findings.recommended_action: Use larger marker panels, compare with size-matched random gene sets, normalize by the global depth trend, or drop the claim.

findings.description:
Several smaller problems:
- The depth-semantics claim says TF-vs-target 'jumps to 0.62 at L11 after being ~0.53 at L0', but L0 joint AUROC is 0.596 (perm p = 0.0099), comparable to L6 and L11.
- The permutation null mean is 0.54, not 0.5, so the mean of 0.572 cannot be compared with the paper's 0.744.
- SV3 PPI is reported as 3/12 significant layers in one table and 10/12 in another; BH<0.05 holds at L7, L9, L10 and L11 for at most one pair set each.
- 'Persistent homology' (9a) is only kNN connected components.
- The HVG set was revised after a first pass gave too few STRING pairs or markers.
findings.evidence: tf_vs_target_classifier.csv rows: L0 0.5959, L6 0.6096, L11 0.6197, null_mean ≈ 0.54. PPI BH values for SV3 from the CSV.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the text, compare against null means, and pre-specify gene selection.

findings.description: Anchors are cell-type centroids, and every ruler (H65 stage DAG, H95, H103, H38 categories) is a deterministic function of cell-type labels. Any representation that separates cell types will therefore pass the gates. Raw-expression PCA/HVG features or a random-init model were never passed through the same LET-head and gate pipeline. The project's own anchor-level benchmark shows PCA-10 of raw expression matches or beats the extracted MaxToki features. 'MaxToki internally encodes a hematopoietic developmental manifold', 'first affirmative deployable result' and 'multi-axis biological hub' therefore cannot be attributed to the model.
findings.evidence: Phase 12 LITE: branch balanced accuracy PCA-10 0.844, SVD-10 0.837, frozen MaxToki avg-pool 0.792, extracted_z10 0.756. 'No significant differences' versus PCA/SVD/avg-pool.
findings.recommended_action: Run the identical Phase 5/7/8 gates with PCA/HVG features and a random-init MaxToki, and claim model-specific encoding only if MaxToki clearly exceeds them.

findings.category: wrong description of metric / selection bias
findings.description: The 'trustworthiness' gate is sklearn trustworthiness(features, z), computed in-sample. It measures how well the 10-D latent preserves the INPUT-FEATURE neighbourhoods, not agreement with the biological ruler. 'Trust ceiling is biology-bounded' and 'an intrinsic limit on how faithful the residual stream is to the antigen-receptor axis' are misinterpretations. The compaction chain compares trust relative to different input spaces (2,464-d vs 154-d). Its top-1 head (L10H6) was selected out of 88 on the same internal panel and then re-evaluated there. 'Compact-top1 beats full-drift on every metric' is therefore in-sample winner's curse.
findings.evidence: phase5_let_anchor.py:236: trust = trustworthiness(features, z_final, n_neighbors=15). Phase 10 loads centroids_internal.npy for all variants. Phase 9 ranks heads on internal-panel metrics.
findings.recommended_action: Define a ruler-based neighbourhood-preservation metric, evaluate compaction variants on held-out panels, and correct for selection among the 88 heads.

findings.description: The 'per-head operators' are slices of o_proj (W_O). The single-head feature is x_l @ W_O[:, h-block], a fixed linear projection of the residual-stream centroid onto the output-projection columns of head h. No attention pattern, Q/K or V of the head is involved. 'Head/layer attribution', 'H65 information is concentrated in late-layer heads (L10H6)' and the contrast with scGPT's L2H5 do not describe what heads compute.
findings.evidence: phase9 line 76: features = (x_l @ A.T) with A = W[:, h*154:(h+1)*154].T.
findings.recommended_action: Attribute with actual head outputs (attention·V·W_O at each position) or head ablations, or relabel the analysis as 'W_O-subspace projections'.

findings.description:
Four problems.
(1) 18 additional rulers (H92-H112) were screened with no multiple-testing control.
(2) A post-hoc '3-gate fallback' drops the category/branch holdout, which is the only gate that separated H65 from its null (the null passed random 0.799 and donor 0.707). H95 and H103 are declared 'positive' under it.
(3) The lung_nonhema 'negative control' assigns random H65 labels, so failure is guaranteed. It cannot show that 'the manifold captures hematopoietic biology, not generic tissue covariance'.
(4) In Phase 17, a head trained on scrambled H95 labels reaches in-sample self-fit 0.8248, identical to the real H95 head, so in-sample fit is not evidence of encoding. The cross-head deficit (−0.173) is expected from attenuation given the H95 self-fit of 0.825. 'Partially orthogonal subspaces' is unsupported.
findings.evidence: phase17 report: self_fit_h95 0.82478761, null_self_fit 0.82478761, head_overlap 0.642, target overlap 0.814. H65 null: random 0.799, donor 0.707, branch −0.001.
findings.recommended_action: Pre-register gates, apply FDR across rulers, keep a discriminating holdout gate, use label-preserving biological negative controls, and assess orthogonality on held-out anchors with attenuation correction.

findings.description: Age is a donor-level label with only 17 donors. The quantile bins split donors aged 56 and 59-60 into different classes. Both MaxToki L5 (0.2755) and HVG-PCA (0.1722) balanced accuracies are below the 3-class chance level of 0.333, consistent with donor-identity overfitting. 'MaxToki beats HVG-PCA by 10.3 pp, i.e. it is encoding something beyond raw expression PCA' is unsupported: no test, and both are worse than chance. The stated reason the null is higher is wrong, since majority-class prediction has balanced accuracy exactly 1/3. The permutation scheme (cell- vs donor-level) is in code not included in the snapshot. The text says '22–74y', but the sampled donors are 33-69. 'L5 is the canonical tap used by attention-grn' is wrong; attention-GRN used L8. The G1 FAIL verdict itself stands.
findings.evidence: sampled_obs.csv: 17 donors, bin '(56.0, 60.0]' contains donors aged 59-60, and three 56-year-olds are in the low bin. Permutation null mean 0.332 ≈ chance.
findings.recommended_action: Use donor-level permutation, report chance level, and probe age as a continuous donor-level regression. Remove the 'beyond PCA' claim.

findings.description: The 'STRONG POSITIVE (novel): MaxToki encodes a tissue-invariant gene geometry' claim averages over layers that include L0. L0 is the static token embedding and is identical across tissues by construction (Pearson = 1.0000). The null shuffles gene identity, which any token-identity-dominated representation beats trivially. Correlations actually decline with depth (lung–immune 1.00 -> 0.78), i.e. context moves geometry away from invariance. For the cross-model results: Geneformer V2 is a masked BERT model, not 'autoregressive'. MaxToki and Geneformer share the Theodoris-lab Ensembl vocabulary and possibly initialization, so 'independent pre-training' is unverified. A single scGPT comparison with symbol mapping does not 'weaken the source paper's claim'.
findings.evidence: cross_domain_alignment.csv: L0 Pearson 0.99999999998 (lung–immune) and 0.99999999999 (lung–ext-lung); best_layer = 0 for all pairs; L11 0.777.
findings.recommended_action: Exclude L0, compare with a context-matched null (e.g., same-tissue different cell types), check initialization provenance, and correct the architecture description.

findings.evidence: See the quoted lines. Exp-1 edge counts 4,960-4,978 (5th-95th percentile). phase6 n_features 50.
findings.recommended_action: Revise all cross-references once the bugs are fixed and the analyses rerun.

findings.description: Line 5 says the circuit is '22x denser'; 2,144,011/52,116 = 41.1x, which is the figure stated elsewhere. Biological coherence (36.1%, the fraction of annotated edges sharing any term) and TRRUST match (0.01%) are reported without a random feature-pair or random gene-pair baseline. Cross-model comparisons of these percentages are therefore uninterpretable.
findings.evidence: circuit_summary.json total_edges 2,144,011. Coherence code shows no null.
findings.recommended_action: Fix the ratio and add permutation baselines (random source/target pairs matched for annotation count).

findings.description: 'H-hub' (TF degree vs kNN eigenvector centrality) gives z = 2.34 and 2.36 in 2 of 3 domains (lung n.s.). This is among at least 10 exploratory hypotheses with no multiple-testing correction, and TF degree is not controlled for expression or token frequency. It is nonetheless called 'the strongest new result'. 'H-depth' is labelled 'non-trivial' although it is not significant against its null.
findings.evidence: Reported z-values and the absence of correction across the six to ten exploratory tests in the table.
findings.recommended_action: Apply FDR across the exploratory tests, control for expression and frequency, and soften the claims.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in experiment3_rerun.py:125-131 and experiments_2_3.py:280-287. 'Pseudotime' is PC1 of log1p expression over 200 randomly drawn cells from tabula_sapiens_immune.h5ad, rescaled to [0,1], with early/late taken as quartiles. Over mixed immune lineages this axis mostly tracks composition. Even so, the summary reads the steering results as moving toward or away from 'maturity'. It calls SOD3/KITLG 'progenitor/stemness factors' and FTL a 'terminal erythroid' marker, although FTL is a ubiquitous ferritin. The summary only notes the PC1 proxy as a spec deviation. Two sub-points are wrong. First, the logit signatures are not near-collinear: state_signatures.npz and the log give cos(g_early_logits, g_late_logits) = 0.881, so the summary's '≈0.999' is itself a misreport. Second, the multiplicity point does not matter: |rho| > 0.3 at n = 200 implies p ≈ 1.6e-5, and BH would keep essentially all 5,767 features. The core problem, an invalid pseudotime proxy plus biological interpretation, stands.

Confirmed. phases2_to_8.log:78 says 'leidenalg not installed'. Both phases2_to_8.py:370-381 and full_12layer_pipeline.py:299-310 fall back to SpectralClustering(n_clusters=min(10, n_alive)). full_12layer.log reports modules = 10 for all 12 layers, so '10 modules ... matches precisely' and '120 modules' are artifacts. Coverage is also 100% of alive features by construction, because spectral clustering labels every alive feature. The indexing bug in phases2_to_8.py (it clusters pmi_pos[:n_alive, :n_alive] and maps the labels onto alive_idx) is real at L0. The 12-layer script fixes it with np.ix_(alive_mask, alive_mask), and the stored L0 labels sit on exactly the 2,498 alive features. The coverage count, however, is unaffected by the mis-indexing.

Confirmed in code: only tests with p < 0.1 and overlap >= 2 enter the BH correction. In significant_enrichments.csv the largest 'significant' raw p is 0.042 at L0, 0.040 at L5 and 0.039 at L11. That implies about 27k to 34k prefiltered tests, of which about 85% pass, so the correction is effectively absent. When I recomputed with the spec's per-feature BH across the 2,369 terms, annotated features fall to about 4.2% (L0), 1.7% (L5) and 1.1% (L11), against the reported 80.7/67.8/61.7%. With global BH over all feature×term tests the rates are about 1%, 0.1% and 0%. The annotation rates, the 'more interpretable than Geneformer' claim and the depth-trend claims are therefore unsupported. The 4,928 vs 4,903 alive-count mismatch is trivial: Phase 1 counts on the eval split, Phase 2 on all positions.

Code confirmed. In phases2_to_8.py:242 'alive' is a scalar True and is never used. At line 292 n_src_alive counts nonzero-norm decoder columns, which gives 4,928 even though only 2,498 L0 features are alive. The novelty percentages are unchanged, because 0 L0 features are SVD-aligned and so 100% of the alive ones are novel either way. The persistence denominators for L0 sources are inflated, though. Dead decoders are random unit vectors, which almost never reach cos > 0.7, so L0→L5 is really 125/2498 = 5.0%, not 2.5%. That breaks the 'matches paper's 2.5%' claim. The two summaries also contradict each other. The 3-layer summary says 'layer-specific, no persistent scaffold, Replicates' (and compares non-adjacent L0→L5 with the paper's adjacent L0→L1). The 12-layer summary says 'dramatically higher persistence' (L6→L7 at 21.5%, L0→L8 at 13.3%). Annotation is described as 'declining' in one and 'U-shaped' in the other, each said to match the paper.

Confirmed in remaining_phases.py: n_highways = (max_pmi_per_src > 3).sum(), with no null and no minimum co-occurrence. For rare features a single co-occurrence already gives PMI > 3, and same-position residual continuity inflates cross-layer PMI. The metric and threshold do follow the spec (01-sae-atlas.md Phase 7), so 'Replicates' is accurate as a statement about the spec metric. The problem is the uncontrolled interpretation ('dense computational cascades'). It is not strictly 'guaranteed' for mid-frequency features, and the spec notes that scGPT drops to 62.9% on the same metric. This is an inherited methodological weakness plus an over-reading.
